E1

Method and interpretation

Read disposition separately from proof.

ELI · How to read the labels

The current ledger records 691 fixed findings among 859 classified records. This assessment has narrower evidence: 22 current rechecks and 71 earlier judgments carried forward, leaving 766 unverifiable. Current rechecks take priority over the dated dossiers below. A green test run or a fixed label is not proof that every original problem is gone.

This appendix is justified by the size of the finding matrix. The main report contains the argument, consequential defects and recommendations. These entries supply the complete source-to-disposition inventory without making the main reading depend on hundreds of expanded records.

Coverage: current reconciliation independently matches all 859 original IDs to exactly one ledger entry: 691 fixed, 32 duplicates, 25 not reproduced, 111 wontfix, zero blocked or missing. Fourteen ledger entries changed since the earlier inventory. All cited commits exist, but B1-21’s 3d5caf5 is still not an ancestor of 057370d. The 22 current rechecks cover all earlier unresolved/partial findings, five previously unverifiable decisions and B1-21’s provenance. Seventy-one earlier judgments are carried with their original limits, not newly certified. The remaining 766 stay unverifiable.

ClassMeaning at this revisionCount
ResolvedSource inspection supports repair of the original mechanism and relevant regression evidence was inspected. Limits are stated per entry. This is not a product-readiness certificate.84
Partially resolvedA meaningful part was repaired, but the original consequence or contract remains open under stated conditions.4
UnresolvedThe mechanism remains, a direct probe confirms it, or an explicit owner-blocked decision is still outstanding.2
RegressedAn independently established original finding became worse after an apparent repair. None was assigned here. This does not assert no regression exists.0
SupersededAn identified owner decision changed the applicable interpretation. O2, O5 and D5’s named-refusal checklist policy are cited explicitly.3
UnverifiableThe evidence reviewed here does not justify a current mechanism-level conclusion. Ledger status is retained as a claim.766

A quoted failure scenario below is a historical review description, not a newly observed incident. Credential-shaped examples, if present in source text, are replaced using the repository’s shared redaction policy before HTML generation. New cross-cutting findings are NEW-F01–NEW-F05 in the main report. H/M/O labels are clusters and decisions, not extra B-series findings.

The destructive-path failure names cleanup calls in execution/continuity-store.ts:478,481,490,500 and registry/plan-admission.ts:272,277, plus the forbidden-flag checks in publish/argv.ts:13,18. The last two are defensive rejection code caught by a broad text scan, not evidence of an actual force-push path. The cleanup sites need the recorded authority resolution. Repeated occurrences of the same test are reported separately from distinct failure identities.

The full run recorded 5,401/5,452 passing tests and 51 failing occurrences, representing 50 distinct test identities because the destructive-path test runs twice. Failure count is not a count of distinct product defects. The simulation correction-verifier assertion expects an older message, and the seed-creation assertion expects an earlier refusal than the journal-ahead guard now provides. Several landing journeys lack the newly required gate rows. Other failures include reconnect-descriptor disagreement, owner-amendment digest rejection, protected-grant blocked outcomes and interrupted-start state mismatches. These need fixture-versus-implementation triage. No passing unit total erases a failing integration layer.

The old source below intentionally asserts the old failures. It will not pass unchanged on the repaired revision and is not the current probe script. The guard result alone is no longer evidence of a missing owner correction path.

ELI · Four small experiments

These experiments recreated four narrow problems: a changed tool escaped a weaker check, a model-routing choice was rejected, an interrupted image file could not recover, and a budget rule refused the tested stop condition. The experiments used temporary test data. A successful experiment means the reported problem was reproduced. It does not mean the problem was fixed or that it happened during a real customer task.

The command below imports current source directly, creates synthetic files under a temporary directory and makes no provider, publication or owner-only call. Selecting the fallback in a constructed test object does not change any real sandbox configuration. The fixtures are never executed as commands.

  • E-P1 · B10-02: a same-inode, same-size, restored-mtime seed rewrite passes tool-policy enforcement. This does not bypass the bwrap read-only mount.
  • E-P2 · B6-06: plan-author appears in routable phases while its override is rejected.
  • E-P3 · B6-09: delivery to an existing truncated frame refuses re-entry and leaves the short file unchanged.
  • E-P4 · B3-22: L13 refuses the exhausted automatic/re-entry case when the owner tranche remains. The probe does not establish the frequency or reachability of a stuck real attempt.

B1-01resolvedrecorded: fixedThe closure commit's author and committer come from the checkout's live `git config user.name` and `user.email` at commit time, which AGENTS.md invariant 11 forbids; every other host commit in this area pins the owner's identity instead.

Independent assessment

Host-created commits use the pinned owner identity in all four author/committer variables. Closure no longer obtains identity from local Git configuration.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/git/commit.ts:27-45; core/src/cli/commands/close.ts:203
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The historical trailer breach is retained by the exact owner-approved exemption, not erased. Future generic multi-user ownership would need a new explicit policy.

Original problem and consequence

AGENTS.md invariant 11 says: 'Not `git config user.name`/`user.email` at commit time ... Every commit's author and committer identity is the owner's own (`Santiago Marin <santiagomarinsuarez@me.com>`), full stop'. close.ts:204-205 read both values, and line 207 refuses only when they are missing, empty, or contain a newline, carriage return, < or >. Any other identity is accepted. closure.ts:100-101 pins that identity into GIT_AUTHOR_* and GIT_COMMITTER_* for the closure commit, and closure.ts:102 documents it as 'Identity comes from Git config'. If a session's checkout config names an agent, `awsf close` writes that identity into the closure commit and nothing refuses it. The only commit-history fence (core/test/unit/meta/no-agent-coauthor.test.ts) runs after the commit exists, and its AGENT_IDENTITY_PATTERNS match only agent-shaped strings (claude, gpt, codex, copilot, gemini, chatgpt, anthropic.com, openai.com), so it would not flag a non-agent, non-owner identity either. No meta-test scans source for user.name or user.email reads. commit.ts:16-17, protected-commit.ts:74 and integration.ts:43-46 all pin the owner identity instead.

Historical classification: bug · high · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/cli/commands/close.ts:204 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B1-01. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

fixed: closure no longer reads git config; prepareClosureCommit pins HOST_AUTHOR in all four GIT_* (H9)

B1-02resolvedrecorded: fixedA silence timeout fires transport.cancel() with no rejection handler. cancel() is terminateTree(), which throws EnumerationUnavailable or SignalUnavailable when the census or the signal cannot be delivered, and no unhandledRejection handler exists in core/src, so the host process exits.

Independent assessment

Cancellation rejections and phase-write failures are captured for the durable stop path. The inspected follow-up retains late cancellation evidence.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/cli/commands/production-run.ts; follow-up 1a5ccea
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The earlier closeout reported a timing-sensitive cancellation failure. The fresh full-suite result, not its isolated historical pass, determines present gate health.

Original problem and consequence

A provider goes silent past silence_timeout_seconds while the census cannot run: a macOS ps census can time out after 5 s under load, and on Linux an unreadable /proc throws the same way. cancel() rejects, the bare void discards the promise, and the unhandled rejection ends the whole production run instead of recording a failed cancellation. The identical call at line 2804 is wrapped in .catch(() => undefined), so the omission is inconsistent. The rejection originates in transport-broker.ts lines 766-768, where cancel forwards terminateTree, and the errors are raised at darwin.ts line 110 and posix.ts line 88.

B1-04resolvedrecorded: fixedThe prompt is written with child.stdin?.end(spec.stdin) and no 'error' listener is attached to child.stdin, so an EPIPE on a write still pending when the provider exits is an unhandled 'error' that terminates the host.

Independent assessment

Provider stdin has an error listener. EPIPE follows the provider exit path instead of crashing the host.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/execution/transport-broker.ts:942-981
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The paired startup and large-prompt fixtures exercise the reported mechanism. Live provider startup failures were not induced.

Original problem and consequence

A provider exits before it drains stdin (bad argv, missing credentials, a startup crash) while a prompt larger than the stdio socket buffer is still being written. The pending write fails with EPIPE, Node emits 'error' on the stdin Socket, nothing handles it, and the host process crashes mid-run, so the caller never sees the provider's exit. Probe sizes: 64 KiB and 128 KiB were absorbed, 256 KiB and 512 KiB crashed, and a 1 KiB prompt is absorbed, so only large prompts reach this path.

B1-05resolvedrecorded: fixedThe released provider's stdin socket has no 'error' listener, so a write that fails with EPIPE (the provider exited before draining the prompt) is emitted as an unhandled 'error' event that kills the host process.

Independent assessment

Provider stdin has an error listener. EPIPE follows the provider exit path instead of crashing the host.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests

core/src/execution/transport-broker.ts:942-981
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The paired startup and large-prompt fixtures exercise the reported mechanism. Live provider startup failures were not induced.

Original problem and consequence

A provider CLI fails at startup (bad flag, auth error) and exits while a prompt larger than the stdio socket buffer is still being written after release. #transportFor's stdin.end() then gets EPIPE, Node throws the 'error' as uncaught, and the host exits with code 1 right after startProcess resolved. The barrier never sees the failure, so no RegistrationFailed, billing decision or terminal evidence is journaled for that call. Measured with the real broker: a 64 KiB prompt gives provider exit code 0; 256 KiB, 512 KiB and 4 MiB prompts give 'Error: write EPIPE' and host exit code 1.

B1-08resolvedrecorded: fixedresolvedHost() applies WHATWG URL parsing first, which disagrees with git's transport parsing in two ways: an scp-style host:path remote without a user yields null, and a backslash-authority URL yields the allowlisted host while git connects to a different host.

Independent assessment

Ambiguous URL spellings are refused, scp-style hosts are parsed, and every push URL contributes to the allowlist decision.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/git/publish.ts:102-166
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Only the original host-check defect is closed. Optional host restrictions are an accepted policy choice, and multi-destination publication is not atomic.

Original problem and consequence

publish.ts:73 `new URL(remoteUrl)` succeeds on `github.com:owner/repo.git` (scheme github.com, empty hostname), so line 75 returns null. Probe: `github.com:owner/repo.git` -> null, while `git@github.com:owner/repo.git` -> github.com. With policy.host = github.com, row 9 (remote-host-mismatch) refuses a valid remote, a fail-closed false refusal. The reverse case: `https://github.com\@evil.example/owner/repo.git` parses to hostname github.com (probe), so row 9 passes, but git ls-remote on the same string fails with 'Could not resolve host: evil.example', so git's transport goes to evil.example. The host check therefore does not constrain the destination for that spelling. Precondition: the owner's remote URL carries that spelling, and no URL is validated anywhere on the publish path. I ran ls-remote only; push uses the same transport helper.

B1-10resolvedrecorded: fixedThe TERM grace period is measured with the wall clock (Date.now()) and polled with `while (Date.now() < deadline)`, so a backward clock step stretches the wait until the clock catches up, and SIGKILL is not sent while a survivor ignores SIGTERM.

Independent assessment

Termination grace uses a monotonic clock and attempts SIGKILL when TERM/grace enumeration throws.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/execution/process-controller.ts:372-389
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The underlying operating system can still refuse signaling. Such failure must remain visible rather than be labeled a clean kill.

Original problem and consequence

awsf cancel (cli/commands/cancel.ts:59) or a transport cancel (transport-broker.ts:768) runs terminateTree against a provider that ignores SIGTERM, and the wall clock steps back one hour during the 2 s grace (NTP correction, VM resume, manual clock set). The loop keeps polling for about an hour and the KILL is not sent within that time. Measured with a fake port: the control without a step sent SIGKILL at poll 81; with a 1 h backward step at poll 3 the loop reached the 3000-poll probe cap with SIGKILL never sent. A forward step has the opposite defect: it cuts the grace period to zero.

fixed: grace timed with performance.now(); a SIGTERM or mid-grace census throw now sends SIGKILL before the original throw propagates

B1-11resolvedrecorded: fixedThe ChildProcess returned by spawn() has no 'error' listener; spawn failures (a missing cwd, EAGAIN/EMFILE) arrive as an asynchronous 'error' event, which Node throws as an uncaught exception instead of letting the barrier's start step reject.

Original problem and consequence

The attempt's worktree (spec.cwd, line 614) no longer exists when a phase launches, for example after it was removed or pruned following preflight. spawn() emits ENOENT asynchronously, nothing listens, and the host process exits with code 1 before the handshake starts. The reservation is never refunded or recorded as a RegistrationFailed, so crash recovery has to reconstruct it. Measured with the real broker and cwd '/nonexistent-probe-cwd-b1d': 'Error: spawn .../node ENOENT' was emitted on the ChildProcess and the host exited 1 without startProcess settling. The message names the executable rather than the missing directory, so the failure is also misdiagnosed.

B1-15resolvedrecorded: dup-of B1-10terminateTree lets an exception from the TERM signal or from a grace-loop census escape before the KILL step, so a group that ignores SIGTERM is never killed and the caller receives only a rejection.

Independent assessment

Termination grace uses a monotonic clock and attempts SIGKILL when TERM/grace enumeration throws.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/execution/process-controller.ts:372-389
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The underlying operating system can still refuse signaling. Such failure must remain visible rather than be labeled a clean kill.

Original problem and consequence

SIGTERM is sent at line 352, and the grace loop at lines 354-358 calls this.port.census() with no guard; the only KILL is at line 362. If the census throws on any poll, or SIGTERM itself throws, the function rejects with no KILL sent while the group may still be running. The caller then sees a rejection, not a survivor report, and review.ts:637-640 turns that into survivorReport = null and continues. The win32 port hits the TERM case in practice: it sends SIGTERM as taskkill /PID ... /T without /F (execution/platform/win32.ts:145), which exits non-zero for a windowless console process, and win32.ts:155-158 maps that to SignalUnavailable, so the ladder never reaches KILL there. Measured in probe P7 with a fake port: a census throw on the third call gave 'rejected: EnumerationUnavailable, signals sent: [SIGTERM]'; a TERM throw gave 'rejected: SignalUnavailable, signals sent: [SIGTERM]'; the control gave [SIGTERM, SIGKILL]. This is separate from verified #1 and #19, which concern how the rejection is handled in the silence path. The win32 exit behaviour follows taskkill's documented refusal and cannot be run on this host. Severity: medium-low (rare on Linux; plausible on darwin's ps census and on win32).

Original problem and consequence

publish.ts:111 resolves the host from `remote get-url --push`, and argv.ts:15 pushes to the remote name, which git sends to the push URL. publish.ts:125 reads the tip with `ls-remote remoteName refs/heads/<branch>`, which uses the fetch URL. Probe: origin url = ../fetch.git (main = X), pushurl = ../push.git (main = Y, unrelated to X), local HEAD Z descends from X. ls-remote printed X, and `merge-base --is-ancestor X Z` exited 0, so fastForward = true and row 14 (non-fast-forward) passes. The real `git push --porcelain origin Z:refs/heads/main` was rejected with `[rejected] (non-fast-forward)` and exit 1, which runPublish reports as PublishBlocked git-failure (publish.ts:209). The mirror case (fetch tip unrelated, push tip an ancestor) would refuse a publish the push accepts; I derived this from the same mechanism and did not run it. The non-forced push keeps the remote safe, so the damage is a wrong verdict shown to the owner and a misreported failure. The fix is to read the tip from the same URL the push uses.

B1-23resolvedrecorded: fixedThe silence-timeout callback voids the transport cancel promise and drops its TerminationReport, so a rejected cancel becomes an unhandled rejection that exits the awsf process, and a process group that survives cancellation is journalled as FAILED anyway.

Independent assessment

Cancellation rejections and phase-write failures are captured for the durable stop path. The inspected follow-up retains late cancellation evidence.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/cli/commands/production-run.ts; follow-up 1a5ccea
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The earlier closeout reported a timing-sensitive cancellation failure. The fresh full-suite result, not its isolated historical pass, determines present gate health.

Original problem and consequence

The silence timer fires after silence_timeout_seconds (2700 s by default). terminateTree (core/src/execution/process-controller.ts:286) rejects when its census throws EnumerationUnavailable (process-controller.ts:322 and :337) or its signal port throws SignalUnavailable on a failed kill(-pgid) (core/src/execution/platform/posix.ts:88). Because the returned promise is voided, nothing handles the rejection. core/src contains no unhandledRejection or uncaughtException listener, so Node 22 raises it as an uncaught exception and the awsf process exits before the turn is persisted; the persist and cleanup at production-run.ts:2804-2828 never run. If cancel resolves instead with survivors (TerminationReport.terminated false), the silence path never reads them. The completed-turn path at production-run.ts:2816 throws on survivors, but the silence path writes the process row as FAILED with endedAt at lines 2822-2828 while the group may still be alive. This is the fire-and-assume defect that core/src/execution/liveness-monitor.ts:1-20 warns against; LivenessMonitor, the module that reports termination for a silence trip, has no production caller and is referenced only under core/test/.

Original problem and consequence

protected-commit.ts:66 runs `rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index` through systemGitRunner (changes.ts:14-28, which copies the entire ambient environment). Probe: with GIT_INDEX_FILE=/elsewhere/other.index the command prints /elsewhere/other.index. Then beforeIndex is read from that path (line 67), the lock is `${indexPath}.lock` (line 109, O_EXCL at line 115), and line 143 `renameSync(lockPath, indexPath)` installs the staged index over that file while the worktree's real index is left stale. The final check at lines 175-177 compares against the same wrong path, so it passes. protected-reconcile.ts:117-120 documents this exact hazard, and lines 132-133 refuse a path that does not match the worktree Git directory, so the commit side and the recovery side disagree. B1-31unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe barrier sets at to 'spent' before the durable spend hook runs and before the release token is written, so a throw from onSpent, onCorrection or onReattached is reported as failing at 'spent', whose message says the release token may have reached the child although it was never written.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

In runLauncherBarrier, spent = true and at = 'spent' (lines 521-522) are set before await onSpent (line 524) and before await launch.release() (line 532). If onSpent rejects, abandon() kills the unreleased child, so no provider ran, yet RegistrationFailed reports 'the launch failed at spent ... and whether the release token reached the child is not knowable, so the call is billed' (line 419). The host knows the token was never attempted, so the diagnostic misstates the provider's state; the billing outcome itself is the intended conservative over-count. The same throw also stores the cancellation error in refundError (line 556, refund.error ?? cancelError), although that field is documented as set when the refund itself failed, and nothing in core/src reads it. Severity: low. Code-reasoned, not probed.

fixed: launcher barrier keeps at as spending during durable spend hook so failures do not claim release reached child.

B1-33unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe launch barrier refunds an unspent reservation even when tearing down the gated child threw or left survivors, contrary to the ordering rule its own comments state.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Lines 494-497 state the rule: every exit from the block 'destroys the tree first and settles the money second ... because a returned reservation next to a surviving process is a lie about what the system did.' In the catch block, launch.abandon (line 541) can throw, which is recorded as cancelError (lines 542-544), or can return a TerminationReport with terminated false and a survivors list (launcher-barrier.ts:226-246; transport-broker.ts:649 delegates to terminateTree, which returns survivors at process-controller.ts:366). Line 548 ignores both outcomes and calls releaseOnRegistrationFailure whenever spent is false, so the call returns to the ledger while the child's process group may still exist. If the failure came before register (line 513), the survivor is also absent from the journal, which is the unrecorded-process case the broker header (transport-broker.ts:3-8) says cannot be killed. No provider ran, because GO was never sent, so the impact is ledger and survivor accounting rather than a double spend. The journal and the ledger nonetheless both record a clean release over a live process.

B1-34unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe launcher execs the provider with process.execve after Node's runtime has set SIGPIPE and SIGXFSZ to SIG_IGN. execve keeps ignored dispositions, while libuv's spawn path resets them to SIG_DFL, so the provider starts with both signals ignored.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Every provider launched through the gated child starts with SIGPIPE and SIGXFSZ ignored, and so does any descendant that starts through a plain fork/exec without a reset, such as shell pipelines and tools that do not reset signals. A process writing to a closed pipe gets EPIPE instead of dying from SIGPIPE, and a write past RLIMIT_FSIZE gets EFBIG instead of SIGXFSZ, so a tool that does not check write errors keeps running after its reader has gone. Node-spawned descendants reset the dispositions, so the effect is not uniform. Node exposes no API in this runtime to restore SIG_DFL from JavaScript. A fix has to exec through a reset, for example /usr/bin/env --default-signal=PIPE,XFSZ (GNU coreutils; BSD and macOS env do not have that flag).

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/execution/launcher.ts:146 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B1-34. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: launcher resets signal dispositions for SIGPIPE and SIGXFSZ before process.execve.

Original problem and consequence

Latent: LivenessMonitor has no production caller yet (only tests import it). Once it is wired in, a host suspended for longer than the 2700 s window resumes with a clock jump: noteOutput followed by the first tick reports reason 'silence', and terminateTree kills a healthy provider. Measured with Date.now stubbed: noteOutput(4096) followed by a 3 h forward step gave reason 'silence' at once; a 1 h backward step followed by 45 min of real silence gave reason null, so the silence went undetected. The production silence watchdog is a separate setTimeout re-armed in cli/commands/production-run.ts:2714-2720 and does not use this class.

B1-36unverifiablerecorded: fixedtick() counts any change in the summed group CPU as activity, but groupCpu sums only the members alive at that instant, so a member exiting lowers the sum and resets the silence window with no work done.

Original problem and consequence

Latent until the monitor is wired (see the first candidate), but wiring it as-is reintroduces the hole. A provider whose helper child exits every few seconds lowers the group sum at each exit; each drop sets lastActivityAt, so the window never reaches its 2700 s limit and the run never trips. Probe: with a flat counter the monitor trips at 10 s; with one member exit every 5 s and no real work it reached 60 s with reason null. The rule should count only increases (or per-member CPU), not any difference.

Original problem and consequence

transport-broker.ts:155-157 refuses only an empty id, and assertSpawnSite (lines 124-137) checks only the edge pair. The agent-phase validator checks ledger.reservation(...) is held with cost 1 before any spawn (lines 516-518), but the plain task-edge path has no equivalent. rework.ts:973-976 launches L19 with reservationId: reservation.id through this path, so runLauncherBarrier runs start() (launcher-barrier.ts:478), which spawns the gated child; register() (line 513) durably records the process; and only then does spendOnGo (line 519) call CallBudget.settle, which throws ReservationNotHeld for a settled or unknown id (call-budget.ts:432-437). The barrier kills the child and the refund fails the same way. No GO was sent, so no money is spent. The journal, however, holds a registered process for a launch the ledger refused, and the broker's stated rule that refusals precede any child (transport-broker.ts:17-19) does not hold for this class.

Original problem and consequence

Inputs: a ProcessTransportBroker built with correctionLaunchVerifier installed and onCorrection omitted. The production wiring at core/src/cli/commands/production-run.ts:1923-1924 supplies both, so this is latent rather than reachable on the shipped path. startProcess receives a valid kind 'phase-correction' registration whose origin reservation is spent, so #assertPhaseCorrectionLaunch (transport-broker.ts:566-589) accepts it. Line 453 then passes no onCorrection to runLauncherBarrier, so at launcher-barrier.ts:525 the call 'await onCorrection?.(durableRecord)' is a no-op, the register() journal row is written, and launch.release() at launcher-barrier.ts:532 writes the GO token. The provider turn runs with no attempt.updated row recording the correction round, tranche and continuity handle, and the launch's releasedAt is never set. Nothing in the broker or the barrier refuses. The guard the commit title promises belongs in #assertPhaseCorrectionLaunch next to the verifier check at transport-broker.ts:566-567, or in runLauncherBarrier beside the reconnect check at launcher-barrier.ts:455-457. The reconnect class already has the first form (transport-broker.ts:471-473 throws when onReattached or the ledger methods are missing). The 132fb0b code it replaced was also optional ('await this.#options.onCorrection?.(...)'), so the absent-sink gap predates the commit; the commit moved the write before release without making the sink mandatory. Probe (scratchpad B1-B/probe-correction-sink.mjs, run against the unmodified barrier): settlement 'correction' with no onCorrection gives released=1 and no error; with a sink the sink runs while released=0; settlement 'reconnect' with no callbacks is refused with released=0.

B1-40unverifiablerecorded: fixedhostCommitContentDigest() turns every lstat failure into a 'removed' row, not only ENOENT, so an unreadable path is hashed as absent and the content check cannot tell it apart from a real deletion.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

commit-reconcile.ts:30-31 `try { info = await lstat(absolute); }` followed by `catch { rows.push({ path, removed: true }); continue; }`. EACCES, ELOOP and EIO are all recorded as removed. reconcileHostCommit compares this digest with intent.contentDigest at lines 73 and 102. If the path is unreadable when the intent is recorded and still unreadable at reconcile time, the digests match and the function returns 'committed' or 'not-committed' without verifying that path's working-tree bytes. The path-set check at lines 98-101 still applies, so the gap is limited to a path that stays unreadable across both moments; a readable-to-unreadable change produces a mismatch and is refused, which is the safe direction. Low likelihood, but it routes an error through the proof's own 'removed' vocabulary.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: hostCommitContentDigest catches only ENOENT as removed and rethrows non-ENOENT lstat errors.

B1-41unverifiablerecorded: fixedreconcileHostCommit compares the stored commit message with the raw recorded message, but git normalizes the message it stores when commit -m runs, so a host commit whose message has trailing spaces on a line or consecutive blank lines is refused as carrying a different message although AWSF wrote it.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence

Original problem and consequence

The intent records the raw message (cli/commands/production-run.ts:2467, message: commitMessageFor(envelope.payload!)), and commitAsHost passes that same string to git commit -m (git/commit.ts:18). Git's default whitespace cleanup strips trailing spaces and collapses consecutive blank lines, so the stored body differs from the recorded text and the comparison at line 90 fails. Recovery after a crash at the commit boundary then refuses the candidate and leaves the attempt for manual intervention. Measured in probe P8: a clean message reconciled to committed; the same message with trailing spaces on the subject line, and the same message with a double blank line, each returned refused with 'the created commit carries a different message than the recorded intent'. Fail-closed, but it blocks a legitimate recovery. Severity: medium-low.

fixed: reconcileHostCommit normalizes commit message whitespace before comparing with intent.

B1-43unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe executable-bit and owner-private checks read permission bits that DrvFS (/mnt/d) reports as 0777 for every file, so on a worktree under /mnt/d every granted regular file is classified as 100755 and protected commit and recovery refuse ordinary files.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

protected-commit.ts:85 derives the mode from `(stat.mode & 0o111) === 0 ? "100644" : "100755"`. In this checkout `stat -c %a` returns 777 for AGENTS.md, core/src/git/publish.ts and package.json, so the derived value is always 100755, and line 86 throws 'grant-bearing execution cannot change executable modes' for any granted file whose tree entry is 100644, which is the normal case. protected-reconcile.ts:165 repeats the same derivation, so inspectProtectedPublication refuses the recorded candidate and recovery cannot complete. protected-lock.ts:29 (assertOwnedRegular with owner-private) refuses any mode with bits in 0o077, so captureLockWitness (protected-lock.ts:234, reached from protected-commit.ts:131) and adoptRetainedIndexLock (protected-reconcile.ts:304) refuse on DrvFS as well. The lock-witness refusal fires after index.lock has been created (see the next candidate). Default worktrees live under ~/.local/state/awsf-worktrees on ext4 (platform-paths.ts:61-62), so this bites when worktree_root or AWSF_WORKTREE_ROOT points into /mnt/d. The owner's memory notes the same DrvFS 0777 trap for /mnt/d worktrees, and no code in this batch accounts for it.

Historical classification: bug · low · PLAUSIBLE. Original location: core/src/git/protected-commit.ts:85 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B1-43. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: isPermissionMaskedMount handles masked filesystem permission bits on DrvFS and 9p mounts.

B1-44unverifiablerecorded: fixedunfinishedProtectedEffect() returns null whenever any consumption is orphaned, even when an unbound intent exists, so an unfinished protected host effect is reported to its callers as nothing to reconcile.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Lines 72-79 compute `unbound` (intents with no binding), but line 78 `if (orphaned.length > 0) return null;` returns before line 79 `return unbound[0] ?? null;`. Probe against the real module: consumptions [c1 (no intent, no binding), c2], intents [the intent for c2], bindings [] returns null; the same intent without c1 returns the c2 intent. Callers read null as 'nothing retained'. production-run.ts:4103-4104 makes reconcileRetainedProtectedEffect return null, so the owner is never asked to reconcile and resume continues at production-run.ts:4195 into preflightRecovery. production-run.ts:1352 reports 'no exact host effect exists to reconcile' for the same state. A HEAD compare-and-swap and index.lock from the intent therefore stay unreconciled behind a message that says there is nothing to reconcile. The function's own comment (lines 66-70) calls a second unfinished effect corruption and the code throws for it, yet this branch drops the unbound intent silently. Reachability: needs an orphaned consumption and an unbound intent in one attempt. protected-grants.ts:118 allows one consumption per grant, so this needs at least two protected phases in one attempt. I did not construct that full sequence end to end.

It also says the force and auto-delete halves "now also cover the argv-array spellings the previous scan never saw". The authorization table tests only refspec facts (authorize.ts:138 `"force-refspec": ({ refspec }) => !refspec.forced,` and authorize.ts:140 for deleting), publish-fence.test.ts:152 checks only that the push token appears in argv.ts, and the FORBIDDEN list (no-destructive-paths.test.ts:23-33) has `--force\b` but no `--mirror`, `--delete`, or `--prune`. git push --mirror force-updates and deletes remote refs (git-push(1)), so a one-token edit at argv.ts:15 would reach the owner's remote while every test stays green. Latent: argv.ts has no such flag today, and the no-destructive-paths test passes (2 pass, 0 fail) on this tree.

B1-49unverifiablerecorded: not-reproduced per-commit ClosureSnapshot caching avoids repeated blob subprocess scansA fresh awsf close calls readClosureSnapshot eight times for three distinct commits, and each call spawns one git process per registered blob, so one close spawns about 3,800 git processes and takes on the order of 50 seconds on this host.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

close.ts:145 reads the base snapshot and close.ts:146 reads head. close.ts:232 calls verifyClosureCommit, which reads the parent (head) and the commit again at closure.ts:73-74. close.ts:239 calls finishClosureCheckout, which calls verifyClosureCommit again (closure.ts:122, reading head and commit at lines 73-74) and then reads head and commit once more at closure.ts:123-124. Each read spawns 478 git processes (show 1, ls-tree 1, and one cat-file per registered blob at closure.ts:54, which is 476 here) and took 6.2-6.8 s in probe-closure.mjs. Cheaper alternatives: (1) memoize snapshots by commit SHA for the duration of one close, since a commit's tree never changes, or pass verifyClosureCommit the before and after snapshots the caller already holds; this alone removes five of the eight reads, about 32 seconds here; (2) read all registered blobs through one 'git cat-file --batch' process fed the blob ids on stdin, which needs an input option on runSystemCommand (it wraps spawnSync, which accepts one), reducing each read to a single spawn.

B1-50unverifiablerecorded: not-reproduced unreadable, malformed, and unsupported mirrors now throw; only ENOENT is freshContinuityStore.load() maps every failure (missing, unreadable, corrupt JSON, wrong schema) to an empty store, and every later open() or recordTurn() rewrites the durable mirror from the in-memory map, so one failed read at run setup turns the next phase open into an overwrite that deletes the other phases' provider locators.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

A read at run setup (production-run.ts:1863 `await continuity.load();`) fails with EIO or a permission error, leaving the map empty and the run going on. The first open() for a later phase calls #flush() (continuity-store.ts:238-244), which atomically replaces private/continuity.json with that one record. The locators of earlier phases are then gone from disk, so a same-session correction for them fails closed with ContinuityUnavailable ('no conversation was opened under this handle') in this run and in every later start, while the provider conversations stay on disk unreachable. The same file's InterruptedTurnStore refuses every unreadable or unverifiable file with privateFailure() (continuity-store.ts:249-251, 346-363), so the file carries two error policies for the same kind of durable state. Simpler fix: a missing file is the only empty case, and every other load failure throws, so open() can never flush over a store it failed to read.

B1-51unverifiablerecorded: fixedWorktree cleanliness is re-derived at 24 literal `status --porcelain` call sites and in four helpers, and only closure.ts pins --untracked-files=all, so every other predicate inherits the host's status.showUntrackedFiles setting and calls a checkout with untracked files clean when that setting is no.

Original problem and consequence

With status.showUntrackedFiles=no in the owner's git configuration, assertClean (changes.ts:117-120) passes on a worktree that holds untracked files. assertClean is the before-precondition of permission sessions (sandbox-broker.ts:430) and of the production-run.ts and rework.ts checkpoints, and land.ts:58 is the dirty-canonical-tree preflight while publish.ts:100 feeds the dirty-checkout row. Two consequences follow. A canonical checkout with untracked files passes the land preflight and the post-land verify, so completeLanding fast-forwards a checkout that dirty-canonical-tree exists to refuse. A stray untracked file present before a provider turn is absorbed into the per-turn before-snapshot, because captureChangeSet uses ls-files --others, and commitAsHost (commit.ts:14) then stages it with add --all, so only the cumulative base-relative gate stands between that file and the candidate. The effect is latent and requires the setting, but it is a config-dependent hole in the clean-tree guarantee. Simpler fix: one isWorktreeClean(runner) in changes.ts that pins --untracked-files=all, used by every site.

B1-52unverifiablerecorded: wontfix InterruptedTurnStore has no production construction site, so this latent write/read cost is not paidInterruptedTurnStore.write re-reads, re-parses and re-hashes the whole prior checkpoint generation on every write after the first, and each generation carries the full cumulative output, so G generations cost O(G x S) bytes; no production caller constructs the store yet, so this is latent.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

Line 371 'const prior = await this.read(previous);' goes through privateBytes (up to 16 MiB), JSON.parse, assertTurnCheckpoint and sha256. Line 375 requires checkpoint.output.text to start with prior.output.text, which means every generation repeats all the output so far; canonicalJson (line 394) and writePrivateExclusive (line 403) then write that whole text again, so total bytes written grow quadratically with the number of checkpoints. Only core/test/unit/execution/interrupted-turn-store.test.ts constructs the store. Cheaper alternative: remember the last generation this instance wrote (its digest is already known) so the write path compares previous.digest in memory instead of re-reading the file, and store output deltas so each generation's size is proportional to new output. Fix before the store is wired to per-chunk writes.

B1-53unverifiablerecorded: wontfix a settlement-strategy extraction is broad and would move reconnect accounting into the platform-neutral barrierThe reconnect class is special-cased through all three layers instead of being a settlement strategy the barrier calls: the barrier branches on the settlement name and validates three optional hooks at runtime, the broker re-checks three optional ledger methods at runtime, and CallBudget holds reconnect-only maps and methods, so every new launch class must edit the platform-neutral barrier.

Independent assessment

Original problem and consequence

Concrete costs. (a) settlement 'reconnect' without a hook is a thrown Error at launcher-barrier.ts:455-456 rather than a type the compiler checks. (b) refundable (:462) is derived from the settlement name, so a new settlement that is refundable but not a reservation has to edit the same three-way chain at :519-530, and its refund rule is inferred rather than declared. (c) BrokerReservationLedger makes three reconnect methods optional (transport-broker.ts:273-275) and transport-broker.ts:471-474 re-checks them, so the ledger contract is a runtime promise. (d) CallBudget keeps four reconnect-only structures (call-budget.ts:260-263) and reconnect methods (:482, :498, :507) that repeat the continuityDigest comparisons used by the reservation ledger. The barrier's own header (launcher-barrier.ts:15-23) says it must stay platform-neutral and minimal, and this is the opposite of that. Simpler general change: the barrier takes one settlement strategy as a discriminated union, with its own spend, attest and refund hooks; the reconnect module owns its bookkeeping and passes the strategy in; and the ledger exposes only reserve, spend and release.

Original problem and consequence

Cost: a new launch identity field, or a tightened evidence rule, has to be written into both validators by hand. The correction validator is the one that stands in for the reservation as the spend ceiling, so an edit that reaches only one of the two leaves the other weaker without any test necessarily failing. Simplest form: one assertLaunchIdentity(registration, refuse) covering runId, taskSessionId, workflowId, phaseId, phaseOrdinal, adapterId and role, and one evidenceMatchesLaunch(evidence, registration) covering taskSessionId, taskState RUNNING, workflowId, phaseId, phaseOrdinal, phaseKind agent, adapterId and role. Each validator keeps only its own trailing clauses: reservationId for agent-phase, and correctionRound, tranche, continuityHandle and verifiedContinuity for correction.

Original problem and consequence

policy/sandbox-broker.ts:430 calls assertClean(request.worktree, 'before', this.#git) and line 431 then calls captureChangeSet(request.worktree, this.#git) on the same tree with nothing in between. For ordinary tracked and untracked files the captured fingerprint is empty exactly when status --porcelain is empty (tracked changes against HEAD plus untracked files that are not ignored), so the clean check can be made on the fingerprint the constructor already takes. Measured here: the status scan takes 3.4-4.0 s, and the diff that captureChangeSet runs over the same tree costs the same order (git diff --quiet HEAD alone took 2.8 s). Cheaper alternative: raise WorktreeNotClean from the fingerprint and drop the separate scan, saving one full tree scan per permission session.

Original problem and consequence

The duplicated steps are the witness capture arguments (protected-commit.ts:131-137 and protected-reconcile.ts:390-396), the directory fsync (protected-commit.ts:168-169 and protected-reconcile.ts:417-418) and the HEAD, tree and index verification triple (protected-commit.ts:175-177 and protected-reconcile.ts:421-425). They already diverge. The transport finishes the index rename after a handled interruption (protected-commit.ts:144-166), while the recovery path lets the same interruption propagate through its finally and leaves the lock for a later run. Each shape is defended in its own comments, but the mutation-boundary rules (witness before compare-and-swap, re-prove before rename, verify after) now live in two places, so a new check added to one, for example before the rename, has to be mirrored by hand in the other or the two paths disagree on what a refused publication leaves behind. Simpler fix: one publication routine with an explicit finish-on-interruption policy, called by both the transport and the recovery.

B1-70unverifiablerecorded: wontfix concurrent recursive validation needs a global work limit and changes fail-fast/refusal ordering; keep pre-PREPARED traversal serialseedWorktreePaths validates each seeded tree with one awaited lstat per entry in strict sequence before any copy starts, which takes 12-14 seconds for the 6,571-entry node_modules that awsf.config.yaml seeds on every start.

Original problem and consequence

validateSeedEntry (worktrees.ts:93-104) opens each directory and awaits validateSeedEntry for each child inside a for-await loop, so no two lstat calls are ever in flight. probe-seed-walk.mjs replicates that traversal over the repository's node_modules (6,571 entries, 514 directories, 14 symlinks) and measured 14.1 s and 11.9 s serially, against 5.4 s and 6.2 s when the same traversal runs 16 children at a time. start.ts:344 calls seedWorktreePaths unconditionally after createWorktree, and adopt.ts:500 does the same, so each attempt pays the serial walk before the copy begins. Cheaper alternative: run each directory's children through a bounded pool of about 16 and keep the validate-before-copy ordering, which preserves the refusal-before-copy guarantee and cut the validation pass by about 55 percent in the probe. The cp copy that follows is not measured here.

Jev answers stop-judgment with its three declared answers plus one undeclared key. B2-05unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe sessions 'before' cursor is validated as any ISO timestamp with 0-9 fractional digits but reaches a text comparison unnormalized, so a cursor not in the stored millisecond form returns rows at or after the cursor and mis-orders the page.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A client pages with before=2026-10-12T10:00:00Z, which is accepted because the regex allows no fraction and Date.parse succeeds. listSessions compares started_at < ? as text (queries.ts:85-86), while stored values have the form 2026-10-12T10:00:00.000Z. The row at exactly 10:00:00.000 compares as smaller ('.' sorts before 'Z') and is returned again, and the row at 10:00:00.500 is returned even though it is newer than the cursor, so page boundaries duplicate and reorder rows. The dashboard avoids this by echoing the server's startedAt (dashboard/src/session-pages.ts:17), so the defect reaches hand-written API clients and any cursor not in canonical form. Fix: normalize with new Date(before).toISOString() after the validation at routes.ts:412, before routes.ts:429 passes the value on.

B2-07unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe production consumer of probe failures keeps only failure.reasonCode, so the raw file the probe retains is referenced by no journal record, unlike the other raw/ writers, and the retention write itself can reject probeQuota.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Removed by 21d892b: QuotaProbeResult's stderr and error fields, the only raw error detail callers received before. In their place 21d892b made retention part of the failure contract: nonzero and unparseable responses are retained before journalling, and the comment above retainQuotaFailureInAttempt (probe.ts:164) says the returned path is attempt-relative 'so the journal records no machine path', which presumes the journal carries it. The callbacks at production-run.ts:1699 and 3279 keep only reasonCode, dropping retainedPath, exitCode, faultCount, timeoutMs and foundVersion. The quota-snapshot evidence (core/src/observability/attempt-evidence.ts:181) has no path field, and doctor/quota.ts and cli/commands/quota.ts render reasonCode, not the retained path or exit code. The other raw/ writers do record their paths in journal records (rawOutputPath at production-run.ts:3065, diffRef at production-run.ts:3421). Separately, retainFailureBytes is unguarded: an EACCES or ENOSPC from mkdir/writeFile (probe.ts:296) rejects probeQuota (probe P4). The call at production-run.ts:1689 sits after the try block that closes at line 1671, so the rejection leaves executeProductionCommand. That contradicts the docstring's 'No failure throws into the run merely because the quota gauge could not be read.'

B2-11resolvedrecorded: fixedactOf() maps the owner's resume-activation evidence only to 'resume', never to 'continue', so a Delegate 'continue' proposed at a ticket-block stop can never pair as a match and the continue judgment act can never be earned.

Independent assessment

Continue can be observed through cancellation plus an explicitly linked successor, rather than falsely treating every resume as continue.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/delegate/agreement.ts; core/test/unit/delegate/agreement-continue-b2-11.test.ts
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
This supplies the observation path needed to earn agreement. It does not prove enough real owner decisions have accumulated to authorize it.

Original problem and consequence

policy.ts:279 proposes 'continue' at a ticket-block stop when Jev picks it, and allowedActsFor offers it there (policy.ts:145). The owner-side resume that clears a ticket-block journals resume-activation (production-run.ts:3441; the branch fires for the ticket-block restart phase because its kind is 'code', not 'agent'), and actOf maps that record to 'resume' (agreement.ts:59). pairAttempt then compares expectedAct('continue') === 'continue' with 'resume' and marks every such pair 'mismatch'. Pairs with no observed act are 'none' and are excluded from the window (autonomy.ts:56), so the window fills with mismatches and autonomyFor('continue') stays 'not-earned' under any lease (autonomy.ts:85), although the header at autonomy.ts:4-6 says continue unlocks at 7 of 8. The evidence carries only a checkpointId, so actOf cannot tell a ticket-block resume from a quota resume. 'route-fallback' and 'wait-until' appear in ObservedAct (agreement.ts:24) but actOf can never return them either, and the default branch at agreement.ts:67-68 hides the gap.

B2-12resolvedrecorded: fixedautonomyFor reports the code-decided owner acts raise, resume, wait-until and cancel as live under any lease, although it never receives the acts the lease names, so the 'lease that names it' condition of AGENTS.md invariant 13 is not enforced by the authority predicate.

Original problem and consequence

AGENTS.md invariant 13 says: 'The Delegate acts only under an owner lease ... under an owner-granted, task-scoped, revocable lease that names it.' autonomy.ts:81 checks only for a missing lease, and autonomy.ts:82 returns live true for every code-decided act whenever a lease exists. The signature (autonomy.ts:69) takes leaseAutonomy typed 'earned' | 'all' | null (autonomy.ts:24), not PolicyLease.acts (policy.ts:93-94), so a lease that names only route-fallback still reports cancel, raise, resume and wait-until as live. raise, resume and cancel are OWNER_ACTS (docs/driving/marimba/marimba-guard-rules.mts:25), which is what makes this a breach of the rule and not only a design note. It is latent: no core/src caller reads .live yet, and the delegate-authority fence that invariant 13 names as enforcement (W19 task 8) is absent from core/test/unit/meta, so nothing mechanical catches it. The first executor that gates on .live alone would breach the rule.

B2-17resolvedrecorded: fixedcurrentPlans swallows every error from the per-read catalog re-resolution and keeps serving the previous plan set, so a plan that becomes unresolvable while the dashboard runs is neither refused by name nor reported, contrary to AGENTS.md invariant 12.

Verification strength
owner decision + regression tests

Original problem and consequence

AGENTS.md invariant 12 says: 'A ticket set whose plan cannot be resolved is a hard failure, not a skip; a plan whose declared format the fence does not implement is refused by name rather than parsed to zero tasks.' routes.ts:392-397 re-resolves the catalog on every read, and any throw returns the old plans object (routes.ts:396). Edit awsf.project.yaml while the dashboard is running so that plans.format names an unimplemented format (plan-source.ts:277-279 throws UnsupportedPlanFormatError by name) or the plans root disappears: /api/v1/tickets and /api/v1/sessions keep returning the last-good backlog with HTTP 200, and the named refusal never reaches any response. routes.ts:387-388 documents the swallow as deliberate ('a catalog that fails to resolve mid-edit keeps serving the last good set'). The rule carves out no mid-edit exception, so the deliberate design conflicts with the rule as written. This candidate rests on that textual conflict; it was verified by code reading, not by a runtime probe of the mid-run path.

Original problem and consequence

The dashboard is serving tickets and the catalog is briefly absent (an editor's save-by-rename, a delete and recreate, a checkout). On the next read, currentPlans() (routes.ts:390-399) calls resolveTicketPlanSources, which returns [] on ENOENT (routes.ts:339) rather than throwing. The catch at routes.ts:393-397 never runs, planCatalogKey([]) differs from plans.key, and routes.ts:398 installs planCatalog([]). Plans and tickets vanish (a single-ticket read returns 404 ticket-not-found), and the PlanTicketReader per-file cache is discarded, so the first read after the file returns re-parses every ticket. A present-but-malformed catalog keeps the last good set (it takes the throw path), so the promise holds for malformed content but not for a missing file.

The caller receives no ApiRouter and so cannot call close(), and the handle stays open for the life of the process. The CLI exits right after, so the impact there is small; a host that rebuilds routers in-process accumulates handles. The same shape appears in server.ts: createApiServer builds the router at server.ts:35, and when start() rejects on listen (server.ts:51-63, for example EADDRINUSE) it returns the error without router.close(). createApiServer is referenced only by its unit test today, so the server.ts half is latent.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/api/routes.ts:382 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B2-22. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: createApiRouter closes readDb if plan catalog resolution throws; createApiServer closes router if server.listen rejects.

B2-23unverifiablerecorded: fixedoneHeader's 'must occur at most once' check tests for an array, but Node never yields an array for host or origin, so the branch is dead and a duplicated Host header is accepted using its first value.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A raw request carrying 'Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>' followed by 'Host: evil.example' passes validateAuthority, because Node keeps only the first host value (loopback) and silently drops the second. RFC 9112 section 3.2 requires a 400 response for more than one Host field, so the guard's stated contract is not enforced. Duplicate Origin headers are joined by Node into one comma-separated string that URL parsing refuses, so Origin is refused by accident, not by this check. A browser cannot send a duplicated Host, and routing only reads the first value, so I found no exploit; the defect is the unenforced contract and the dead branch.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/api/security.ts:47 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B2-23. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: oneHeader rejects duplicated host headers containing comma-delimited values with invalid-host.

Original problem and consequence

routing.quota_stop.default is 60 minutes and an adapter is named toString (IdentifierString in config/schema.ts:43 allows it). For a route with 30 minutes to reset, buildQuotaReadout gives configuredThresholdMinutes null and verdict disabled, while a control route named claude-main gets below. The only stop is verdict === 'below' (production-run.ts:3297), so the start path fails open and the run is not parked. The resume threshold lookup at production-run.ts:4001 uses the same indexing and refuses with the misleading 'below its threshold' message. The likelihood is low because the adapter name has to collide with an Object.prototype key.

B2-35unverifiablerecorded: dup-of B13-04The scheme/userinfo credential pattern is quadratic on long letter-digit runs, and publicApiValue applies every credential pattern to every string of every API response, so one large unbroken token stalls the Node event loop.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A string containing an unbroken run of about 40,000 letters, digits, '+', '.' or '-' (a long hex blob inside an event payload, envelope, or provider response, for example) makes scrubCredentialString take about 4.4 s of synchronous CPU per call. The leading scheme group [a-z][a-z0-9+.-]* is retried from every start position and backtracks across the whole run before failing at the missing '://', so cost grows with the square of the run length: measured about 4x per doubling, and extrapolated to roughly 15 s for this pattern alone at 80,000 characters. Every API response passes through it (responses.ts:59 via jsonResponse), and decide.ts:179 applies scrubJsonText to provider responses, so each such request stalls the single-threaded dashboard for its duration.

Historical classification: bug · low · PLAUSIBLE. Original location: core/src/api/responses.ts:49 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B2-35. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

dup-of B13-04: bounded scheme length in URL credential pattern prevents quadratic backtracking on unbroken character runs.

B2-37unverifiablerecorded: fixedask() returns refused-by-switch before validating the request, so with the project switch off an invalid question set comes back as an outcome instead of the QuestionValidationError that decide.ts documents as a code defect.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

With decision.jev off, a stop-judgment question set broken by a code change (an empty choice criteria, or a score with one level, for example) is never validated: ask() returns { outcome: 'refused-by-switch' } and decide() writes a clean refused record. The defect surfaces only when the switch is turned on, and then the same throw is caught by the callers (core/src/delegate/shadow.ts:103 and core/src/cli/commands/delegate-replay.ts:163) and journaled as 'unavailable', so it is never reported as a defect. The contract at decide.ts:63 ('Throws QuestionValidationError for a request that could never be valid ... a code defect, not an outcome') and at jev-transport.ts:384-387 is not met while the switch is off. Fix: run validateJevRequest (line 393) before the switch check at line 389; nothing is sent in either order.

B2-39unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe groups list and the group detail disagree about whether a group exists: the list pushes every group directory, including one with no journal at revision 0, while the detail route and the CLI each re-derive absence from a revision-0 sentinel.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

A first capture that fails after AttemptLock.withLock has created projects/<p>/groups/<id>/ (for example verifyOperation throws in planning/store.ts append, or the process dies before the first append) leaves a directory with no journal. replay() returns emptyGroup (revision 0) because a missing journal is an empty ok scan, so listGroupSummaries lists the group with revision 0 and title null. GET /api/v1/groups?group=<id> then answers 404 group-not-found, and awsf group reports 'group not found' for the same id, so the dashboard shows a row it cannot open. The fix belongs in the reader: readGroupTree should report absence once, and the list, the route and the CLI should all consume that one fact instead of checking revision === 0 at each call site.

fixed: Omit revision-zero directories from the group list, matching detail and CLI absence semantics.

B2-40unverifiablerecorded: fixedpublicApiValue copies every response body, then scrubCredentials copies it again while running the credential scrubber over every string leaf and rebuilding all ten credential RegExps for each string, so each sessions poll during an active run pays a full scrub of the whole page.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

While a run is active the dashboard polls every 500 ms (dashboard/src/composables/usePolling.ts:4 live cadence) and loadAllSessions (dashboard/src/session-pages.ts) requests every page of /api/v1/sessions on each poll, so the whole projection is scrubbed each time. On a synthetic 100-card page (65,000 string leaves, 2.0 MB JSON) publicApiValue alone takes a median 693 ms and the full dispatch 804 ms, so one page occupies most of a poll interval on the single API event loop; linear extrapolation to 300 sessions gives about 2 s of scrubbing per 500 ms poll on this machine. The cost per response is string leaves times ten RegExp constructions plus ten replace passes. Cheaper alternative: build the global pattern variants once at module load instead of inside globalCredentialPattern on every call (precompiling those variants alone cut the scrub from 318 ms to 92 ms on a 52,900-leaf page), and fold the private-key filter and the scrub into one traversal.

Historical classification: cleanup · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/api/responses.ts:49 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B2-40. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Precompile shared global credential patterns and perform private-key removal plus credential redaction in one detached traversal.

B2-42unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe metrics handler recomputes the whole payload on every request, and that recomputation runs one synchronous git cat-file (spawnSync) per sealed shift ticket of every shift session plus a status.json read and a shift recompile, with no cache even though the inputs (recorded base SHA and sealed manifest digest) never change.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

The metrics tab polls GET /api/v1/metrics every 5 s while it is open (dashboard/src/routes/metrics.vue, usePolling with the idle cadence). readRunFacts calls readShiftTaskClasses for each shift session (metrics/role-rows.ts:553), and task-class.ts:35 spawns git once per ticket through systemGitRunner, which goes through runSystemCommand and spawnSync (execution/transport-broker.ts:247), so the single API event loop is blocked for the duration of every spawn (each allowed up to 30 s). Measured here: 17.4 ms median per cat-file. Five shifts of eight tickets is about 0.7 s of blocked event loop per metrics poll, and the 500 ms sessions polls queue behind it. The join depends only on the recorded base SHA and the manifest digest, so memoizing it per journal path and digest removes the spawns after the first request, and one git cat-file --batch per shift would also cut them.
