B2-43unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe adapters route derives every adapter's status from its config kind and never asks the adapter layer for its own availability, although HarnessAdapter.isAvailable() (adapters/availability.ts executableAvailability, reached through adapters/registry.ts adapterFor) owns that verdict.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

For a claude-code entry whose executable is not installed, GET /api/v1/adapters reports status 'configured' and code null, while ClaudeCodeAdapter.isAvailable() for the same entry returns blocked with ExecutableNotFound. The antigravity special case at line 600 re-derives AntigravityAdapter.isAvailable()'s verdict (antigravity.ts:33-41: blocked, E_ADAPTER_UNVERIFIED) by kind, so the route goes stale if that verdict changes. If 'configured' is meant to mean 'not probed', the route still answers a health question, because the type is named AdapterHealth and 'blocked' is a health reading. Fix: build each adapter with adapterFor(entry) and report its isAvailable() result, which makes the handler async.

Original problem and consequence

A later module that calls the Jev endpoint through `(0, fetch)(url)`, `globalThis["fetch"](url)`, `const f = fetch; await f(url)`, `const { fetch: f } = globalThis`, or `self.fetch(url)` passes both the meta-test and the awsf doctor fence row, which report 'fence intact'. Importing JEV_ENDPOINT from the transport also avoids the endpoint regex, since the path string never appears in that module. The regex is also the only enforcement, and a second copy in the doctor can drift from the one in the meta-test. The simpler mechanism is to check the capability rather than one call shape: a word-level `fetch` identifier check over core/src outside the transport, kept in one shared pattern module that both the test and the doctor import.

B2-45unverifiablerecorded: fixedA broad catch around decide() turns a persistence failure that happens after an answered Jev call into a recorded 'unavailable' outcome, so the Delegate's audit line misstates what Jev returned.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

decide() asks the transport, receives an answer, and then calls appendTaskDecision (decide.ts:68). If that append or assertDecisionRecord throws (disk full, I/O error, a builder defect), the catch at shadow.ts:103-107 writes a delegate.proposal with decision.outcome 'unavailable' and recordId null. policy.ts:201 then maps the non-answered judgment to rationale jev-unavailable, even though Jev answered and the call was charged. Agreement and autonomy (task 6) later score that proposal against the owner's act as if no answer existed. decide() already states that a QuestionValidationError is a code defect, not an outcome, and this catch hides that too. The depth fix is for decide() to surface persistence failure as its own state, or propagate it, and for the shadow runner to act only on the typed outcomes.

Historical classification: cleanup · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/delegate/shadow.ts:103 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B2-45. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Convert only transport throws to typed unavailable; let decision validation and durable-append failures propagate.

B2-49unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe ticket-source route opts out of the shared response scrubber by overwriting the body of a response the scrubber has already built, so the exception is implicit and the shared helper's contract is untrue for this route.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

jsonResponse always scrubs its body through publicApiValue (responses.ts:59). The ticket-source route needs verbatim repository text, so it builds jsonResponse(null) and then spreads a new body over it. The scrub still runs on null, the verbatim body is attached by overwrite, and nothing in responses.ts names the exception. Any later change to the response shape that adds a field alongside body, or any reader who trusts that every jsonResponse body is scrubbed, gets the bypass without knowing it exists. The fix is an explicit verbatim option in the shared helper (for example a sibling constructor in responses.ts), so the one exception is stated where the scrubbing is defined.

The switch decides whether any Jev call may leave: JevTransport.ask returns refused-by-switch when it is off (jev-transport.ts:389-390). Fix: export one reader and call it from shadow.ts, delegate-replay.ts and jev-doctor.ts.

B2-55unverifiablerecorded: fixedJev's two gates, the project switch and the credential, are resolved separately by each caller with different defaults, so the no-call guarantees depend on which caller runs.

Independent assessment

Verification strength

Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

shadow.ts:88 reads the switch from the attempt repository's catalog, but cli/commands/delegate-replay.ts:82 returns "on" when no catalog path is given without reading any catalog, so a live replay built without catalogPath asks Jev in a project whose awsf.project.yaml sets decision.jev: off. A third copy, decision/jev-doctor.ts:77-91, reports an unreadable or invalid catalog as an error, where shadow.ts:51-64 turns Jev off. The credential is caller-resolved too: JevTransport reads process.env when env is omitted (jev-transport.ts:361), and shadow.ts:89 omits env when the caller gives none. The only guard against live calls under test is the NODE_TEST_CONTEXT env rewrite at cli/main.ts:263, which protects one caller and not the default. Latent today: delegateReplayCommand has no CLI caller, and recordShadowProposal has one caller (main.ts) that always passes env. The simpler mechanism is one decision/ function that resolves switch and key from an explicit project root and env, used by every caller, with a transport that takes its credential explicitly and never falls back to ambient process state.

fixed: Require an explicit env object at the transport boundary; unresolved project identity fails closed, and missing-catalog/default-on cannot borrow ambient credentials.

B2-56unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe stop-judgment adapter is written twice: the shadow runner (shadow.ts:91-107) and the live replay judge (core/src/cli/commands/delegate-replay.ts:156-166) each map decide() to a JudgmentInput and decision with the same unavailable fallback, and projectSwitch is copied in both files (shadow.ts:51-64, delegate-replay.ts:81-89).

Original problem and consequence

The two copies differ only in the caller kind ('stop' versus 'replay'), the taskRoot they pass, and how the optional now and newId are passed. Any change to the fallback or the mapping (a new decide() outcome, recording the thrown reason) has to be made twice, and the shadow path and replay path can then disagree about what the same failed Jev call means for the same policy input. Simplest form: one helper in delegate/ returning a judge of the existing ReplayJudge shape (replay.ts:115-118, (facts, allowedActs) => Promise of {judgment, decision}), parameterized by caller kind, taskRoot and the optional now/newId/projectDecision; both call sites pass it. The projectSwitch copies collapse to the single-try form delegate-replay.ts already uses, which matches shadow.ts's two-try version except when loadCatalog throws an error whose code is ENOENT.

B2-57unverifiablerecorded: fixedparseScope recomputes the binding window id with a second limitingWindowId call after parseScopeFigure already derived the same value at line 185 and discarded it, passing a throwaway faults array.

Independent assessment

Original problem and consequence

The same fact is derived twice and the second derivation hides its faults. When the minutesToReset gate at line 204 passes, the second call returns the same id as the first, so it only re-derives a known value. Probe: a valid instant reports windowId w1 with minutesToReset 60, and an invalid instant reports windowId null with minutesToReset null, which is the gate working. A later change to the binding rule applied in one call and not the other would make windowId name a different window than the minutes figure. Simplest form: return the bindingId from parseScopeFigure alongside minutesToReset, and set windowId to it only when minutesToReset is non-null, which removes the second call and the discarded faults array.

Original problem and consequence

policy.ts:15 imports raiseActsNeeded from cli/commands/shift.ts, which imports node:fs/promises and raise.ts, so the delegate policy reaches up into the CLI layer. policy.ts:217 computes the ceiling-pause target as callsSpent + callsReserved + agentCallsFrom(...) + 1. production-run.ts ceilingPauseBefore adds the reserve only when the guard at 3167 holds (no route continuity, maxCorrections not 0, auto allowance not 0), and its advice minimumCeiling is budget.committed + initialCalls + 1 (3177). StopFactsPhase carries only id, ticket and route, so the policy cannot evaluate that guard. The literal is right today only because production pauses only where the guard held. If production changes the reserve, the shadow raise plan and the owner-facing advice drift apart, and agreement scores the gap as mismatches. The fix is to move the reserve rule and raiseActsNeeded into state/tiers.ts beside ceilingFor, have the pause advice and the policy call one function, and carry correction eligibility in the stop facts.

Original problem and consequence

In live mode each stop is one stop-judgment call (decide, then JevTransport.ask with a deadline of JEV_DEADLINE_MS, 30 s). The stops are independent: each judgment reads only its own facts and allowed acts, yet replay.ts:141-153 runs them in series, and delegate-replay.ts:173 runs the attempts in series too. A 40-stop replay therefore waits for 40 round trips, and four in flight would take about a quarter of that. Separately, replay.ts:147 slices the journal prefix for every stop, and buildStopFacts rescans it five or six times through the evidenceOf helper (stop-facts.ts:164-174) for the transition, gate, quota, phase-accepted, review and envelope evidence. Not measured. Bounded concurrency needs Journal.append (called per record from appendTaskDecision) to be safe under overlapping decide() calls, which was not checked here.

ELI B2 · Delegating work without giving away control

This batch covers delegated decisions, spending limits and the information sent to the dashboard. The checked repairs make unexpected answers easier to record, show plan errors honestly and require permission for each delegated action. That supports keeping the owner in control. It does not prove that every decision or spending-limit rule works, because most findings in this batch were not rechecked in depth.

Carried scoped judgments: 7 of 66 findings. The other 59 remain unverified. No new mechanism-level review of this batch is claimed.

B3-01resolvedrecorded: fixedEach K1 field reason is capped at 4000 characters, but evaluateWriteBoundary joins its problem list with no bound, so a write-boundary refusal naming roughly 31 or more unclassified shift DO-block paths produces a record that fails its own contract; assertDriverPreflightRecord then throws and the preflight refusal is never journaled.

Independent assessment

Bounded refusal text retains leading problems and an omitted-count suffix so a failed preflight can itself be journaled.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/contracts/driver-preflight.ts:75-92; core/src/preflight/fields.ts:39-42
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Truncation is intentional and should not hide the fact that more problems exist.

Original problem and consequence

A multi-ticket shift whose DO blocks name more than about 30 repository paths that the driver did not classify with --read. fields.ts:292 adds one problem per token, verdict() at fields.ts:37 joins them with no truncation, and preflight.ts:434 asserts the finished record, which fails maxLength 4000. The command aborts with 'invalid awsf.driver-preflight/v1 record at /fields/1: Expected union value' and no record is journaled, although the contract header (driver-preflight.ts:14-15) says the record is appended whether or not every field passed. The driver loses the list of problems it needs to fix. The same unbounded join feeds the grant-refusal reason at production-run.ts:1438 (owed.paths.join) against the same cap, which applies to the grant-refused record reason at driver-preflight.ts:196, so a long planned-path list aborts the grant refusal the same way.

fixed: verdict() and the grant-refused reason use boundedJoin under K1_REASON_MAX_LENGTH, so long problem/path lists keep the leading items and end with an exact "… and N more"; both refusals validate against their records

B3-05unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe trailing-object salvage in extract() only tries suffixes that start after the first brace (opening > first), so the envelope object that starts at the first brace and ends before the last brace is never tried; a valid envelope followed by prose that contains braces is refused as not-json.

Original problem and consequence

A model emits a correct envelope and then a trailing note such as 'Note: the {x} placeholder is unused.' The outermost slice (first brace to last brace) contains the note and fails to parse. The backward loop at lines 104-109 starts at the last brace and stops at the first brace, so the envelope itself is never retried, and parseEnvelope returns a not-json violation. The same envelope with the note placed before it is recovered as trailing-object, so acceptance depends on where the prose sits. The file's own comment (lines 95-97) says prose on either side of a well-formed object is recovered here. A not-json result costs a correction round, and fails the phase when the phase has none.

B3-07unverifiablerecorded: fixedAn absent attempt ceiling resolves to the global DEFAULT_CALL_CEILINGS in ceilingFor, and CallBudget.snapshot() writes that default back as the attempt's recorded ceiling. start.ts reads the same absent value against the configured risk.call_ceiling table, so the preflight and the ledger disagree on one attempt's ceiling.

Original problem and consequence

A pre-dial attempt has no budget.ceiling, which attempt.ts keeps absent on purpose (lines 288-294). With risk.call_ceiling.T2 set to 2, the preflight at start.ts:279-280 sizes against 2, but the ledger built at call-budget.ts:269-270 resolves ceilingFor(2) = 5, so a 5-call reservation is allowed (probe p1). The first attempt.updated persist writes ceiling 5 (call-budget.ts:325), so the default becomes the attempt's recorded ceiling, which attempt.ts says must never be written in. The configured ceiling is exceeded by 3 calls. Latent for the current config: root awsf.config.yaml:149 sets T2 to 5, equal to the default, and the production newCommand callers pass the configured table (new.ts:124-126), so only pre-dial attempts reach this path. Fix: keep ceiling absent in the snapshot and resolve an absent ceiling from the configured table at one shared site.

B3-08unresolved057370d recheck · Historical ledger: recorded: not-reproduced durationMs >= 0 is correct contract invariant; negative duration requires external clock rollback not reproducedCommandDispatchResultSchema requires durationMs >= 0, but the three command-dispatch writers compute it from the wall clock (Date.now() minus a start stamp), so a backward clock step during a configured gate command writes a negative durationMs that the ledger reader refuses on every later read of that attempt.

Independent assessment

Elapsed durations still subtract wall-clock readings while the contract requires a non-negative integer. Not reproducing an external clock rollback does not remove the mechanism.

Verification strength
inspection only
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/cli/commands/production-run.ts:2337,2385; core/src/cli/commands/rework.ts:1160,1198; core/src/cli/commands/adopt.ts:895,935
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Inject a backward wall-clock step and verify durable command results remain valid. No system clock was changed here.

Original problem and consequence

A gate command runs across a backward wall-clock step (NTP step, WSL2/VM resume correction, or a manual clock change). production-run.ts:2183 stores a negative durationMs; persist() appends the command-dispatch-result evidence with no assertCommandDispatchResult call on the write path; the next ledger read in core/src/workflow/command-ledger-store.ts:80 runs assertCommandDispatchResult over every stored result and throws 'command dispatch result is invalid', so every later read of that attempt's command ledger (restore, recovery, adoption, next gate dispatch) fails and the attempt cannot be resumed from its ledger. The adapter path avoids this: core/src/adapters/stream/event-sequencer.ts:589 clamps the same kind of value with 'elapsed > 0 ? Math.round(elapsed) : 0', so only the dispatch writers are exposed. Rare trigger, durable consequence.

B3-09unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe worktree-relative path pattern's `..` and `//` lookaheads use `.*`, which does not match a newline, and `^`/`$` anchor only the whole string, so an embedded newline blinds both rules and WorktreeRelativePath accepts traversal that its own comment says is refused.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A path such as "x\n/../../../etc/passwd" passes WorktreeRelativePath, while "../../../etc/passwd" is refused, and "x\n//y" passes the doubled-separator rule. Any model-emitted path that reaches an envelope schema therefore skips the structural floor the comment promises (envelope-base.ts:15-21). The escape is contained today for artifact paths: production-run.ts artifactReader (lines 875-880) resolves the path and refuses one that leaves the worktree. The other model-claimed path fields I traced (changedFiles, findings.file) are compared as strings with git-derived paths (diffMatchesClaims; gates/review.ts:51), so nothing opens a file from them. The same lookahead shape is in ShiftManifestTicketSchema.path (shift-selection-record.ts:21) and closure-record.ts:6; the shift manifest is host-sealed, so that path is not reachable from model output. Low. This is distinct from Altitude-6, which concerns the other rule sets, not newlines.

B3-10unverifiablerecorded: fixedcanonicalJson serialises any non-plain object (Date, Map, class instance) as {} and NaN or Infinity as null, while undefined throws, so distinct values share one digest and the digest silently ignores their content.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

canonicalJson({at: new Date(0)}) and canonicalJson({at: new Date(1000)}) both return {"at":{}}, so their sha256 digests are identical; the same holds for {x: NaN} and {x: null}, and for {m: new Map([["a",1]])} and {m: {}}. Recovery, grant, amendment and ticket-selection digests all go through this function, so an input carrying a Date or NaN would be bound to a digest that does not change with its content. I found no live digested input of those types: the Date-producing sites on digest paths (grant.ts:45, land.ts:311, protected-grants.ts:227) write toISOString() strings, and quota readings store null for non-numeric minutes. Latent, low. The inconsistency is the footgun: an undefined field fails loudly (line 67), while these fail silently.

B3-11unverifiablerecorded: fixedbound() cuts the rendered value at 199 UTF-16 code units, so a surrogate pair that straddles the cut leaves a lone high surrogate at the end of the retained violation's received text.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A rejected envelope whose text reaches the cut inside an astral character, such as an emoji, gets a received value ending in a lone high surrogate followed by the ellipsis, and the value is 200 units long. When that evidence is rendered or written as UTF-8 the character becomes U+FFFD instead of the emoji. There is no crash and no other field is affected, so the impact is cosmetic. The fix is to cut on a code point boundary, for example by spreading the string into code points, or to back off one unit when the cut lands on a high surrogate.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/contracts/parse-envelope.ts:54 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-11. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: The retained violation value backs off a high surrogate at the cut, so it ends on a whole character.

B3-12unverifiablerecorded: fixedNON_BLOCKING_REVIEW_SEVERITIES is taken from REVIEW_SEVERITIES by position ([0] and [1]) rather than by filtering out BLOCKING_SEVERITIES, so it matches the non-blocking set only because the current vocabulary happens to start with the two non-blocking values.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Latent, no current failure. review-output.ts:9 defines REVIEW_SEVERITIES as low, medium, high, critical, and review-output.ts:16 defines BLOCKING_SEVERITIES as high, critical, so today [0] and [1] give low and medium, which is correct. If a severity is inserted below medium (for example 'minor' after 'low'), the set becomes low and minor; a medium architecture finding is then non-blocking but fails NonBlockingArchitectureReviewFindingSchema, and the plan context cannot be composed. Nothing ties this list to BLOCKING_SEVERITIES, so the drift stays silent until the planner phase fails. Filtering REVIEW_SEVERITIES by BLOCKING_SEVERITIES stays correct under any reordering.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/contracts/plan-context.ts:19 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-12. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: NON_BLOCKING_REVIEW_SEVERITIES is the vocabulary filtered by the blocking set, not a position slice.

B3-13unverifiablerecorded: fixedassertExactProtectedPath refuses backslash, colon, asterisk, question mark, brackets, braces and bang, but still accepts double quote, less-than, greater-than and pipe, which Windows file names cannot contain, so a protected grant can name a path the owner's NTFS-mounted checkout cannot hold.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

The owner grants a protected path such as src/a|b.ts. assertExactProtectedPath accepts it, so the grant and its consumption are issued, and the failure surfaces late when the builder tries to create the file on the /mnt/d (NTFS) checkout, rather than being refused at grant time. This is fail-closed (no bypass was found), but the character list does not match the Windows-reserved set it appears to cover, and the error text promises an exact, normalized, repository-relative path.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/contracts/protected-grant.ts:106 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-13. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

fixed: assertExactProtectedPath refuses double quote, less-than, greater-than and pipe.

B3-15unverifiablerecorded: fixedREVIEW_CONTEXT_DIFF_MAX_CHARS is documented as sized against the 256 KiB envelope byte cap, but the diff bound counts UTF-16 code units, so a bounded diff made of 3-byte UTF-8 characters serializes past that cap.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A candidate whose changed lines are mostly 3-byte text (CJK, em dashes, box-drawing) is bounded by boundReviewDiff to 95,805 code units (review-evidence.ts:159 passes the 96,000 budget), but the serialized diff alone is about 279,562 bytes, above MAX_ENVELOPE_BYTES = 262,144. The reviewEvidenceFitness precondition then fails its 'the envelope fits the wire limit' check (gates/review.ts:326), which the file says is answered before the call is spent. The bound never trims further, so that candidate cannot be reviewed. ASCII diffs of the same size fit (about 96,202 bytes). Low severity: the trigger needs a diff that is mostly 3-byte characters.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/contracts/review-context.ts:35 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-15. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: composeReviewEvidence bounds the diff to a 192 KiB UTF-8 allowance; ASCII diffs keep the full budget.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A stored envelope with valid true and payload null, or valid false with a non-null payload and an empty violations array, passes Value.Check(StoredEnvelopeSchema(...)). No production code calls the mirror today (only core/test/unit/contracts/stored-envelope.test.ts does), so this is latent; a future read-side check built on the mirror would accept a record whose validity and payload contradict each other.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/contracts/stored-envelope.ts:69 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-17. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: StoredEnvelopeSchema is a union of valid and invalid shapes, so validity, payload and violations must agree.

B3-18unverifiablerecorded: fixedwrapEnvelope accepts a ParseEnvelopeResult, whose extraction label records how the JSON object was recovered, and returns a StoredEnvelope that drops it, so the persisted envelope never records the salvage kind that parse-envelope.ts says the retained trace must distinguish.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A final message holds an abandoned object followed by a whole trailing object. parseEnvelope returns valid false with extraction 'trailing-object' (probe p3). engine.ts store() (parse at line 314, persist at line 325) calls wrapEnvelope and persists the result, whose keys (envelopeId through rawOutputPath, valid, payload, violations) include no extraction. A reader of the stored record cannot tell that the host took the trailing object, which is the case the parse-envelope.ts comment says must be readable after the fact; the only route is to re-run parseEnvelope over the retained raw output. No production code reads extraction (grep finds only tests). The StoredEnvelope header says identity, validity and provenance are host-assigned on this type, and extraction is provenance.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/contracts/stored-envelope.ts:102 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-18. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: wrapEnvelope keeps the parser's extraction label as optional provenance on the stored record.

B3-19unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe readout's instant pattern is `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T` with no end anchor, so the timestamp fields accept a date followed by any text, including nothing after the T.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Value.Check accepts "2026-10-13T" and "2026-10-13Tgarbage" as `cut`, as a stop's terminalAt, and as newestLanded.landedAt, and this schema is what assertTrapsReadout uses to vet the readout. Every current producer writes full ISO strings, so no real record is refused. The defect is that the contract admits values that are not timestamps, so a malformed time would pass the readout check. Latent, low. The unanchored `\S` patterns in attribution-record.ts:42 and next-steps.ts:8 are unanchored on purpose (they require a non-space character), so they are not the same defect.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/contracts/traps-readout.ts:9 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-19. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Readout instants are anchored full ISO timestamps.

B3-20unverifiablerecorded: fixedtoJsonSchema places the caller's options before the schema's own keys, so a $id, title or description the caller passes is overwritten whenever the TypeBox schema declares its own; five non-envelope emitters pass an absolute $id that never reaches the output.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

emitTicketJsonSchema (ticket.ts:53), emitShiftManifestJsonSchema (shift-selection-record.ts:66), emitProjectCatalogJsonSchema (registry/catalog-schema.ts:149), emitContractProjectionJsonSchema (registry/contracts.ts:95) and emitPlacementJsonSchema (registry/placement-schema.ts:37) each pass $id https://awsf.local/schemas/... but the emitted $id is the bare value the schema declares (awsf.ticket/v1, awsf.shift-manifest/v1, awsf.project/v1, awsf.contracts/v1, awsf.placement/v1). The caller's namespace never reaches the output, so the option is dead code. Envelope emission keeps its absolute $id because envelope schemas declare none (control case in probe p2).

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/contracts/typebox.ts:90 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-20. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: toJsonSchema precedence documented (declared identity wins); dead $id options removed from ticket and shift emitters.

B3-22resolved057370d recheck · Historical ledger: recorded: wontfix needs owner decision: L13 owner-tranche clause cannot be met in productionL13's owner-tranche clause requires the per-phase counter correctionsOwner to reach allowance.owner, but no production path increments that counter, so GATING -> BLOCKED with correction-budget-exhausted is refused for every production budget whose owner allowance is at least 1 (the repo's own awsf.config.yaml ships owner: 1).

Independent assessment

The owner tranche remains a required L13 predicate while the production correction path has no corresponding owner-spend operation. A guard probe reproduced the refusal with auto and re-entry budgets exhausted.

Verification strength
guard probe + source inspection
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/state/guards.ts:247-262; awsf.config.yaml:153-156
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The ledger acknowledges this. Resolve the policy/implementation mismatch and test the exhausted-budget owner journey. Severity is medium for availability, not merely cleanup.

Original problem and consequence

Under the repo's own config (awsf.config.yaml:150 correction_allowance { auto: 1, owner: 1 }), correctionsOwner is 0 in every production run, so L13 always refuses with 'the owner tranche still has 1 correction(s)', even when the automatic tranche and the owner re-entry are both spent. Once those two are spent, L10 is refused for every actor (CorrectionAllowanceExhausted, global), so GATING's only exit is human cancel (L14). The counter has no production writer: the sole increment is call-budget.ts:594, reached only for an owner or human phase actor (phase-machine.ts:184); production-run.ts:2981 authorizeCorrection returns only actor 'host' (lines 2991, 3003) or a refusal, and engine.ts:379-380 defaults to 'host'. Owner task re-entries draw ownerReentries (call-budget.ts:570), and transition() never reads correctionsOwner (task-machine.ts:391-406). Live caller: adopt.ts:1058 calls L13 on failed fresh gates after persisting the FAILED phase (adopt.ts:1053), and adopt.ts:1129 calls it on a failed fresh review preflight. The adoption budget is zero-seeded (adopt.ts:426-434), so the throw names an exhausted budget that was never spent and leaves the attempt at GATING with no BLOCKED edge recorded. The zero-allowance init template (init-template.ts:52) makes the clause vacuous, so the defect shows only when owner allowance is at least 1.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/state/guards.ts:240 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-22. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

wontfix needs owner decision: L13 owner-tranche clause cannot be met in production: No path spends correctionsOwner, so with owner allowance >= 1 GATING->BLOCKED is unreachable; wire owner corrections or drop the owner clause from L13.

B3-23unverifiablerecorded: fixedL17 skips every check of the observed reviewFailure when reason.code is review-unavailable, so a blocker can be journaled as transport unavailability while the recorded failure is a different one (for example a permission breach), as long as the retry count is at least 1.

Original problem and consequence

Evidence {reviewTransportRetries: 1, reviewFailure: "permission-breach"} with reason.code "review-unavailable" is ACCEPTED as REVIEWING -> BLOCKED, while the mirror case (code "permission-breach" with reviewFailure "quota-exhausted") is REFUSED. In the current host, code and failure come from one classifier (production-run.ts:3893 omits reviewFailure for this code), but adopt.ts:1264, rework.ts:1611 and review.ts:737 set reviewFailure to the code they pass, so the callers do not agree on the shape, and this guard is the only place that could reconcile a contradictory pair. If one appeared, the owner would be told to retry a transport failure (the review-unavailable remedy), and the trap readout would count a breach under the transport trap (traps/catalogue.ts:135, seeds.ts:69). The retry test is also `retries < 1`, while its message says the rule is 'one fixed-route transport retry'. Latent: no contradictory pair is produced by the code I traced.

B3-24resolved057370d recheck · Historical ledger: recorded: fixedThe pure phase edge table has no CORRECTING->FAILED or QUEUED->FAILED edge, while settleAbnormalExit (which has no production caller) and its unit test require both to settle as FAILED, and the production abnormal-exit path reaches CORRECTING->FAILED through PhaseExecution.fail().

Independent assessment

QUEUED and CORRECTING can now fail, matching abnormal exits. The plan still describes the older edge count.

Verification strength
inspection + closeout disclosure
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/state/phase-machine.ts; FIXREPORT.md: D3
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Behavior improved. The contract/plan discrepancy needs the recorded owner amendment, not a silent status or prose change.

Original problem and consequence

Low severity, latent. A transport error thrown by send() during a same-session correction leaves the phase in CORRECTING (engine.ts:408 sets it, engine.ts:425 sends). The catch at engine.ts:582-584 calls execution.fail(), which moves CORRECTING to FAILED because workflow/phase.ts:104-108 accepts any state other than SUCCEEDED, SKIPPED or CANCELLED. The table in phase-machine.ts, which its test describes as 'the diagram ... no thirteenth' edge, refuses that transition. Nothing enforces the table on this path today. A change that routes the abnormal exit through phaseTransition or settleAbnormalExit, as the phase-machine header ('any abnormal exit records a failure') implies, would throw IllegalPhaseTransition(CORRECTING->FAILED) inside the catch and replace the original provider error.

fixed: Phase table gains QUEUED->FAILED and CORRECTING->FAILED, matching the abnormal-exit rule and production.

B3-29unverifiablerecorded: fixedUNREPORTED_TOKEN_USAGE is an exported, unfrozen object used by reference as the default usage in three command paths, which persist it and return it, so an in-place write to any returned usage object would change the shared default for every later attempt in the process.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

production-run.ts:2866, review-phase.ts:1029 and rework.ts:1028 assign `events.some(usage) ? sumUsage(events) : UNREPORTED_TOKEN_USAGE`, then persist and return that same object. No code in src writes into a usage object in place today: the one such write, adapters/stream/usage.ts:67, targets a copy (`{ ...UNREPORTED_TOKEN_USAGE }` at usage.ts:51). A later edit that patched a returned usage object, for example to fill in a count the provider omitted, would make every later 'not reported' attempt in the process report that count, with no error. Latent, low. Freezing the constant (ESM code is strict, so the write would throw) turns that into a loud failure at the first write. visual-references.ts:23 already freezes its shared limits object, so the pattern is known to the codebase.

B3-31unverifiablerecorded: fixedverifyProtectedWrite mints the write authority from an object literal whose kind and paths fields come before the spread of the verifier's result, so any kind or paths key that the verifier returns replaces the authority's own fields.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Today verifyConsumedProtectedGrant returns exactly {grant, consumption, policy} (workflow/protected-grants.ts:138), so the spread adds no conflicting key and the minted authority is correct. A later change that adds a paths or kind field to that return (for instance a path list the verifier already computes) would silently replace the write capability's path set and kind. protectedExemptionAllows (line 28) would then exempt the replaced list, and protectedWriteContext (line 32) would read the replaced kind. TypeScript does not flag it, since a later spread also wins in the merged type. Latent, low. Spreading the verifier's result first, or naming grant, consumption and policy explicitly, removes the ordering dependency.

Historical classification: bug · low · PLAUSIBLE. Original location: core/src/contracts/protected-capability.ts:39 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-31. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Write capability minted by mintWriteCapability, which sets kind and paths after the verifier's fields.

B3-32unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe published-status copy of the recovery checkpoint is validated by the bare PhaseRecoverySchema, so the cross-field rules carried by the removed or replaced lines (non-empty prefix unless a saved reply exists, a named ticket for ticket-block, stage-to-commit-evidence agreement) are enforced only in assertPhaseRecovery, which the publish path never calls. Low severity: defense-in-depth gap, no reachable writer produces these states today.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Commit 67cfd02 deleted the minItems: 1 on the prefix array (phase-recovery.ts:36 now reads prefix: Type.Array(AcceptedPhaseSchema)). Commits 8411c13, d79a2c5 and a619bcb moved the kind, stage and ticket rules into assertPhaseRecovery and assertHostValidationProgress. The only production caller of assertPhaseRecovery is workflow/phase-recovery.ts:52, on the inspect path. publish.ts:301 validates the publish output with parseEnvelope, which runs Value.Check and nothing semantic (parse-envelope.ts:199). So a PUBLISHED status carrying an inconsistent checkpoint (completed-phase with prefix [], ticket-block with no ticket, or validating at stage accept with no commit evidence) is accepted and sealed. The writer does not assert either (production-run.ts:2937 persists the checkpoint without assertPhaseRecovery), so the inconsistent state would only be refused later by inspectPhaseRecovery.

B3-34unverifiablerecorded: fixedPlaceholders are resolved by sequential string replacement over text that already contains interpolated untrusted content: the rework prompt interpolates the owner's defect and the persisted request into the template, then runs injectOutputSchema and a second replaceAll over the whole string (rework.ts:485-496), so the substitution rescans data.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

A defect or original request that quotes the literal token {output_schema} gets the full schema block spliced into the quoted text, and a quoted {previous_envelope} is rewritten to the reference sentence. AWSF's own specs contain the literal (specs/awsf-plan.html, specs/awsf-v2-w05-design-to-plan-build-prompts.md), so a rework of AWSF work that quotes them is corrupted. Probe: the rendered handoff contains two schema blocks, the 'Concrete defect' line begins with schema text, and the request line reads 'keep SEE-REFERENCE rendering intact'. Simpler general change: one renderer that resolves every placeholder in a single pass over the template and never rescans inserted values, used by compileAgent, renderPrevious and reworkPrompt alike; equivalently, interpolate untrusted text only after placeholder resolution.

Historical classification: cleanup · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/contracts/json-schema.ts:79 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-34. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Resolve schema and explicit prompt tokens in one pass, and compose rework prompts before interpolating untrusted defect/request text.

Original problem and consequence

Commit 2a6197a made consequence a required key on awsf.review-output/v1 without changing the schema id, so reviews retained before it stay valid: true with no consequence. latestEnvelope returns them through an as-cast (run-report.ts:111-112), and the report line `Consequence: ${finding.consequence}` (run-report.ts:207) prints 'Consequence: undefined' for any legacy attempt whose report is regenerated. The same record fails the write-side parseEnvelope and would fail StoredEnvelopeSchema(ReviewOutputSchema), but no read path runs either check. Simpler general change: validate once in the evidence reader (readAttemptEvidence, review-record.ts:35) with StoredEnvelopeSchema(schemaForId(schemaId)) and mark mismatches invalid, so every consumer receives only payloads the current schema accepts instead of each caller casting.

B3-36unverifiablerecorded: fixedassertCandidateSeed re-implements the owner-amendment binding check by hand, comparing eleven named fields, instead of calling assertOwnerAmendmentBinding (owner-amendment.ts:98), which compares the whole binding against the expected activation.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

The hand-written comparison at lines 32-36 sees only the fields it names. If SeedOwnerAmendmentSchema gains a binding field that is not pinned by a literal (RescueOwnerAmendmentSchema already has such a field, reconnectGeneration, owner-amendment.ts:38), assertCandidateSeed accepts a seed whose amendment carries a different value for it, because nothing compares that field. assertOwnerAmendmentBinding compares the full binding by canonicalJson (owner-amendment.ts:100) and exists for exactly this check ('validate against the host's current activation, never against provider-supplied bindings'). It is called only from core/test/contract/recovery-amendment.test.ts and rework-amendment.test.ts, never from core/src. Cost: a second, hand-maintained copy of the binding rule that drifts from the schema. Latent today, because the schema pins every field the seed check omits. Remedy: build the expected seed binding (entry 'seed', anchorId, logicalTurnId and priorAmendmentDigest null, correctionRound 0, deliveryFrontier 'first-builder-input', plus the eleven named values) and call assertOwnerAmendmentBinding(value.ownerAmendment, expected).

Original problem and consequence

driver-preflight.ts:203-205 declares a local sha256 with the same body as owner-amendment.ts:56-58, and the file already imports canonicalJson from that module (line 4). The same body reappears as `digest` in decision-record.ts:141. shift-selection-record.ts:52, ticket-selection-record.ts:17, attribution-record.ts:83 and proving-ground.ts:121 inline createHash over canonicalJson instead of sha256(canonicalJson(...)). The pattern literals appear at 11 sites for 40-hex (candidate-seed.ts:6, closure-record.ts:5, command-ledger.ts:7, host-validation.ts:5, interrupted-turn.ts:7, owner-amendment.ts:45, phase-recovery.ts:8, plan-admission.ts:22, preview-record.ts:24, protected-grant.ts:6, visual-references.ts:89) and 16 sites for 64-hex (for example driver-preflight.ts:66, owner-amendment.ts:6, interrupted-turn.ts:6, visual-references.ts:35), plus the sha256: form at project-register-output.ts:50. guards.ts:20-24 states the policy directly: the 40-hex pattern is 'imported rather than restated', because one unguarded path field is one place the rule does not hold. Changing the object-id format would mean finding all 27 literals and the duplicated bodies. Latent: every copy agrees today. Remedy: call sha256, and move the pattern constants into contracts/typebox.ts, the shared module, rather than test-output.ts or review-context.ts.

B3-38unverifiablerecorded: wontfix no production caller makes this repeated checkpoint hashing a current hot pathassertTurnCheckpoint re-hashes the whole accumulated output.text on every call, and InterruptedTurnStore calls it on each write and again on the prior generation, so each checkpoint write re-verifies every earlier byte of the turn and the total cost grows with the square of the generation count. Latent: nothing in core/src constructs InterruptedTurnStore yet.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

Once the store is wired to persist a checkpoint per output chunk, InterruptedTurnStore.write() runs structuredClone of the whole checkpoint, then assertTurnCheckpoint on the clone (one SHA-256 pass over output.text), then this.read(previous): a read of the whole prior file, a JSON.parse, a second assertTurnCheckpoint (another SHA-256 pass over output.text) and a SHA-256 over the file bytes. That is about three full passes per generation. On this machine a 1.09 MB output costs 4.1 ms per SHA-256 pass, 3.0 ms for JSON.parse and 1.3 ms for structuredClone, about 17 ms per write at 1 MB before file I/O, and the sum over G writes of a growing output is quadratic in G. Cheaper alternative: keep the verified prior generation in memory after a write so the next write checks only the new bytes against its digest, and in read() skip the repeated output-digest pass, because read() already checks sha256(file) against the journal reference and write() validates before it persists. Severity low; no production cost today.

Historical classification: cleanup · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/contracts/interrupted-turn.ts:102 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-38. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

wontfix no production caller makes this repeated checkpoint hashing a current hot path: InterruptedTurnStore is defined in execution/continuity-store.ts and used only by its unit test; removing checks or caching mutable checkpoints would weaken the public checkpoint validator without a production use case.

B3-40unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe backward suffix salvage caps the number of attempts at 1,024 but not the characters those attempts parse, so one malformed reply of about 207 KB costs about 1,026 full-length JSON.parse calls over about 209 million characters before it is refused.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

A final message of about 207 KB holding 1,100 unclosed {"a": openers before a single closing brace makes extract() re-slice and re-parse the 200 KB body once per opener, because every suffix runs from its opener to the last closing brace and fails at end of input. Measured best-of-5 on this machine: 718.7 ms for that reply, against 3.6 ms for a same-length balanced control, 2.3 ms for a flat unclosed control and 0.9 ms for a 150 KB valid envelope. Lines 102-103 say the bound prevents unbounded salvage work; the bound limits the count, so worst-case CPU is about 1,024 times MAX_ENVELOPE_BYTES per reply, run synchronously on the event loop. Severity low: only pathological or adversarial output reaches it, and a realistic truncated 1,800-artifact reply takes 3 parses and 3.9 ms. Cheaper alternative: charge the length of each attempted suffix against a budget of about trimmed.length and stop when it runs out; the result is unchanged for every reply whose salvage succeeds within that budget.

Historical classification: cleanup · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/contracts/parse-envelope.ts:105 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-40. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Replace repeated suffix JSON parsing with one string-aware matching-brace scan and a single suffix parse, preserving recovery precedence.

B3-44unverifiablerecorded: wontfix avoiding repeat validation needs a new trusted/prevalidated APIassertProtectedConsumption and assertProtectedCandidateBinding each re-run the full assertProtectedGrant (a Value.Check over every file and parent plus a canonical-JSON digest of the whole grant) on every call, and the journal scan calls them once per consumption, intent and candidate record, so the same grant is re-validated once per record.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

readProtectedState (core/src/workflow/protected-grants.ts) validates each grant record once at line 51 and then again inside every consumption and binding check that names that grant, at lines 61, 73 and 98. Measured per call: 0.34-0.73 ms for a 3-file, 6-parent grant (4 KB of JSON); 1.4-2.1 ms for 16 files by 8 parents; 4.0-5.3 ms for 64 by 8 (73 KB); 250-430 ms at the schema maximum of 64 files by 256 parents (about 14 MB of JSON). readProtectedState is reached from several command paths (land.ts:195, 239, 279, 302; production-run.ts:1337, 2567, 4102, 4128; next.ts:50), and each reach repeats the scan. Severity low: at realistic grant sizes the redundant work is a few milliseconds per record. Cheaper alternative: validate each grant once per scan, which line 51 already does, and pass the validated grant to a binding check that does not validate it again; or memoize assertProtectedGrant per grant object in a WeakSet once the grant is frozen.

Historical classification: cleanup · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/contracts/protected-grant.ts:137 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-44. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

wontfix avoiding repeat validation needs a new trusted/prevalidated API: The exported consumption and candidate-binding assertions independently validate caller-provided grants; skipping that check would weaken their standalone contract, while measured ordinary-size overhead is low and no immutable validated-grant token exists.

B3-49unverifiablerecorded: fixedL11 authorizes the mandatory review spend on a bare gatesPass boolean, while the file's own rule (lines 88-93) says an edge that spends a call to preserve a green must check the gate rows; only L25 does, so the depth fix landed on one edge instead of on the shared green check.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

Both production L11 call sites send a literal gatesPass true and attest no gateEvidence (production-run.ts:3794, rework.ts:1386), so the edge authorizes a provider review with no row evidence. A caller that attests rows showing commands_pass failed for the same SHA is still ACCEPTED at L11, while L25 refuses the identical row. A later caller that computes gatesPass stale or wrong spends the T2 review on a red candidate and the guard does not notice. L20 (guards.ts:348), the human gate that precedes the fast-forward of canonical main, checks only the same boolean. Simpler general change: L11 and L20 call gateEvidenceViolations as L25 does, and the host attests gateEvidence when GATING exits, so every green-consuming edge reads one row-level check instead of a flag.

Historical classification: cleanup · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/state/guards.ts:211 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B3-49. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Require current-candidate passing host gate rows for L11 and L20; gather candidate_hygiene and commands_pass rows from journal evidence and wire them through production, rework, adoption, and landing authorization.

B4-01resolvedrecorded: fixedgatherLandingClosures decides whether an attempt landed from status.json (readAttempt) instead of from the journal that the removed code derived it from, so a status.json that lags the journal hides a landing and a missing or empty status.json rejects the closure inventory for the whole project.

Independent assessment

Closure inventory derives landed state from the journal and degrades an affected entry when the projection is missing, empty or stale.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/closure/readout.ts:46-134; follow-up 1a5ccea
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
A corrupt journal can still refuse the inventory. Projection recovery must never invent lifecycle history.

Original problem and consequence

Removed by 4c75b5c: the old loop read the attempt journal (closureJournalRecords), derived the status from its last record (deriveAttemptStatus), and only then applied the LANDED/PUBLISHED gate, so status.json never decided whether an attempt had landed. The journal is the truth (journal.ts header) and status.json is a projection written after the journal append (runWriteProtocol in attempt-lock.ts; withClosureJournal at closure-journal.ts:31-33), with no fsync before the rename (status-store.ts:15-17). (a) A crash between the attempt.transitioned append that records LANDED (land.ts:343) and its status write leaves status.json pre-landing: line 56 skips the attempt, so the landing is missing from the inventory, unclosedLandings (model.ts:34-36) and preflight's closure evidence (preflight.ts:349, 356, 416) report nothing open, and readClosure (readout.ts:34-35) answers 'not closed' while status.ts:237 still says closure is read from the journal. (b) A journal with no status.json (a crash between the first journal append and the first writeStatus; attempt creation is persistAttempt at new.ts:187), or an empty status.json after a power loss, makes readAttempt throw (attempt.ts:329-331; tryReadJson rethrows the JSON SyntaxError). Nothing catches that at line 55, so gatherLandingClosures rejects for every attempt in the project and every preflight for that project fails until the broken attempt directory is repaired by hand. The removed derivation tolerated both states.

Historical classification: bug · high · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/closure/readout.ts:55 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B4-01. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: closure inventory derives landed state from the journal; a missing, unreadable or lagging status.json or a torn tail degrades only its entry (LandingClosureFact.degraded)

B4-03partially resolved057370d recheck · Historical ledger: recorded: fixedA crash between the journal append and the status write leaves the journal one record ahead of status.json, and no production path reconciles it: the next persistAttempt appends a record whose source_seq differs from its event.next.revision, so the status and the journal disagree about the sequence.

Independent assessment

A journal-ahead check refuses a later write that would fork sequence and revision. This prevents additional corruption after a lost status write.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/persistence/attempt-lock.ts:241-288
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Refusal is not automatic reconciliation. Demonstrate operator recovery after append/status crash boundaries without manual evidence edits.

Original problem and consequence

A kill lands after the 'appended' step of revision 2: the journal holds source_seq 2 with next.revision 2, status.json still says revision 1, and attempt.lock is left naming a dead pid. Every retry then fails with EEXIST until a human deletes the lock (verified; doctor only reports it). After that manual delete, a retry reads status.json (readAttempt in attempt.ts:329 uses tryReadStatus), builds next.revision 2, and validate() passes because it compares only against status.json. Journal.append assigns source_seq 3 from the journal tail, so the journal gets 3/2; the next write gets 4/3 while status.json ends at lastSourceSeq 3. scanJournal accepts the file, so replay does not notice; the closure contiguity predicate (closure-journal.ts:15) refuses the attempt only at closure time. recoverAttempt (replay.ts:262), the designed repair that would reconcile this, has no production caller: it appears only in core/test/simulation/crash-injection.test.ts, and reclaimLock appears only in that same test. The stated guarantee (attempt-lock.ts:179-185: a reader can never observe the journal and status.json disagree) is breached with no detection on the write path.

Historical classification: bug · high · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/persistence/attempt-lock.ts:198 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B4-03. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: runWriteProtocol refuses (JournalAheadOfStatus) a write whose status the journal has passed, so a lost status write can no longer fork source_seq from revision

core/src/persistence/journal.ts:308-355

Original problem and consequence

Case A: the crash cut the last record mid-JSON. Journal.append throws SyntaxError from lastSourceSeq (journal.ts:123) on every later call, and the file is unchanged. The designed discard (recoverAttempt, replay.ts:276-284, which says the torn bytes stay in the file) has no production caller, so the attempt stays unwritable until someone edits the journal by hand. Case B: the crash kept the record's JSON but not its trailing newline. Journal.append then returns success with source_seq 4, but its bytes land on the same physical line as record 3, so an acknowledged write is unreadable: scanJournal refuses the file at line 3 ('line is not valid JSON'), and that refusal blocks every reader of the file. Case B needs a narrow crash point, but no code on the write path defends against it.

A power loss (or kernel crash) persists a record's closing brace but not its newline. lastSourceSeq returns that record's seq (journal.ts:123), so the next Journal.append writes `{record N+1}` plus newline directly after the unterminated bytes. Every appender is exposed: persistAttempt (attempt.ts:365), closure-journal.ts:28, project-closure-journal.ts:72, planning/store.ts:169, delegate-replays.ts:32, and the task-attributions, task-decisions, task-delegate and task-relations appenders. The file now has one line holding two JSON objects. scanJournalText (replay.ts:110) refuses it as 'line is not valid JSON' at line N, and every scanJournal reader refuses the journal from then on. replay.ts:96-98 treats that unterminated line as an unacknowledged tail, so the correct continuation is a new line or a refusal, never an append onto it. A torn partial line instead makes append throw SyntaxError and leaves the file unchanged, which is the loud case.

Historical classification: bug · high · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/persistence/journal.ts:123 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B4-05. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: an unterminated whole record is adopted and the next append starts on a new line, so both records stay parseable

Original problem and consequence

awsf relate requires an existing attempt (relate.ts:193 throws otherwise). The live path appends the declaration and calls projectRelation (relate.ts:209-210), which runs the UPDATE at projector.ts:232-233 against sessions that already exist, so attempt 1 receives T04. A later attempt 2 of the same task, for example a retry, is inserted by createSession with continuesTask taken from its own status (dashboard-projection.ts:62, then attempt-projection.ts:25), which is null unless --continues was passed. Nothing in new or retry reads the declaration: declaredContinuation is called only from operator.ts, preflight.ts, relate.ts and status.ts, and no later projection rewrites continues_task. The dashboard therefore shows NULL for attempt 2, while awsf status for attempt 2 (status.ts:233 feeds the declaration into formatRelation for every attempt) and the rebuilt database (operator.ts:51 layers the declaration onto every attempt projection) both show T04. The projectTaskRelation docstring (projector.ts:214 and 216-219) promises that every attempt of the task carries the edge, which the live path does not deliver. Probe e2-relation-live-vs-rebuild.mjs: live 's1/attempt 1 -> T04 | s2/attempt 2 -> null'; rebuild 's1/attempt 1 -> T04 | s2/attempt 2 -> T04'.

B4-18unverifiablerecorded: dup-of B4-01The reverse landing-tail reader refuses whenever status.json is behind the journal, and gatherLandingClosures gives it no per-attempt isolation, so one lagging attempt rejects the closure inventory for the whole project.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

The removed readout (4c75b5c) read the whole attempt journal, checked contiguity, and took the status from the journal's last record, so a status.json one revision behind was never an error for inventory readers. The replacement compares the journal tail with projection.revision (closure-tail.ts:23 and 28-29) and throws 'closure refuses a non-contiguous attempt journal or stale projection revision'. That throw propagates through readout.ts:59 (the readJournal call has no catch) and rejects gatherLandingClosures for the whole project. Trigger: a crash between journal.append and writeStatus in withClosureJournal (closure-journal.ts:31-33), for example during the closure-record write of awsf close, or during the LANDED to PUBLISHED write (task-machine.ts:122, the only edge out of LANDED). Every preflight for that project (preflight.ts:349, 356, 416) then fails for every task until the lagging attempt is re-closed, because withClosureJournal derives the status from the journal (closure-journal.ts:26) and rewrites status.json on its next append or reconcile (closure-journal.ts:33 and 42). The refusal itself is intentional for the per-attempt reader (bounded-readers.test.ts:81 asserts it), so the defect is the blast radius: one attempt's projection lag rejects the whole project's inventory.

Historical classification: bug · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/persistence/closure-tail.ts:28 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B4-18. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

dup-of B4-01: 722ad92 already supplies journal-derived status to the tail; new 4-case regression proves closure-record lag and publication lag preserve a healthy sibling, bytes and intentional stale/torn/corrupt refusals.
