Original problem and consequence

On a power loss after Journal.append resolved for the first record of an attempt, the directory entry for journal.jsonl (created at journal.ts:39 by open 'a', after mkdir at :38) may not have reached disk, so the journal file disappears while status.json, written by writeAtomic with a rename and no fsync (status-store.ts:15-17), may survive. Original problem and consequence

runWriteProtocol (attempt-lock.ts:200) treats the status write as the durable step after an fsynced journal append. On a filesystem that does not order data ahead of the rename (the repository lives on /mnt/d, which is DrvFS/NTFS), a power loss after the rename can leave status.json zero-length. readJson (status-store.ts:21) then throws a SyntaxError. tryReadJson rethrows it because only ENOENT maps to null (status-store.ts:28-29), readAttempt (attempt.ts:330) throws, and inspectPhaseRecovery (phase-recovery.ts:43) refuses the attempt, so recovery stops at the very file it exists to repair. Not probed: reproducing it needs a power-loss simulation, so this rests on code reading.

B4-25resolved057370d recheck · Historical ledger: recorded: fixedA sealed ticket blob is read as decoded UTF-8 text and re-encoded before the digest check, so a ticket whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 fails verification and its task classes silently disappear from the metrics.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A ticket saved with a non-UTF-8 byte (for example a Windows-1252 quotation mark) is sealed with the SHA-256 of its raw bytes. At metrics time systemGitRunner returns stdout decoded as utf8 (transport-broker.ts:248), so the invalid byte becomes U+FFFD and Buffer.from(..., 'utf8') produces different bytes. compile.ts:228 throws ShiftTicketDigestMismatch, readShiftTaskClasses (task-class.ts:61-63) catches it and returns an empty map, and every builder row in that shift is 'unclassified' with no notice. The run path has the same decode and re-encode (workflow/shift/bind.ts:54), so the run fails loudly, but with a 'changed since selection' message that names the wrong cause. Fix: read blobs as bytes rather than re-encoding decoded text.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/metrics/task-class.ts:37 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B4-25. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Sealed ticket blobs are read as the bytes Git stored (latin1 through runSystemCommand), so the digest check sees the sealed bytes; a non-UTF-8 ticket refuses as unreadable instead of a digest mismatch.

B4-26unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe catch blocks that run an explicit ROLLBACK and rethrow replace the original error when SQLite has already rolled the transaction back, so the journaled projection-failure notice and the rebuild refusal report 'cannot rollback - no transaction is active' instead of the cause.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

The state root fills during a projection. SQLite rolls the transaction back on its own (SQLITE_FULL), and the explicit ROLLBACK then throws. In projectAttemptStatus that error replaces the disk-full error in the inner catch (projector.ts:186-188), the outer catch copies it into notice.detail (projector.ts:207), and rebuildDatabase copies it into the refusal reason (rebuild.ts:318-319). The same pattern is at projector.ts:974-976 (projectEvent) and sqlite.ts:216-218 (runMigrations), so a migration that hits a full disk reports the ROLLBACK error. The owner sees the wrong cause, and the disk-full diagnosis is lost. Fix: run ROLLBACK in its own try and rethrow the original error when it fails.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/observability/projector.ts:187 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B4-26. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: rollbackAfterFailure helper at both projector ROLLBACKs and the migration ROLLBACK keeps the original disk-full cause.

Original problem and consequence

A migration added as 0008_x.sql, 8-x.sql or 0008.sql is dropped by the filter at :67 with no error, so the database stays at user_version 7 while its author expects the schema to have moved, and every later open still succeeds. B4-30unverifiablerecorded: fixedwithLock's finally awaits handle.close() before unlink(), so a rejected close skips the unlink and the close error replaces the error the callback threw.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost

Original problem and consequence

If close() rejects after the callback has already failed (for example validate or journal.append rejecting at attempt-lock.ts:196-198), the finally throws the close error at :131 and never reaches :132. The caller sees the close error instead of the real cause, and attempt.lock stays on disk naming a pid that has moved on, so the next withLock on that attempt fails with EEXIST until a human removes it. Close and unlink are independent teardown steps and should not share one try: the unlink belongs in its own finally.

A later attempt 2 is then created. Rebuild: rebuild.ts:337-339 projects decisions after every session exists, so the same record attaches to session 2. B4-34unverifiablerecorded: fixedrebuildDatabase sorts every journal's records by wall-clock recorded_at with a string tie-break on sessionId:source_seq, so one attempt's records can be applied out of sequence when two share a millisecond across a digit boundary (seq 9 and 10) or the clock steps back, and the rebuild then refuses.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Journal appends stamp recorded_at with new Date().toISOString() (journal.ts:166), so two appends in the same millisecond tie. The tie-break compares the strings 'sid:10' and 'sid:9', and '1' sorts before '9', so seq 10 is applied before seq 9. projectAttemptStatus requires sourceSeq === cursor + 1 (projector.ts:142) and returns ok false, so 'awsf db rebuild' (operator.ts:79) refuses a healthy journal with 'non-contiguous attempt projection: cursor 8, source_seq 10'. A backward wall-clock step between two appends (an NTP step or a VM clock correction) produces the same refusal. The defect is latent here: across the 195 attempt journals on this machine (240,243 records) no adjacent pair had equal or decreasing timestamps. Fix: a k-way merge across journals that always takes each journal's next record in seq order, instead of sorting records by wall clock.

Historical classification: bug · low · PLAUSIBLE. Original location: core/src/observability/rebuild.ts:288 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B4-34. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Rebuild replays each journal in its own source_seq order via a heap k-way merge.

Original problem and consequence

Two processes open a database that has a pending migration N at about the same time (for example the dashboard and a run). If the timeout were added as the A2-3 fix proposes, the loser would replay migration N's CREATE statements inside its own transaction and fail on the table that already exists, so the pending check has to be repeated inside the IMMEDIATE transaction.

Original problem and consequence

The rebuild calls closeDatabase(db) in its finally block and then retainAndSwap, which renames only candidatePath to targetPath (rebuild.ts:238) and leaves candidatePath-wal behind. If the checkpoint fails or is incomplete (an I/O or disk-full error during checkpoint, or a checkpoint held back by a reader), committed frames stay in the candidate's WAL, closeDatabase reports success, the swapped-in file lacks those frames, and rebuild returns ok:true with no check after the swap. The projection is disposable and rebuildable from the journals, so the damage is a wrong dashboard until the next rebuild. Verified: the swallow itself. With a reader holding an older snapshot, the explicit checkpoint returned busy 1 and closeDatabase returned normally with a 300 KB WAL left. Not reproduced: the row loss end to end. The swapped file then failed to open with disk I/O error because the reader still held the inode, and an I/O error could not be injected here.

Original problem and consequence

The problem section is the owner's request (land.ts:105, problem: status.request). A request containing a line '## Changes' (plan-derived requests often carry Markdown headings) makes the reader's first match for the Changes marker land inside the Problem text, so the Changes section shows the request's tail followed by the real changes, shifted one section. The dashboard reads the summary through api/routes.ts:449 and displays it with no error. Probe p5-landing-summary.mjs: a problem of 'Fix the parser.' followed by a '## Changes' line reads back as problem 'Fix the parser.' and changes 'rewrite the parser entirely', then '## Changes', then the real change text. Altitude fix: the structured LandingSummary already exists at write time (land.ts:114), so persist it as JSON and render the Markdown as a view, instead of parsing free text back out of a display format.

B4-47unverifiablerecorded: wontfix no declared mapping exists from provider-resolved IDs to route-selector familiesThe route-arm replay's observed identity is the launched route, so provider-mismatch and model-mismatch check the configuration the runner was given rather than what answered, and the resolved model that was projected never reaches the scorer.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

A replay on arm X whose provider answered with a different resolved model than X names, for example a silent fallback, still produces a valid pair, because the scorer never receives the answer. RouteArmReplay carries observed {provider, model} only, taken from the launched route, and has no resolved-model field (route-arm-score.ts:53-69). That pair is then counted in arm X's recall and first-pass intervals as if X had been measured, and the invalidation reasons can fire only when the launched route differs from the arm. Altitude fix: carry the answering provider and resolved model through RouteArmReplay, and map the resolved id to its selector family (armKey already strips the adapter prefix), so the invalidation reasons describe what answered. The author's stated reason, that a resolved id never equals a selector, is a reason to map the ids, not to stop observing them.

Recorded response and provenance

B4-48unverifiablerecorded: dup-of B4-34The rebuild re-sorts records across journals by recorded_at and breaks ties with a string on sessionId:seq, so two records of one attempt in the same millisecond can be projected out of order; projection then refuses a healthy journal, and that refusal blocks the rebuild which is the only exit from the degraded hold.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

journal.ts:166 stamps recorded_at with millisecond precision, so two consecutive appends to one attempt journal that complete within one millisecond share a timestamp. This needs an fsync under 1 ms, so the likelihood on a DrvFs mount is low, but the failure is deterministic once it happens. The comparator at rebuild.ts:289 compares the strings for seq 9 and seq 10 and sorts 10 first. projectAttemptStatus (projector.ts:142-146) then refuses with 'non-contiguous attempt projection: cursor 8, source_seq 10'. rebuildDatabase returns ok:false, the live awsf.db is untouched, and the session stays degraded because only a successful rebuild lifts the hold (rebuild.ts:10-12 and the DegradedObservabilityHold message at rebuild.ts:57-59). The CLI rebuild (operator.ts:25-79) uses the attemptStatus path, so the normalize path's silent skip is not reached from the CLI. Altitude fix: stop re-deriving cross-journal order from timestamps. Each journal is already in source_seq order, so merge journals by recorded_at while reading each one in order (a stable k-way merge), or compare seq numerically. Also count applied records per source rather than checking only the final cursor (rebuild.ts:353-364).

B4-52unverifiablerecorded: fixedprojectAttemptStatus calls createSession on every projected journal record, so each record re-runs the scrub of the full config snapshot and request text (JSON.parse, a scrub of every string leaf, JSON.stringify) even though the INSERT is a no-op once the sessions row exists.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

Every persisted provider event (text.delta is the bulk) and every attempt status write reaches projectAttemptStatus through dashboard-projection.ts:60, and line 136 runs createSession before the cursor check. createSession evaluates scrubJsonText(init.configSnapshotJson) (projector.ts:342) and scrubCredentialString(init.requestText) (projector.ts:338) before INSERT OR IGNORE, which does nothing once the row exists. Measured with the repo's 5,819-byte snapshot (210 string leaves) and a 4,680-byte request: createSession costs 2.8 ms per call and a projected record 2.5 to 3.5 ms, against 0.8 to 1.1 ms for a record with a tiny snapshot and request, so roughly 2.5 ms of pure re-scrub per record. The owner's projection holds 216,637 event rows across its twelve largest types, and awsf db rebuild replays each record through the same path (rebuild.ts:315), so a full rebuild spends on the order of 9 minutes re-scrubbing one unchanging snapshot (an estimate from the measured per-record cost). Each live streamed event also waits about 2.5 ms longer before the next one is persisted. Cheaper alternative: check for the sessions row first and call createSession only when it is absent, or cache the scrubbed snapshot per session_id.

Historical classification: cleanup · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/observability/projector.ts:136 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B4-52. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Check for the session row before createSession so later records avoid re-scrubbing immutable snapshot and request fields.

B4-55unverifiablerecorded: wontfix retaining the migration tokenizer avoids replacing SQL-aware splitting with a fragile line-regexA 60-line hand-written SQL tokenizer exists only to hoist three one-line PRAGMAs out of each migration transaction, and node:sqlite can run a whole migration body in one exec.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

splitStatements (lines 129-189) tracks quotes, bracket identifiers and two comment forms so that runMigrations (202-203) can route statements matching TRANSACTION_UNSAFE_PRAGMA (line 126) to a pre-transaction preamble. The only such statements in the seven migrations are journal_mode, synchronous and foreign_keys at lines 1-3 of 0001-initial.sql, and foreign_keys at line 1 of 0004-published-state.sql; no migration has a quote or comment containing a semicolon. Cost: the migration runner carries a tokenizer that no current migration exercises, and it is the hardest code in the file to review while it decides every schema change. Simpler form: take the preamble with a multiline, global, line-anchored match for the three PRAGMAs, and run the rest of the file as one db.exec inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Check equivalence by running runMigrations on both forms over the seven migrations before adopting.

wontfix retaining the migration tokenizer avoids replacing SQL-aware splitting with a fragile line-regex: Existing SQLite tests pin semicolons in comments/quoted strings and PRAGMAs behind comments; schema migration correctness outweighs removing this low-risk parser.

B4-58unverifiablerecorded: fixedEach persisted generic event is deep-copied and regex-scrubbed four times on the live path: Journal.append scrubs it into the record and then serializes the record with a second scrub, and applyEvent scrubs the event again and serializes it with a fourth scrub.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

Journal.append sets event: scrubCredentials(event) (journal.ts:167) and serializes the whole record with stringifyRedacted (journal.ts:169), which scrubs again. The projection then reads the same event through applyAttemptEvidence and applyEvent, which scrubs it (projector.ts:869) and serializes it with stringifyRedacted(event) (projector.ts:926), a fourth pass. Scrubbing is idempotent, so the stored bytes do not change. Measured at 38 to 44 microseconds per pass for a 120-character text.delta-shaped event, that is about 0.16 ms per persisted live event, and about 0.08 ms per record during a rebuild, which runs only the projector's two passes. It is the smallest cost listed here, but it is pure repetition. Cheaper alternative: scrub once at the boundary and serialize the already-scrubbed value with JSON.stringify, keeping one scrub so that credential-shaped values are still redacted before they reach the journal or the projection.

Historical classification: cleanup · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/persistence/journal.ts:167 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B4-58. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Scrub once at journal/projection boundaries, then JSON.stringify the already-scrubbed record/event.

B4-59unverifiablerecorded: wontfix flat light-tier intake has a distinct no-plan format and is not consumed by the shift compilerThe ticket frontmatter is split three times with different newline tolerance: the body reader and the invariant-12 fence accept LF only, while the plan-ticket listing and the light-tier store accept CRLF, so one CRLF ticket is listed and selectable but refused by the shift compiler and preflight.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence

Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost

Original problem and consequence

A ticket saved with CRLF line endings passes parsePlanTicketData (used by the listing, doctor and ticket selection; plan-tickets.ts:45 uses \r?\n) but fails parsePlanTicketBody (plan-ticket-body.ts:27 uses \n only), which the shift compiler (workflow/shift/compile.ts:159-162) and preflight (preflight/shift-tickets.ts:42) call. It throws E_PLAN_TICKET_NO_FRONTMATTER, and parsePlanTicketIdentity returns null. Selection therefore accepts a ticket the compile step cannot read, and the error names no line-ending cause. The fence (ticket-plan-sync.test.ts:103) also uses the LF-only pattern, so a committed CRLF ticket fails the meta-test, which bounds the practical reach to uncommitted files. The comment at plan-ticket-body.ts:9-15 says the split is defined once, but the code has three definitions. Altitude fix: one exported splitter used by the listing, the store, the compiler and the fence.

B4-62unverifiablerecorded: wontfix moving the snapshot out of each atomic status record changes recovery durabilityEvery persisted provider event rewrites the whole status.json, and that document embeds the full config snapshot text, so each rewrite re-scrubs the snapshot and writes about 13.5 KB, of which roughly 5 to 6 KB never changes during the attempt.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

production-run persists each persistable event through the attempt write protocol, and attempt-lock.ts:200 calls writeStatus on every write. writeStatus (status-store.ts:35) runs scrubCredentials over the whole status, including configSnapshotJson (an AttemptStatus field, attempt.ts:118), a single string of about 5 to 6 KB that is scrubbed by all nine credential patterns. writeAtomic then writes the full JSON to a temp file and renames it (status-store.ts:16-17). For the owner's newest attempt the status file is 13,527 bytes and the session has 1,693 text.delta rows, so the text deltas alone rewrite roughly 23 MB of status for that one attempt (1,693 rewrites at about 13.5 KB each). The scrub of the snapshot alone costs roughly 0.2 ms per rewrite, extrapolated from the measured 190 us for a 4.7 KB request string. Coalescing rewrites would break the recovery rule that tolerates exactly one record of staleness (replay.ts), so the cheaper alternative is to stop duplicating the constant snapshot into every status write: store it once per attempt or reference it by digest, after checking the status consumers.

Historical classification: cleanup · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/persistence/status-store.ts:35 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B4-62. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

wontfix moving the snapshot out of each atomic status record changes recovery durability: Status/journal records remain self-contained and one-record-stale recovery stays unchanged; no coalescing or status-store write change was made.

Original problem and consequence

A core/src module that runs execFile('git', ['push', '-f', remote, 'HEAD:main']), or passes the refspec '+HEAD:main' or ':main' (a remote branch delete), leaves the test 'no force/auto-delete paths in core/src' green. AGENTS.md invariant 8 says the force and auto-delete halves are unconditional absences that 'now also cover the argv-array spellings the previous scan never saw', naming a +-prefixed refspec source and an empty or all-zeros source. The three refspec patterns (lines 16, 18, 20) each require ':refs/' after the source, so short destinations pass. The -f pattern (line 25) needs push to appear after -f on the same line, so an argv that names push first passes. --delete is not listed at all. The deletion patterns (lines 27-29) cover only the sync fs calls, so 'await rm(worktreePath, { recursive: true, force: true })' and 'await unlink(lockPath)' pass. core/src already awaits unlink at execution/operation-lease.ts:72 and :83 and persistence/attempt-lock.ts:76 and :132. This fence cannot separate lock releases from a future async worktree or branch removal, so the async removal class gets no signal at all.

AGENTS.md invariant 5: "`core/src/state/**` imports nothing impure — no I/O, no clock, no `child_process`, no filesystem. Enforced by the state-purity fence meta-test." Edits that pass the fence: `import { performance } from "node:perf_hooks";` (clock), `import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";` (timer), `import { createInterface } from "node:readline";` (I/O), `import "node:fs";` (side-effect, no `from`), and `const fs = await import("node:fs");` (dynamic, no `from`). The http alternative needs a `/` or a quote right after it, so `node:http2` also passes. No clock module appears anywhere in the pattern, so the clock half of the invariant is unenforced. core/src/state imports only relative modules today, so the green result does not cover these spellings.

B5-44unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe orphan-set check skips every readdir entry that is not a real directory, and the ticket reader drops any file whose name fails the TICKET_FILE pattern, so a symlinked ticket set or a misnamed ticket file is never checked against its plan.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

AGENTS.md invariant 12: "A ticket set whose plan cannot be resolved is a hard failure, not a skip". Line 66 `if (!entry.isDirectory()) continue;` skips a symlink, since a Dirent for a symlink is not a directory, so a symlinked set pointing at an unregistered plan produces no failure. Line 99 `.filter((name) => TICKET_FILE.test(name))`, with the pattern at line 41, silently excludes names such as T5.md or T100.md, so their state, milestone and prompt are never compared to the plan. Neither case appears in the tracked tree today (no symlinks under specs or core/src; the only non-canonical file in a ticket set is README.md), so both are latent.

B5-45resolvedrecorded: fixedThe owner-act set is derived only from switch arms whose body contains the literal processOwnerTerminal(), so owner-terminal commands reached through an if-block, a helper, or another module (seed, retry --adopt-as, group apply) are missing from OWNER_ACTS and from the delegation guard.

Independent assessment

The shared owner-act vocabulary includes seed, group apply and retry --adopt-as. Fences follow terminal call sites rather than only switch-arm text.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
docs/driving/marimba/owner-acts.mts; core/test/unit/meta/owner-act-list-b5-05.test.ts
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Maintain a negative case whenever a new command spelling or shared helper is added. Text/AST fences are checks, not an independent security principal.

Original problem and consequence

Invariant 13 keeps owner acts out of Delegate reach, and this repo defines an owner act as a command that constructs an owner terminal (boundary-claims.test.ts:199). Three such commands escape the spelled derivation. seed is an if-block (main.ts:605) that gates at main.ts:615 with options.terminal ?? processOwnerTerminal(). retry --adopt-as calls adoptionTerminal(options.terminal) at main.ts:1111, and the helper that holds the literal sits at main.ts:231-232, outside the retry arm text. group apply reaches processOwnerTerminal() at group.ts:100 through groupCommand. None is in OWNER_ACTS (marimba-guard-rules.mts:25), and delegation-guard.sh:118 loops over the same fourteen verbs. So ownerActViolation returns null for the seed, retry --adopt-as and group apply spellings. The list exists, per marimba-guard-rules.mts:20-23, for a driving session with prompts off, where a PTY can answer the confirmation, and it does not cover these three. Line 281 then asserts that retry constructs no owner terminal, which locks the false claim into the suite. Altitude fix: route every owner-terminal construction through one dispatcher-level gate, and derive both the guard list and this test from that registry rather than from switch-arm text.

Historical classification: cleanup · high · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/test/unit/meta/boundary-claims.test.ts:211 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B5-45. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

B5-46resolvedrecorded: fixedThe push-token leg matches only a quoted push literal, so a push argv written as a template literal, inside one command string, or with the plumbing verb send-pack sits outside core/src/publish/argv.ts and passes all three publish legs.

Independent assessment

The fence covers additional literal/argv spellings and contextual any-typed authorization values. The original known bypass shapes have negative tests.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/test/unit/meta/publish-fence.test.ts
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
This remains a finite syntactic fence. The independent destructive-path fence is still red and needs an owner-approved policy resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Invariant 8: the push argv 'is constructed in core/src/publish/argv.ts and nowhere else.' The token regex needs a quote on both sides of push. Probe: [`push`, remote, spec] (template literal), ["-C", repo, "git push origin main"] (verb inside a longer string), and ["send-pack", remote, spec] (plumbing push) all PASS. The derivation leg (publish-fence.test.ts:99-122) inspects only object literals contextually typed as AuthorizedPublishPlan and as-casts, and a second argv site builds no plan, so the brand leg does not see it either. The file header names the locality leg as the backstop, and it is this regex that fails. Altitude fix: bind the authority at the spawn boundary, so remote-writing git verbs (push and send-pack) reach git only through the publish argv constructor, rather than matching one token spelling.

Invariant fences that assert deepEqual(offenders, []) over a walked root include child-process-fence.test.ts (line 11), state-purity-fence.test.ts (line 10), sqlite-write-fence.test.ts (line 16), no-destructive-paths.test.ts (line 36), no-shell-true.test.ts (lines 16-17), jev-transport-fence.test.ts (line 25) and the sweeps in no-credentials-in-fixtures.test.ts. Original problem and consequence

Invariant 13: 'Only core/src/decision/jev-transport.ts calls the Jev endpoint.' The file header (lines 1-5) says the fence keeps a second request builder from appearing through another door, and the regex does not see that door. Probe rows that PASS both legs: await global.fetch(url) (the leading [^.\w] excludes a dotted receiver, and only globalThis.fetch is spelled); const send = fetch; (no call paren); await globalThis["fetch"](url); and https.request with the path built as "/api/" + "alpha/decisions". A module added under core/src with any of these makes a second call to the endpoint with no fence failure. Altitude fix: fence the outbound request sinks rather than the URL, forbidding http(s) client calls and fetch aliases outside the transport and the API server, and keep the literal path only as a backstop.

B5-50unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe force and deletion scan matches spelled string forms only (a -f that must be followed by push on the same line, refspecs only when the destination starts with refs/, and a few exact commands), so argv-array force and delete spellings that invariant 8 names as covered slip through.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

Invariant 8 says no force or auto-delete path exists anywhere in core/src, and names the argv forms of a plus-prefixed refspec source and an empty refspec source as covered. These one-line specimens all pass the fence (probe-fences.mjs): ["push", "-f", remote, "HEAD:refs/heads/main"] (the -f rule needs a later push on the same line, so push-first order is missed); ["push", remote, "+HEAD:main"] (the refspec rules need a refs/ destination); ["push", remote, ":main"] (a remote branch deletion by short name); ["push", "--delete", remote, branch]; ["worktree", "remove", path] (the worktree rule needs whitespace, not a quote and comma); await rm(target, { recursive: true, force: true }) (only rmSync is listed); and ["branch", "-D", name]. A force push to main, or a remote deletion placed in core/src, passes. Altitude fix: stop enumerating string spellings; check the argv that reaches git at the single spawn boundary (transport-broker.ts) for force, delete, and plus or empty-source refspecs in any position, and define deletion by named API rather than by a Sync suffix.

fixed: Added TypeScript-AST detection for literal argv force/delete flags and destructive refspecs at Git/process call boundaries, independent of token order; regression fixtures cover the review forms while preserving every existing deny match and O2 lock allowlist entry.

B5-51unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe shell fence checks one option spelling, shell: true, while invariant 4 bans shell interpretation in any form: exec and execSync always run /bin/sh with no shell option, and shell also accepts a string path, so both pass.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

Invariant 4: 'No shell: true, anywhere. Executable + argv array only.' transport-broker.ts is the one file allowed to import node:child_process (child-process fence), and its import at line 21 is import { spawn, spawnSync, type ChildProcess } from node:child_process. Replace that import with exec and call exec(commandLine, done): the child-process fence allows it because the file is the allowed one, the shell fence finds no shell key, and the runtime refusal at transport-broker.ts:158 (shell !== false) runs only in assertSpecSafe on the spec path, while runSystemCommand hard-codes shell: false at line 250. Probe: execSync of printf %s "$0" prints /bin/sh, and spawnSync with shell set to /bin/sh runs under a shell too. The probe rows for a string shell path, a quoted key, a variable value, exec(string) and execSync(string) all PASS. Altitude fix: fence the import surface, allowing only spawn, spawnSync and ChildProcess from node:child_process, so no shell-capable API is reachable whatever the options; keep the runtime refusal.

fixed: Shell fence covers tracked code and driving docs and restricts the broker's child_process import surface to the approved spawn APIs and types.

B5-53unverifiablerecorded: fixedwalkFiles() calls statSync on every directory entry, although readdirSync with withFileTypes lists the same files without a stat per entry, and every meta-test that sweeps core/src pays that cost.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

On this mount a walkFiles() over core/src (402 entries, 339 matching files) takes about 2.0 s (2004 and 2182 ms in two orders; 2006 ms best of three), while a withFileTypes walk of the same files takes 0.16-0.23 s; core/src contains no symlinks, so the result sets are identical. The meta fences make 25 such statSync walks of core/src per run, core/test/unit/candidate-ref.test.ts:192 makes one more, and core/test/fixtures/trap-fence.ts adds an lstat walk (call sites in evidence), which is roughly 50 s of avoidable stat calls per run. Cheaper alternative: readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }) and call statSync only for entries where isSymbolicLink() is true, which keeps the symlink-following behaviour unchanged.

B5-55unverifiablerecorded: fixeddoc-reconciliation.test.ts imports two constant arrays from core/src/cli/main.ts, which loads the whole CLI module graph into its test process; cheatsheet-reconciliation.test.ts line 5 does the same.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

CLI_COMMANDS and CLI_BOOLEAN_FLAGS are literal values in main.ts (lines 72-80), but importing main.ts pulls in its 67 static import lines (most of them cli/commands modules, plus config, registry and persistence modules, and everything they load). Measured in fresh processes on this mount: importing main.ts takes 32.1, 31.3 and 30.2 s, against 0.07 s for registry/plan-source.ts. doc-reconciliation.test.ts uses nothing else from that graph, so about 30 s of each unit run is module loading for two arrays. cheatsheet-reconciliation.test.ts also loads config/load.ts (13.8 s) and state/task-machine.ts (9.2 s), so its saving is only the part of the CLI graph those imports do not reach, which was not timed. Cheaper alternative: move CLI_COMMANDS and CLI_BOOLEAN_FLAGS into a leaf module with no imports; main.ts imports and re-exports them (its USAGE string is built from the same array), and both fences import the leaf. The fences then check the same source of truth without loading the CLI.

fixed: Moved CLI command/boolean-flag tables to a dependency-free leaf, re-exported by main.ts and imported directly by documentation fences.

The program holds 678 files, 334 of them dependency declarations (@sinclair/typebox 232, typescript lib 61, yaml 41), so one unit run pays roughly 110 s of program construction for three fences that use an identical rootNames/options pair; two of the three builds could be avoided by hosting the checker-based checks in one test file. Original problem and consequence

Invariant 5: core/src/state/** imports nothing impure, with no I/O, no clock, no child_process and no filesystem. Probe rows that PASS line 7 with no import: export const stamp = () => Date.now(); new Date().toISOString(); performance.now(). Import rows that PASS: const fs = await import('node:fs') (no from), import ... from 'node:http2' (the alternation stops at http when it is followed by 2), node:timers/promises, node:perf_hooks, node:os and node:readline. Transitively, probe-state-closure.mjs finds 60 relative-import modules reachable from state/, with node:crypto reached via task-machine.ts, contracts/index.ts and shift-selection-record.ts. The fence reads only direct files, so a future fs import in any of those 60 modules passes. The crypto found is createHash (sha256) with no randomness source, and no clock or I/O call exists in the closure today, so this is a structural gap, not a live breach. Altitude fix: forbid the global clock and I/O identifiers in state/ by name, and check the relative-import closure of state/ against a module allowlist.

Original problem and consequence

agreementInput(set) (lines 138-146) runs again for each rule. On this mount one pass over the 411 ticket files takes 2.2-2.8 s (three passes: 2751, 2627 and 2233 ms), their frontmatter YAML another 0.2-0.5 s, and the 22 plan files (4.3 MB of HTML) are read again on every call. Thirteen rules therefore repeat identical reads and parses, and twelve of the thirteen passes (roughly 29-40 s per unit run) are avoidable. Cheaper alternative: memoize agreementInput per set.label in a module-level Map; each test file runs in its own process, so the cache lives for exactly one run and every rule still sees identical inputs.

B6-01resolvedrecorded: fixedThe saved-result snapshot caps the whole physical worktree at 64 MiB, and the node_modules copy that this repository's own config seeds into every worktree exceeds that cap, so each completed reply's result-ready checkpoint is silently skipped.

Independent assessment

Saved-result hashing excludes configured seeds with marker rows and records a skip reason. The seeded dependency tree no longer automatically exceeds the output snapshot cap.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/workflow/saved-phase-result.ts:14-85
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Checkpoint eligibility improved. Its trust in immutable seeds depends on H2, whose non-OS fallback remains weak. No current paid-reply reuse rate was measured.

Original problem and consequence

awsf.config.yaml:24 sets runtime.seed_paths to [node_modules], and git/worktrees.ts:193 copies it recursively into each new worktree. savedResultTreeDigest walks every file, including that copy, and throws ResultSnapshotUnavailable once cumulative file size passes 64 MiB; a worktree in this repo's .worktrees directory carries a 136,969,844-byte copy. production-run.ts:2910-2911 catches the error and returns from onResultStored without journaling the result-ready checkpoint, and nothing else reports it. Concrete cost: each valid reply in such a worktree spends about 90 s hashing on the /mnt/d mount (measured) and then leaves no pending reply in the journal, so recovery cannot reuse a paid reply. The commit-stage path (production-run.ts:2470 via validationProgressFor, guarded at 2932-2934 on that same pending checkpoint) never journals a commit intent either, so a crash around the host commit cannot be reconciled from the journal.

Historical classification: bug · high · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/workflow/saved-phase-result.ts:28 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B6-01. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: seed_paths excluded from savedResultTreeDigest (marker row per seed) and passed by every producer and recovery verifier; a result-ready snapshot skip now journals phase-result-unsaved with its reason (projector no-op) instead of returning silently

B6-02unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe shift readout rebuilds the recipe from the canonical checkout's working-tree bytes, so once the owner's landing commit flips a selected ticket's state, awsf status shows a completed shift as 'the recipe cannot be rebuilt' and hides its ticket rows.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

bind.ts:29 reads join(repository, ticket.path) from the canonical checkout, and bindShiftRecipe refuses any ticket whose bytes differ from the sealed digest (ShiftTicketDigestMismatch). The digest covers the whole ticket file, frontmatter state included (plan-ticket-body.ts comment), and AGENTS.md invariant 12 requires a ticket's state to be flipped in the same commit as the plan marker, which is the landing commit. After landing, shiftReadout catches the refusal at lines 189-190 and prints it in place of the ticket rows. bind.ts:35-37 states the design: a proof made after HEAD moves on must read the recorded base's blobs through bindShiftRecipeAt. shift-readout.ts does not use it; the only caller of bindShiftRecipeAt is candidate-seed.ts:147. The defect is a wrong binder choice, not state corruption, so the cost is a misleading status for every landed shift.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: shift readout binds the recipe at the recorded baseSha (bindShiftRecipeAt), so a landed shift keeps its ticket rows; no base (unstarted DRAFT) still reads the checkout

B6-03unverifiablerecorded: fixedOn the verify-candidate branch (reconcile-commands) reconcileHostValidation returns without identifying the durable commit, and verifyRecoveryWorktree skips its HEAD check, so a recovery accepts a worktree whose HEAD is not the durable commit and reports the pre-commit candidate.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A verify-candidate checkpoint records commitResult X as durable. HEAD later sits at C, one commit above X. A ledger verdict of resume makes planHostValidationRecovery return reconcile-commands; L204 returns {commit: null, candidateSha: inherited}, which is the prefix's candidate and not X. L233-237 skip the 'rev-parse HEAD equals worktreeHeadSha' check because reconciliation is non-null, so verifyRecoveryWorktree resolves. The probe accepted this (HEAD f7d7f6c2 against durable 387c5a4b, candidateSha null) and refused the same checkpoint when no ledger verdict was given. This misses the function's own contract (L173-174: every branch either identifies one exact outcome or throws) and the comment at L230-231 (a validating checkpoint answers the tree and HEAD questions against its recorded commit intent). It is mitigated on the live path: engine.ts L510-514 calls reconcileCommit before any re-dispatch, and production-run.ts adoptRestoredCommit (L2490-2498) runs reconcileHostCommit, which refuses a HEAD that moved past the commit. Every verifyRecoveryWorktree caller in production-run.ts (L1461, L3173, L3206, L3330, L3965) discards its return value, so the inherited candidateSha is unused today. The severity is therefore a verifier-layer contract gap. Fix: bind HEAD and the candidate to progress.commitResult on this branch and return that commit as candidateSha.

Historical classification: bug · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/workflow/phase-recovery.ts:204 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B6-03. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

B6-05unresolved057370d recheck · Historical ledger: recorded: fixedThe preserved-bytes check derives each file's Git mode from stat permission bits, but DrvFs (/mnt) mounts report 0777 for every inode, so every bound protected file on a /mnt-backed worktree compares as 100755 against Git's 100644 and is refused.

Independent assessment

The cited fix/test concern early engine failure, not mode bits. The preserved-byte check still maps filesystem execute bits directly to Git mode.

Verification strength
inspection only
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/workflow/protected-grants.ts:211-219; ledger/T4W1-B6-workflow.md:2
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
A /mnt source stat returned 777 on this host. The repository discourages DrvFs execution, which reduces supported-path impact. Prove the intended filesystem case or explicitly record that accepted limitation.

Original problem and consequence

A protected grant whose worktree sits on a DrvFs mount: when `awsf land` runs, land.ts:198, :305 and :323 call assertProtectedPreservedBytes with no exemption for files the land-time phase did not write, so line 216 maps the untouched 100644 file to 100755 and the land fails with 'later phase changed protected bound bytes' although no byte changed. Protected work on such a worktree cannot land. protected-files.ts:113 uses the same stat-bit mapping, so creating a new protected file on DrvFs is refused as an executable-mode change. defaultWorktreeRoot (platform-paths.ts:61-63) puts default worktrees on the Linux filesystem, so the defect fires only when the worktree root is on /mnt, via --worktree-root or AWSF_WORKTREE_ROOT (main.ts:423); the owner's memory records real /mnt/d worktrees that refuse permission-bit checks. Fix: take the mode from the candidate's Git tree delta (delta.afterMode) and compare blobs, never derive a mode from stat bits.

B6-07unverifiablerecorded: fixedA non-fatal TextDecoder silently replaces invalid UTF-8 in ticket bytes. The raw-byte digest check still passes, so a non-UTF-8 ticket compiles with U+FFFD in its brief on the first run, while the sealed-shift rebuild (bindShiftRecipeAt) re-encodes Git's lossy stdout and refuses the same ticket by digest.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A ticket saved in a non-UTF-8 encoding (for example Windows-1252 accents): bindShiftRecipe (production-run.ts:326, start.ts:262, preflight.ts:129) hashes the raw bytes with ticketFileDigest (sha256 over bytes), which matches the manifest, and the builder's brief carries U+FFFD in place of each accented letter. When that shift is later adopted or used as a seed, completedShift (candidate-seed.ts:147) calls bindShiftRecipeAt, which rebuilds the ticket from the utf8-decoded git stdout (transport-broker.ts:248), re-encodes it (shift/bind.ts:54), and fails ShiftTicketDigestMismatch. The same bytes run in one path and cannot be recovered or adopted in the other. The comment at bind.ts:38-40 says such tickets are refused by digest, which only the second path does. Fix: decode with { fatal: true } here so the first run refuses the same bytes.

B6-08unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe PNG decoder inflates the entire IDAT stream with no output bound and checks the declared size only afterwards, so a 4 MiB file can force a multi-gigabyte allocation before the refusal.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

pngFacts calls inflateSync(Buffer.concat(data)) with no maxOutputLength (line 62) and compares pixels.length to the IHDR-derived size only at lines 66-68. Input is capped at 4 MiB (contracts/visual-references.ts:25, enforced in readContained, which reads the whole file). DEFLATE expands that about 1028:1, as measured on zeros, to several GiB for a file at the cap, on a WSL instance the owner's hardware notes put at 4 GB. The allocation happens before the refusal. Passing the IHDR-derived expected length (plus one) as maxOutputLength would bound it to what the header allows. The input comes from the owner's own reference library, so the likelihood is low and the impact is an out-of-memory crash of the start command.

B6-10unverifiablerecorded: fixedAfter a red candidate verification, a correction round that commits nothing is accepted without verifying HEAD, and the accepted result returns the superseded failing verification.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Round 0 commits sha-1 and verifyCandidate returns passed=false (line 529), so the phase corrects. Round 1 changes no files, so hostGit.commit returns null (line 516); the guard at line 523 (candidateSha === null) takes the accept branch and breaks at line 526 with HEAD still the red sha-1 and nothing re-verified. The variable verification is declared once (line 463) and assigned only at line 529, never reset, so line 579 returns round 0's passed=false result as the accepted phase's verification next to candidateSha null. The AgentPhaseResult doc (engine.ts lines 204-210) says the verification is the one that passed. Current production limits the damage: verifyCandidate is passed only for builder phases (production-run.ts:2616), and the runner's onAccepted runs headAdvanced for them (production-run.ts:2948), which throws PhaseGateFailure with 'host commit exists: no host commit'. The owner therefore sees a misleading failure reason instead of 'candidate stayed red', and no production code reads result.verification. Fix: reset verification at the start of each round, and when a round yields no commit after a red verification, throw PhaseGateFailure with that verification's reports instead of accepting.

B6-11unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe read-only git runners forward the whole inherited environment, so an exported GIT_DIR (or GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_COMMON_DIR) makes 'git -C <worktree>' read a different repository, and the protected-path clean check and baselines then describe the wrong tree.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

The host process starts with GIT_DIR=<other>/.git exported (for example from a wrapper or a git hook). protectedReadOnlyGit(worktree) runs 'git -C <worktree> status', 'ls-tree' and 'rev-parse' against <other>, because git honours GIT_DIR over -C. prepareProtectedConsumption and verifyConsumedProtectedGrant call assertClean(..., protectedReadOnlyGit(worktree)) at protected-grants.ts L119 and L132: if <other> is clean while the protected worktree is dirty, assertClean passes and a dirty pre-write tree is accepted. captureProtectedBaselines (protected-grants.ts L121 and L133) reads baselines from <other> and either refuses or binds the wrong blobs. The same pass-through is in phase-recovery.ts L18-21 (readOnlyGit) and in git/changes.ts L14-17 (systemGitRunner), which is outside this batch. The trigger requires the variable to be exported, so it is conditional, and an owner's ordinary terminal lacks it. Fix: one filter that strips GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE and GIT_COMMON_DIR before spawning read-only git.

B6-13unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe review diff is captured with plain `git diff` through systemGitRunner, which forwards the whole process environment and pins no --no-color, --no-ext-diff or --no-textconv. The text the reviewer is judged against therefore depends on the owner's git configuration, while protected reads (protected-files.ts:9) pin those flags.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

With color.ui=always in the owner's git config (or a difftastic-style diff.external), the captured whole diff contains ANSI escapes or no unified output. The hunk test at line 196 (fullDiffHasHunks, /^@@ /mu) becomes false, the fitness gate (gates/review.ts:304, hunks > 0 || (delivered && expected.fullDiffHasHunks === true)) fails, and composeReviewEvidence throws ReviewEvidenceUnfit before any provider call, on every candidate. The failure is loud, but personal git settings the review code never asked for cause it. Fix: pass --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv to each review diff call, as protectedReadOnlyGit already does; line 72 already pins the stat width for the same reason.

fixed: composeReviewEvidence and candidatePathsBetween isolate git diff with --no-color, --no-ext-diff, and --no-textconv flags.

B6-19unverifiablerecorded: fixedUsageAccumulator drops null (unknown) cost turns from the sum and returns the partial total as if it were complete, which contradicts the AgentTurn contract that null is unknown, never zero.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Sends with costs 0.5, null, 0.25: line 306 skips the null turn and snapshot() (line 313) reports costUsd 0.75 over 3 sends, indistinguishable from a complete total. A reader of AgentPhaseResult.usage.costUsd, or of the initialUsage that production-run.ts:2902 rebuilds from originalUsage (production-run.ts lines 2313-2316), takes 0.75 as the phase cost and understates spend whenever a provider omits cost. B6-20unverifiablerecorded: not-reproduced already fixed by f340c76 (try wraps the setup checks)runAgentPhase constructs its PhaseExecution, which emits QUEUED to onPhaseState, before its try block, so the identity and usage refusals at lines 357 and 367-368 exit with QUEUED as the last observed state and never emit FAILED, breaking the documented FAILED-on-every-abnormal-exit contract.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Current mechanism evidence

Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A caller passes an initialEnvelope whose phaseId or schemaId does not match the phase (or omits initialUsage). runAgentPhase throws at 367-368 after the observer has recorded QUEUED, and no FAILED is ever emitted, so a durable phase record stays QUEUED for a phase that aborted. Production cannot reach this today: inspectPhaseRecovery (phase-recovery.ts:121) refuses a mismatched pending envelope, and production always passes initialUsage with initialEnvelope (production-run.ts:2902), so the gap is latent. Fix: move the setup checks inside the try, or emit FAILED from the pre-try branch.

Once an adapter supplies persistAgentSession, a write failure after onAccepted rejects runAgentPhase for a phase whose acceptance is already journalled. B6-22unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe correction launch verifier never checks that the round it authorizes was charged: it accepts a correction with zero charged corrections and accepts the same round again, although its comment and the adapter contract say the tranche must be the one the phase machine charged.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Registration {correctionRound: 1, tranche: 'auto'} on a phase whose conversation has one completed turn, with corrections.used.auto = 0 and allowance.auto = 1: the L237 test is false (0 > 1), the L241 test is false (1 > 1), so verify returns correction evidence with no charge. Registering the same round again with unchanged counters is accepted too. Nothing downstream checks the charge: transport-broker.ts #assertPhaseCorrectionLaunch checks only round >= 1 and a spent origin reservation. Today the caller's ordering protects it: engine.ts L398-406 charges VALIDATING to CORRECTING before the correction send at L425, and correctionStateFor reads the live post-charge counters (production-run.ts L1892-1900), so this is latent. But the verifier's stated job ('This is what replaces the ceiling') is not done: an uncharged correction launch is an unbounded same-session turn that costs tokens and reserves no call. Fix: bind each correction launch to one unconsumed charge recorded for that round and tranche, not to an upper bound on the counters.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/workflow/phase-launch-authorization.ts:235 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B6-22. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Correction launch needs its tranche charged and every round up to it charged; same-round re-registration with unchanged counters still accepted.

Original problem and consequence

The engine reaches verify-candidate only after candidateSha is non-null (engine.ts:523-528), so this phase's commit exists and is recorded in progress.commitResult. Line 204 returns candidateSha: inherited, where inherited (line 185) is checkpoint.prefix.at(-1)?.candidateSha ?? null: the previous accepted phase's candidate, or null for the first phase. The function's own doc (lines 161-162) defines candidateSha as the revision the phase would accept. Line 194 has the same mistake for reconcile-protected. Every current caller discards the value (production-run.ts:1461, 3173, 3206, 3330 and 3965 each call verifyRecoveryWorktree as a bare statement), so nothing acts on it today; a future caller that adopted this candidate would accept the wrong revision. Latent, low severity.

B6-28unverifiablerecorded: fixedEight shipped recipe modules call loadUserPrompt while their object literals are evaluated, so importing the workflow catalog reads prompt files on every load, and production replaces those same prompts with the config-path text before compiling, leaving the import-time read dead.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Any command whose import graph reaches catalog.ts performs 15 readFileSync calls for eight prompt files at module load. If one file is missing or unreadable (for example, a partial checkout or a renamed role file), module evaluation throws ENOENT and every such command fails before it starts. Meanwhile production-run.ts:1388-1392 builds configuredRecipe with each agent phase's prompt replaced by routePrompts userPrompt, so the imported text never reaches a provider. The recipe-support.ts:15 comment 'Recipes stay declarative' is contradicted by this import-time I/O, and the prompt now has two sources of truth. Fix: make the prompt lazy, or drop the field from the shipped recipes so the config is the only source.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/workflow/recipes/build.ts:31 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B6-28. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: The 15 shipped recipe prompts are lazy accessors, so importing the catalog reads no prompt file.

B6-29unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe plan-context recipe gate passes planContext.identifierSet as both the stored-design side and the plan-context side of architectureReviewClear, so its 'carried identifier set equals design' check compares a value with itself and cannot fail.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

The declared gate reports the identifier-spine check as passed for any identifier set, including one the host composed from a different design. Production does not run this declaration: composeProductionPlanContext (production-run.ts L707-718) calls architectureReviewClear(review, {design, planContext: identifierSet}) with the real design, and the plan-context branch (production-run.ts L3576-3582) persists that report and never runs the recipe's gate list, so there is no live bypass today. The defect is in the declaration. The recipe cannot reach the stored design, because the gate context carries only previousEnvelope, which for plan-context is the architecture-review output (phase.ts L8-18), so the author substituted the same object for both arguments. A future generic run of this gate would pass the spine check silently. Fix: carry the design identifiers into the gate context, or drop the identifier arm from this declaration and state that production enforces it.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/workflow/recipes/design-to-plan.ts:105 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B6-29. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Plan-context recipe gate refuses with a named check instead of comparing the plan context's identifiers with itself.

Original problem and consequence

A candidate whose only change adds a binary asset (git numstat reports a dash for both counts), or any candidate mixing binaries with text, is composed with insertions and deletions that omit the binary entries, so the review context summary reads '1 file(s), +0/-0' for a real change. The reviewer still sees the file in changedFiles and the stat, but the context's insertions, deletions and summary understate the change and contradict the code's own stated intent. Fix: skip or flag non-numeric entries rather than coercing them with '|| 0'.

B6-32unverifiablerecorded: fixedjpegFacts reads the frame height and width at offsets 5 and 7 of the SOF segment without checking the segment's payload length, so a truncated frame header throws a RangeError that escapes the decoder's ImageDecodeFailure contract.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Line 83 checks only the segment's total length against the file size. A file whose SOF segment has length 2 and still ends in the EOI marker passes the EOI check at line 76, then readUInt16BE(offset + 7) at line 86 throws RangeError. verifyVisualReferences rethrows anything that is not an ImageDecodeFailure (visual-references.ts:268-271), so the owner sees a raw RangeError instead of a visual-references refusal code. The image is still refused, so the impact is a wrong diagnostic and a broken error contract, not a bypass.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/workflow/visual-image.ts:85 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B6-32. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: A JPEG frame segment shorter than 8 bytes is an ImageDecodeFailure, not a RangeError.

B6-33unverifiablerecorded: dup-of B6-32The JPEG frame-header read takes dimensions at offset+5 and offset+7 without checking the segment length, so a short SOF segment is either read past the buffer end (RangeError) or accepted with dimensions taken from bytes after the segment.
