Original problem and consequence

A JPEG whose SOF0 segment has length 2 and sits just before EOI (FF C0 00 02 FF D9): readUInt16BE(offset + 7) throws RangeError ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE. visual-references.ts:270-271 converts only ImageDecodeFailure, so the RangeError escapes verifyVisualReferences as an untyped crash instead of an image-corrupt refusal. A length-2 SOF with 4 more bytes before EOI is accepted as 30975x13398, dimensions taken from outside the segment, which defeats the module's own promise that a reference that does not decode is not a reference. Fix: require length >= 8 for frame markers, read only inside offset + 2 + length, and convert any RangeError into ImageDecodeFailure.

B6-36unverifiablerecorded: wontfix full journal validation is required before recovery decisions; no safe incremental invalidation modelreadCommandLedger parses the whole journal and re-reads and SHA-256s every retained command output in the attempt on each call, but its only consumer, planCommandRecovery, reads the observation of the single intent the current expectation names.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

Each call runs once per candidate measurement: measureCandidate (production-run.ts:2021) is reached from :3675 for every code phase without a retained measurement and from :2618 for every verify-candidate round. A shift of T tickets therefore pays T full journal scans, and each scan also hashes every output accumulated by earlier tickets, so total work grows as O(T squared). Measured: scanJournalText took 1,436 ms for a 52,432,710-byte synthetic journal (probe-journal.mjs). The owner's shift journal at ~/.local/state/awsf/projects/agentic-workflow-software-factory/tasks/v3-w02-m4m5-shift/1/journal.jsonl is 332,371,127 bytes (stat only); linear extrapolation gives about 9 s per call before any output is hashed. Cheaper: pass the one needed intent (or a lazy observer) into planCommandRecovery instead of observing every result eagerly, and keep the verified ledger incrementally from the last verified offset of the append-only journal rather than re-reading it per measurement.

Original problem and consequence

The call is readFileSync of the entire journal, then a full parse and per-record checks, all on the event loop. It runs at production-run.ts:1337 (once per executeProductionCommand) and at next.ts:50 (each awsf next that lists grants). The whole-file utf8 read also has a hard ceiling: buffer.constants.MAX_STRING_LENGTH is 536,870,888 characters on this Node, so once a journal crosses it the read throws, and the largest journal is already 332 MB. recordedVisualBound (visual-references.ts:499-514, reached from refuseUndeliveredVisualPhases at :521-522 on review and rework commands) is a second whole-journal read on those commands. Cheaper: verify the append-only journal incrementally from a cached offset so each command reads only the records appended since its last verification, and keep the full validation on the paths that authorize a protected write.

B6-38unverifiablerecorded: not-reproduced already fixed by seed-path exclusionsavedResultTreeDigest reads the content of each file in the complete worktree, including the gitignored seed_paths copy, and refuses only after about 64 MiB has been read, so each digest of a seeded worktree pays the full read and then discards it.

Independent assessment

Verification strength

Current mechanism evidence

Original problem and consequence

This repo seeds node_modules (awsf.config.yaml:24 seed_paths: [node_modules]; the seed is a recursive cp in core/src/git/worktrees.ts), so each worktree carries 147,151,379 bytes in 6,043 files. The digest runs per agent phase at production-run.ts:2470 and :2477 (commit intent and commit result; runAgent at :2302 has no try around them) and at :2910 (saved reply, which catches the refusal and returns). Measured on the canonical node_modules: the digest threw 'saved-result tree exceeds 64 MiB' after 82,355 ms, a serial lstat walk of the same tree took 120,324 ms, and a concurrent lstat walk took 15,956 ms. The size decision needs only lstat sizes, so a concurrent pre-pass would refuse this tree in about 16 s without reading any content, and content hashing would run only for trees under the cap. Scope note: the digest is the only check that sees ignored files (captureChangeSet uses git diff HEAD --numstat at core/src/git/changes.ts:54 and ls-files --others --exclude-standard at :64, and neither lists ignored paths), so dropping seed_paths from the digest is an integrity decision for the owner, not a silent optimization.

A workflow whose builder uses a non-BUILD schema, or whose host-committed seed must be reviewed in seeded mode, is refused at compile with InvalidReviewBuildProducerCount until another literal is added to compiler.ts. Seeded mode is also decided by id (compiler.ts:218, consumed by production-run.ts:1406), so the compiler and the runner must change in step. The rule's own comment concedes it holds only by naming ('This cannot make the author schema a build producer in any other workflow', compiler.ts:174-175). The refusal is loud, so the cost is coupling and maintenance rather than a wrong review. Simpler general change: a phase declares its candidate role (for example a flag on the agent or host phase definition), reviewBuildPhaseIds counts declared producers, and seededReviewProducer reads the declaration, so neither the workflow id nor the schema pair appears in the rule.

B6-55unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe pi image-delivery preflight reads pi's settings from the host HOME, although the adapter gives the child a confinement-dependent HOME, so a phase can be refused over a setting the child never reads, and the same fact is answered twice (supportsImages in the adapter and this file check in the workflow layer).

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

The owner has images.blockImages set to true in ~/.pi/agent/settings.json and starts an attempt with --visual-references on a pi route under worktree confinement. The adapter documents that under worktree confinement the child's home is a fresh tmpfs with only auth.json bound (pi-codex.ts:522-525; providerWritableRoots at :529-532 binds only auth.json in that mode), so pi never reads that file and would deliver the images. assertRouteDeliversImages still reads it through HOST.process.env.HOME (production-run.ts:2385, and :1506) and throws route-images-blocked, so a phase that could run is refused. Two answers to one fact now disagree: supportsImages (pi-codex.ts:507) says the route takes images, and the workflow gate says it does not. Simpler general fix: the pi adapter computes the blockImages answer against the same home it passes to the child and folds it into supportsImages, so assertVisualRoute reads one answer and the workflow layer carries no pi file layout. This is fail-closed over-refusal rather than a leak. I checked that PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR cannot reach the child (adapters/env.ts ENV_ALLOWLIST is PATH, HOME, TMPDIR), but the worktree-confinement behaviour rests on the adapter's own comment and I did not run it.

B6-58unverifiablerecorded: wontfix persisted candidate_hygiene evidence does not carry dispatcherId; changing inference needs a durable evidence-contract migration, not a cleanup-only editdispatchPointFor recovers each command dispatcher's identity from phase-name string patterns and silently maps every unrecognized phase to production-run/measure-candidate, so the closed COMMAND_DISPATCHERS set the contract documents is not enforced.

Independent assessment

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only

Original problem and consequence

A fourth dispatch site, or a rename of the adoption or rework phase, is recorded as a production-run measurement and nothing fails. COMMAND_DISPATCHERS is only a type union with no exhaustive switch over it, so a forgotten update to this mapping compiles and runs. For the real dispatcher, ledgerGovernanceFailure finds no dispatch point (reached is false, so it returns null), and planCommandRecovery treats an occurrence with a passing hygiene record but no opening and no intent as never run, returning dispatch and re-running argv that may already have had an effect. The literal 'adoption-tests' is kept in four places (adopt.ts:798, adopt.ts:910, candidate-seed.ts:318, command-ledger-store.ts:31) and 'owner-rework-' in three (rework.ts:812, command-ledger-store.ts:34, metrics/role-rows.ts:398), so reader and writers agree only by convention. Simpler general fix: each dispatcher writes its own dispatcherId and occurrenceKey onto its candidate_hygiene evidence (the keys are computed at production-run.ts:2062, adopt.ts:868 and rework.ts:1117), readCommandLedger reads those fields, and dispatchPointFor with its default branch is deleted, so an unknown record fails loudly.

core/src/cli/commands/production-run.ts:933-973
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The reported static symlink escape is covered. This is not a complete hostile-filesystem race proof.

Original problem and consequence

A builder creates worktree/artifacts/report.json as a symlink to a host file outside the repository and declares that path in its envelope. The lexical check at line 880 passes, statSync (882) and readFileSync (884) follow the link, and artifacts_exist reports 'exists; size=N bytes' for the host file while json_parses reports 'parses; top-level type=object' when it is JSON. For a non-JSON host file the failing note is 'invalid or unreadable JSON' while an absent path gives 'missing', so the note discloses whether the file exists. corrections.ts:154-163 copies the notes of every check of a failed gate into the correction request, and the failing ones into violations, so these facts can reach the provider; the journal records them as well. A symlink named *.json that points at a multi-gigabyte file is read whole and synchronously before any size check, which blocks the host event loop. A plain ../ path is still refused, so the escape works only through links. The impact is metadata disclosure and a host-side read; file content is only parsed, never stored.

Concrete: AWSF is launched from an environment that exports GIT_COMMITTER_NAME and GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL (for example a driving session's identity). git/changes.ts:14-17 copies all of process.env into every git call, so the commit inherits those variables, and the -c values in git/commit.ts:16-17 lose to them. Probe: the author is still Santiago Marin (--author holds) but the committer becomes the ambient identity. An uninterrupted run never re-checks the committer: reconcileHostCommit runs only when a durable validation checkpoint is restored (production-run.ts:2940 and 2498, phase-recovery.ts:205 and 233); the identity checks in cli/commands/review.ts:322-323, workflow/candidate-seed.ts:365-366 and cli/commands/adopt.ts:330-333 run only on owner or preflight paths, and land.ts and publish.ts check no identity. The agent-named committer therefore reaches AWAITING_OWNER and can be fast-forwarded to main. The protected-commit and closure paths already pin identity through the environment, so the inconsistency sits in commitAsHost. The no-agent-coauthor meta-test scans history only after the fact and matches only five tokens (claude, gpt, codex, copilot, gemini, chatgpt, plus @anthropic.com and @openai.com), so a committer named otherwise passes it.

B7-09resolvedrecorded: fixedonPhaseState chains each phase-state write onto phaseQueue with .then, and no rejection handler is attached until a later await. A failed state write therefore becomes an unhandled rejection that terminates the process instead of reaching the BLOCKED path.

Independent assessment

Cancellation rejections and phase-write failures are captured for the durable stop path. The inspected follow-up retains late cancellation evidence.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/cli/commands/production-run.ts; follow-up 1a5ccea
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The earlier closeout reported a timing-sensitive cancellation failure. The fresh full-suite result, not its isolated historical pass, determines present gate health.

Original problem and consequence

The engine calls execution.validating() (engine.ts:457), which runs onPhaseState and queues persistPhase(VALIDATING) on phaseQueue (2579-2581). It then awaits store() file I/O (engine.ts:466) before onResultStored, whose 'await phaseQueue' at 2905 is the first handler. If that persist rejects during the I/O, for example on a failed journal or status write (the revision check at attempt.ts:376, or a projector error that runWriteProtocol awaits at attempt-lock.ts:203), the chained promise rejects with no handler. Node 22 in default mode raises it as an uncaught exception and the awsf process exits. The catch at 3870 never runs, so no BLOCKED record is journaled and the attempt stays RUNNING. Every phase state goes through this same chain (RUNNING, VALIDATING, CORRECTING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED).

B7-19unverifiablerecorded: fixedAn empty --state-root value, and an empty --worktree-root or AWSF_WORKTREE_ROOT, resolves to the process working directory, so attempt state or worktrees are created inside the repository instead of the state home.

Original problem and consequence

parseArgs accepts an empty value because the only value check (line 160) rejects undefined and '--'-prefixed tokens, so '' is stored. resolve('') returns process.cwd(), which is the repository root under `npm run awsf`. `awsf metrics --state-root ''` therefore looks for, and for write commands creates, awsf.db and the journals in the repository root, a location .gitignore does not cover, instead of the XDG state home. The same empty value reaches the worktree arms (lines 423, 596, 794, 817, 1110) because the ?? chain does not fall back on an empty string: `awsf start T1 --worktree-root ''`, or an exported empty AWSF_WORKTREE_ROOT, hands startCommand the repository root (start.ts:192 and 339 call resolve on it). Nothing refuses it: createWorktree's only root check is isAbsolute (core/src/git/worktrees.ts:258), so the attempt worktree is created inside the working tree, against the start.ts:55 precondition 'Outside both the repository and state root'.

fixed: --state-root and --worktree-root reject empty strings; empty AWSF_WORKTREE_ROOT falls back to default to prevent repository root pollution.

B7-23unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe direct-run guard compares argv[1] with import.meta.url, so when the entry is reached through a symlink (npm link or a global install of the declared bin), main() never runs and the process exits 0 with no output.

Independent assessment

Verification strength

Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

package.json:13-14 declares the bin awsf as core/src/cli/main.ts, so npm link or npm install -g installs a symlink to it. An `awsf <command>` run through that link has argv[1] equal to the link path while import.meta.url is the target's real file URL, so the guard is false, no command runs, and the exit status is 0. A driver that gates on exit status (for example `awsf land T1 && awsf publish T1`) would read the silent no-op as success. The justfile's `npm run awsf --` path passes the real path and is unaffected, which is why the defect is latent today. Comparing against realpathSync(invokedPath) would close it.

B7-25unverifiablerecorded: fixedpersistEnvelope writes the immutable envelope file before journaling it and then refuses any later write to that path, so a file left behind by an interrupted write or by a crash before the journal append permanently blocks storing the same phase and correction round.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

The process is killed, or the write is cut short, after writeFile at line 1970 and before the persist at line 1971. The journal then holds no envelope for that round. On a resumed run the agent phases at or after the accepted prefix are built again (lines 1465-1466), so the interrupted phase is executed again and spends a new provider call. When that call returns, persistEnvelope reaches the existsSync check at line 1969 for envelopes/<phase>-<round>.json and throws 'immutable envelope already exists'. That is an ordinary phase failure, so closestBlocker maps it to phase-abort and the attempt goes to BLOCKED. The second call is spent, and the attempt cannot move until someone deletes the stale file by hand. Recovery never reads these files (pendingEnvelope comes from journal evidence, phase-recovery.ts:120-124), so the file has no legitimate use after an interruption.

B7-26unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe silence-timeout timer runs void turnLaunch.transport?.cancel(...) with no rejection handler, although cancel can reject when process enumeration fails. The same cancel call in the abort path (line 2804) does attach .catch.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A provider turn goes silent past silence_timeout_seconds, so the timer at 2716-2719 fires. transport.cancel calls ProcessController.terminateTree (transport-broker.ts:766-769). On Linux, the posix port throws EnumerationUnavailable when /proc is unreadable (platform/posix.ts:134). That rejection has no handler, so Node terminates the awsf process before the abort path's handled cancel (2803-2805) can run. The provider's process tree may outlive the CLI, and the attempt gets no BLOCKED record. This needs a rare enumeration failure, so the trigger is not routine.

B7-30unverifiablerecorded: fixedpersistEnvelope overwrites the phase's raw output before the immutability check that refuses an existing envelope, so the refused write has already replaced the bytes that the earlier envelope's rawOutputPath names.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A crash after the envelope file is written (line 1970) but before its journal append leaves envelopes/<phase>-<round>.json with no journal record. On the next run the same phase re-runs, which is a new provider call. persistEnvelope writes the new output to raw/<runId>.txt at line 1964; the runId is the same as the crashed run's because it is built from the session, phase and attempt only (line 2346). The existsSync check at line 1969 then throws 'immutable envelope already exists' and the attempt goes BLOCKED. By then the raw file the orphaned envelope names holds the re-run's bytes, so the only artifact the owner could inspect for the crashed call has been replaced by the guard's own write. The trigger is limited to a crash inside that window; A1-4 covers the blocking itself, and this is the ordering defect.

Original problem and consequence

The journeys inject a pinned clock (production-runner.test.ts:95 and 313: now: () => '2026-08-24T20:26:39.429Z'). Host envelopes take createdAt from infra.now() (line 3064), but agent envelopes take new Date().toISOString() because the engine falls back when options.now is absent (engine.ts:322), and the protected lock witness does the same (protected-commit.ts:137). Impact is determinism and timeline consistency; no wrong state transition was found.

B7-38unverifiablerecorded: fixedproduction-run.ts re-derives the review-failure taxonomy in two private tables (productionReviewBlocker at 1123-1140 and the code ladder in settleExitedReview at 1197-1208) instead of calling the shared reviewFailureBlocker in review-phase.ts that review.ts, rework.ts and adopt.ts already read, and the two production tables disagree with each other and with the shared one.

Original problem and consequence

(a) A reviewer round that fails both envelope_valid and verdict_consistent is recorded review-inconsistent when it happens live, because the verdict check runs before the cold-envelope check (1132 before 1135). If the host crashes and the attempt is recovered, settleExitedReview tests the cold-envelope set first (1202) and records review-malformed. (b) A reviewer cancelled for silence (2717-2718) is recorded silence when it happens live, via the regex at 1163. After a crash, settleExitedReview can only return review-evidence-invalid, review-malformed, review-inconsistent or phase-abort (1197-1208), so it records phase-abort. (c) ReviewEvidenceUnfit maps to review-evidence-invalid in the shared classifier (review-phase.ts:202) but to phase-abort in production (1159), wherever it reaches the REVIEWING catch, for example the recovery-time evidence rebuild at 3448. The owner's L17 code, and the advice keyed to it, therefore depends on whether the host crashed rather than on what failed.

B7-39unverifiablerecorded: fixedTransition evidence is built three different ways with three id schemes. The one the normal run uses (persistTransition) numbers its ids from a counter that restarts at 1 in every invocation, so a resumed run re-issues ids and seq values the attempt already journaled, and the SQLite projection silently drops those transitions.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

Attempt A runs PREPARED->RUNNING: persistTransition (line 1840) writes id `${sid}:transition:1`, seq 1. The attempt pauses at a resumable quota boundary (the quota-pause checkpoint at lines 3328-3334 writes no transition, so the attempt stays RUNNING with its one journaled transition) and is then resumed. executeProductionCommand runs again, so `let transitionSeq = 0` (line 1764) starts over. The resumed RUNNING->GATING at line 3741 is written with id `${sid}:transition:1`, seq 1, which the original PREPARED->RUNNING already holds; every resumed transition whose counter value the original run used collides the same way. projector.ts:567 writes transitions with INSERT OR IGNORE into a table whose transition_id is PRIMARY KEY and whose (session_id, seq) is UNIQUE (migrations/0001-initial.sql:50 and :59), so the resumed rows are silently dropped from the table that observability/queries.ts:351 and metrics/role-rows.ts:515 read. `awsf db rebuild` replays the same projector functions and loses them again. The journal keeps every record, so the loss is confined to the projection. The other two writers use different schemes: the PREPARED->BLOCKED refusal (lines 1665-1667) uses `${sid}:${revision+1}` with seq = revision+1, and settleExitedReview (lines 1221-1226) uses `${sid}:recovery:${seq}`. One helper with one durable per-session sequence would serve all three. None of the journey tests checked (production-runner, shift-blocked, shift-ceiling, visual-references) asserts transition ids or SQLite transition rows after a resume.

Historical classification: cleanup · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/cli/commands/production-run.ts:1785 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B7-39. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Transition IDs and sequence values derive from the next durable attempt revision across normal, refusal, and recovery transitions.

B7-40unverifiablerecorded: wontfix persistable text-delta batching changes journal evidence granularity and could lose unflushed fragments after interruption; the raw turn file is only retained after completion, so this is not behavior-preservingEach streamed text.delta fragment is persisted as its own attempt event through the full write protocol, and the provider stream loop awaits that write inline, so turn throughput is bounded by per-fragment disk and SQLite work.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

A turn that streams 10,000 text fragments issues 10,000 sequential persist calls. The probe measured about 7.8 ms per persisted event on the native probe filesystem with a realistic 8 KB status (lock create and unlink about 1.2 ms, journal append plus fsync about 4.9 ms, status replace about 2.3 ms; the SQLite transaction is not included), so that turn spends about 78 s in persistence alone. The default max_event_count of 100,000 allows about 13 minutes of the same work per run at that floor. The inline await caps the stream consumer near 128 persisted events per second at that floor. The mount /mnt/d is I/O bound in the import probe and is expected to be slower here (not measured). The same fragment text is stored three times: as a journal line, as a SQLite events row (the projector's applyEvent falls through to a generic INSERT for every persistable kind), and in the raw turn file. Cheaper alternative: coalesce consecutive text.delta into one persisted event per flush window (for example a few KB or a few hundred milliseconds, always flushed before a non-delta event and at the turn's terminal event). That cuts journal records, SQLite rows and fsyncs together, and the raw file keeps the full text either way. Changing the granularity is an owner decision, because the journal is the evidence store (AGENTS.md invariant 10).

Historical classification: cleanup · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/cli/commands/production-run.ts:2798 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B7-40. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

wontfix persistable text-delta batching changes journal evidence granularity and could lose unflushed fragments after interruption; the raw turn file is only retained after completion, so this is not behavior-preserving: Keep the current per-event durable evidence until an owner-approved flush/recovery contract exists.

Original problem and consequence

Mid-run, phase N succeeds and drains the account. The boundary probe records effectivePercentRemaining 0 with minutesToReset null (readout.ts:187-188 gives reasonCode semantics-unresolved and verdict unknown). takePhaseBoundarySnapshot persists that 0 in the quota-snapshot (production-run.ts:3303-3313), then returns false at 3322-3323 because figure is null, so phase N+1 is launched against the exhausted account. The same happens when minutesToReset is known but above the threshold, because the stop needs a below-threshold figure before it looks at anything else. If the provider refuses it as quota-exhausted, closestBlocker maps that to quota-exhausted (line 1145) and the attempt ends BLOCKED from RUNNING, a sealed state (task-machine.ts:58), after one launch attempt. The same account at run start is refused before any call and the attempt stays PREPARED (1719-1722). The boundary also never checks exhaustion when no threshold is configured (3322 returns false when threshold is null), although the TR-14 test title promises refusal without any configured threshold. The resume preflight (4014) has the same blind spot: an exhausted scope whose minutes are above threshold has verdict above and passes.

Original problem and consequence

The awsf bin is core/src/cli/main.ts itself (package.json lines 13-15), so each invocation resolves and transforms the static closure before any command logic runs. Quiet-mount probes of importing main.ts took 47.7 s and 43.8 s of wall time; the 43.8 s run split into 6.4 s of CPU and 37.5 s of filesystem waiting on the /mnt/d mount. A read-only subcommand reaches only its own closure (113 modules for routes.ts, 135 for status.ts) but pays for all 327. Cheaper alternative: use the pattern main.ts already uses for group (line 293, await import of ./commands/group.ts) and load production-run.ts and the other heavy command modules as dynamic imports inside their command arms, so each invocation loads only its own closure. tty.ts alone reaches 60 modules through its imports, so the leaf modules need the same check.

B7-46unverifiablerecorded: fixedA builder's gate round recomputes the worktree change set four times, and each recomputation spawns two git processes, because each gate calls observe() or assurance() independently.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only

Original problem and consequence

phaseGates builds the builder gates so that no_protected_paths (line 960, assurance), diff_matches_claims (line 989, observe), writes_within_globs (line 990, observe) and risk_tier_sufficient (line 996, assurance) each call changesSinceBase. For a non-seeded builder, assurance and observe are the same function, so one round runs 8 git processes over the worktree (diff --name-only and ls-files --others, four times), and every correction round repeats them. The intake gate also calls observe() up to twice at lines 1020-1021. Cheaper alternative: compute changesSinceBase once per gate round, memoized inside phaseGates, and pass the array to each gate. The gates in one round only read the tree, so the result is identical.

B7-50unverifiablerecorded: wontfix productionRecoveryBinding's source digest is a recovery authorization check; recomputing at separate pre-confirmation and execution boundaries detects source changes that a cached digest could missproductionRecoveryBinding re-reads and hashes all 339 core/src TypeScript files (3.16 MB) on every call, and a single resume calls it five times, two of them inside the same lease.

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.

Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

A resume calls preflightRecovery (line 3949) and then executeProductionCommand in preflight mode (line 1398) before the owner confirms (lines 4195 and 3992), repeats both under the lease (lines 4206 and the preflight-only call it makes), and the real run then calls executeProductionCommand (4228, which reaches line 1398). That is five full passes over identical sources. The probe measured one pass at 954 ms and 825 ms on the /mnt/d mount (about 0.3 s of recursive readdir plus about 0.6 s of reads and hashing), so a resume spends roughly 4 to 5 s hashing unchanged source before any phase starts. Each granted writing phase (lines 2337 and 3501) and each unconsumed grant (line 1676) adds another pass through protectedGrantSubject. Cheaper alternative: compute the digest once inside the lease and reuse it for the preflight, preflight-only and real passes, so five passes become two (one before confirmation, one under the lease). Keep the authoritative comparison under the lease, so a source edit made during the owner's confirmation still refuses.

wontfix productionRecoveryBinding's source digest is a recovery authorization check; recomputing at separate pre-confirmation and execution boundaries detects source changes that a cached digest could miss: Keep the independent freshness checks rather than trade away the binding guarantee for elapsed time.

onCorrection (1931-1935), register (1941-1945), onSpent (1951-1955) and the post-exit record (2822-2828) each write { type: process, phaseId, adapterId, role, record: redactLocators(...), status, registeredAt, releasedAt, endedAt, exitCode, exitSignal }. Original problem and consequence

takePhaseBoundarySnapshot falls back to the completed agent's route when the next phase is host-only (line 3250), probes that adapter (lines 3260-3284, where probeQuota runs up to two synchronous spawns), persists the reading, and then returns false because a host-only next phase cannot be stopped (lines 3317-3319). In a build-review run this is the builder-to-tests boundary, and the next agent boundary probes the same adapter again. The code calls the reading an intentional context reading, so this is wasted work only if that context is not needed. Cheaper alternative: skip the probe when the next phase has no route and carry forward the last reading with its observedAt, or record nothing for host-only boundaries. The report is built from await doctorCommand(stateRoot) (attempt discovery and lock-holder reads), then await jevDoctorRow(...) (a switch read plus a walk of core/src for the Jev fence, decision/jev-doctor.ts lines 56-68), then await gatherDoctorRows(...) ELI B7 · Protecting the main run command

Earlier repairs protect command environments, saved-file reads, owner attribution and the distinction between demos and real approval. The plan-admission cleanup decision is now settled: only unchanged files created by that operation may be removed when no durable admission exists. Uncertain results are retained for recovery. Filtering secret settings still does not isolate a host command from every reachable file.

Combined scoped judgments: 10 of 66 findings. The other 56 remain unverified.

B8-02resolvedrecorded: fixedartifactReader's containment test is lexical, but its reads follow symlinks. A symlink inside the worktree that points outside it is reported as an existing, non-empty artifact, and its out-of-tree target is read on the host.

Independent assessment

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/cli/commands/production-run.ts:933-973
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The reported static symlink escape is covered. This is not a complete hostile-filesystem race proof.

Original problem and consequence

The builder creates docs/out.json as a symlink to a JSON file outside the tree. resolve() keeps the path under the root, so the lexical test at line 555 passes; statSync (557) and readFileSync (559) follow the link, so artifacts_exist, files_non_empty and json_parses pass on the outside file's size and content (json_parses also reports that file's top-level type). inspection + regression tests

core/src/cli/commands/review-phase.ts:1035-1038; core/src/cli/commands/rework.ts:994-997

The BLOCKED outcome for this case is never written, although EDGE_BLOCKER_CODES.L8 in core/src/state/errors.ts permits the silence code and blocker() at lines 610-618 maps timeouts to it. The catch that would cancel the detached child is never reached. The builder path bounds the same loop: production-run.ts arms a timer from runtime.silence_timeout_seconds at line 2788, re-arms it per event at 2791, and on expiry aborts the controller and cancels the transport (lines 2716-2719). Nothing else bounds the child: no adapter sets a timeout, the broker's only deadline is the 5-second identity handshake (core/src/execution/transport-broker.ts line 699), and LivenessMonitor in core/src/execution/liveness-monitor.ts is imported by no module. The owner-rework journey tests use fake adapters that emit events at once, so no test covers a silent launch.

B8-04resolvedrecorded: fixedThe host commit pins its committer only with -c user.name and -c user.email. Git ranks GIT_COMMITTER_NAME and GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL from the process environment above that config, and the host copies its whole environment into every Git call, so an exported committer variable becomes the committer of the new candidate. The candidate's committer is never checked when it is created.

Independent assessment

Host-created commits use the pinned owner identity in all four author/committer variables. Closure no longer obtains identity from local Git configuration.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/git/commit.ts:27-45; core/src/cli/commands/close.ts:203
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The historical trailer breach is retained by the exact owner-approved exemption, not erased. Future generic multi-user ownership would need a new explicit policy.

Original problem and consequence

A host process started with GIT_COMMITTER_NAME and GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL set (core/src/git/changes.ts lines 14-27 copy all of process.env into each Git call) makes commitAsHost (core/src/git/commit.ts lines 15-19) record that identity as the committer of the new candidate. rework.ts lines 1081-1087 persist the candidate with no identity check. The only identity check, inspectCandidate at lines 418-419, runs at the NEXT owner rework and then refuses the candidate, so the leak surfaces late. Probe B8-A1/gitprobe with the exact commitAsHost argv and an isolated HOME: with GIT_COMMITTER_NAME and GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL set, the committer is the leaked identity while the author stays the owner, because --author also overrides GIT_AUTHOR_*. This session already has GIT_EDITOR=true injected into its environment, so the harness does export Git variables. Latent in the current environment, but it breaks AGENTS invariant 11 (every commit's author and committer identity is the owner's own, full stop) whenever the variable is set.

B8-05resolvedrecorded: fixedcommitAsHost pins the owner identity only through -c user.name, -c user.email and --author, but git lets GIT_COMMITTER_NAME and GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL from the process environment override user.name config, and systemGitRunner passes the full process environment, so a session whose environment carries those two variables commits with its own identity as committer.

Independent assessment

Host-created commits use the pinned owner identity in all four author/committer variables. Closure no longer obtains identity from local Git configuration.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/git/commit.ts:27-45; core/src/cli/commands/close.ts:203
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The historical trailer breach is retained by the exact owner-approved exemption, not erased. Future generic multi-user ownership would need a new explicit policy.

Original problem and consequence

AGENTS.md invariant 11: "Every commit's author and committer identity is the owner's own (`Santiago Marin <santiagomarinsuarez@me.com>`), full stop - a session must never let its own default git identity leak into a commit." With GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=Claude and GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=noreply@anthropic.com in the environment, commitAsHost produces a commit whose committer is Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>. Its callers include the owner-rework candidate (core/src/cli/commands/rework.ts:1081), the production phase commit (production-run.ts:3047) and the awsf init baseline (init.ts:43). Afterwards only the tip-only owner checks in T2 review and rework preflight (review.ts:322-324, rework.ts:418-419) refuse such a commit. No landing or publish guard reads identity (none in core/src/state/guards.ts, cli/commands/land.ts or cli/commands/publish.ts), so a T1 candidate, or an init baseline, can carry the foreign committer into history. integration.ts:156-162 pins all four identity variables for exactly this reason; commit.ts pins none. The fence does not reach this path: no-agent-coauthor.test.ts (2 of 2 pass on 335a184) scans git log --all of this repository after the fact, and no test runs commitAsHost under a hostile identity environment (integration.test.ts:51-53 does that for writeIntegrationCommit only). The leak is conditional on those two variables being present in the process environment.

B8-06unverifiablerecorded: fixedcreateTarget creates the managed worktree and then seeds and persists it with no failure handling, so a seed or persist failure leaves a DRAFT target whose git-registered tree the journal never records, and every retry is refused with AttemptWorktreeExists, whose advice points at awsf start.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A configured runtime.seed_paths entry is missing from the canonical repository (seedWorktreePaths throws WorktreeSeedError, worktrees.ts:175-177), or persistAttempt fails after createWorktree. adopt.ts:494 has already run git worktree add, and nothing catches the error, so executeAdoption rejects with the target still DRAFT and no GATING or BLOCKED record. On retry the fresh path reaches createWorktree again (createTarget, adopt.ts:723), and worktrees.ts:264-268 throws AttemptWorktreeExists because the path exists. That message (worktrees.ts:234-255) describes an interrupted awsf start and tells the owner to clear the tree with Git and run awsf start again (renderer.ts:177-178), which is the wrong entry point for an adoption target; adoption retries use awsf retry with --adopt-as (adopt.ts:249-256). The same seed failure in start.ts is caught and recorded as BLOCKED with the tree path (start.ts:350-372, reason preflight-failed), so the journal shows the tree and the attempt does not stay DRAFT. Recovery is a manual git worktree removal. Impact: low to medium (a recovery dead-end with misleading advice, no data loss).

fixed: createTarget records managed worktree in attempt status and cleans up failed creations so retries are not blocked by orphaned trees.

Original problem and consequence

An `awsf retry --adopt-as` run is killed (Ctrl-C, closed terminal, or power loss) while its configured gates run in measure(). Before the first gate the target is GATING with status.phase = {name: 'adoption tests', state: 'RUNNING'} (adopt.ts:820-821) and an open command-ledger occurrence (adopt.ts:873). Every later run finds the target by existing === 1 (adopt.ts:597-607), and the resume guard at adopt.ts:626-635 refuses it because resumed.phase !== null. The resume branch never calls measure() (adopt.ts:1092-1096), so the ledger restore logic built for exactly this interruption is unreachable. The only other exit is cancel (cancel.ts:69), which also ends adoption into that target id. The owner has to adopt into a new target name and pay for the gates again. Impact: medium.

Original problem and consequence

claude-code.ts:534-535 settles run.completed with exitCode null when the child has not exited within DEFAULT_EXIT_WAIT_MS (transport-loop.ts:44, 5000 ms). review-phase.ts:1014-1022 then persists the process as FAILED and sets processSettled = true although observed.settled is false, and runTurn throws E_BACKEND_FAILURE (review-phase.ts:1027). The catch at adopt.ts:1226-1229 cancels the transport, but adopt.ts:1234 then skips the settlement that review.ts:706-712 and rework.ts:1580-1585 both write, because those two also test observed.settled === false. Consequences: (a) a child that the cancel terminated stays FAILED instead of CANCELLED; (b) when the cancel reports survivors or throws, the record stays FAILED and adopt.ts:1270 clears status.process, and FAILED is not in ACTIVE_PROCESS_STATES (recovery-diagnostics.ts:22), so diagnoseRecovery reports the attempt inactive (probe below) and the live-survivor refusal in inspectSealedCandidate (adopt.ts:296-298) cannot fire. A BLOCKED attempt that carries an L7 candidate is adoptable (completedCandidate, recovery-diagnostics.ts:42-48), so its still-running reviewer child is not seen. Impact: medium, because it defeats the sealed-source survivor guard whenever the cancel does not terminate the child.

B8-12unverifiablerecorded: fixedreadAttemptEvidence JSON.parses every journal line, including an unterminated trailing fragment that the canonical reader (replay.ts scanJournalText) discards as the durable prefix, so one crash mid-append makes awsf review, land and close fail with a raw SyntaxError.

Independent assessment

Current mechanism evidence

Original problem and consequence

A crash during AppendOnlyLog.appendLine (journal.ts) leaves journal.jsonl ending in an unterminated fragment. The next awsf review reads evidence at review.ts:440, or at review.ts:772 when the attempt is REVIEWING with a reservation, and throws SyntaxError before any decision is made. awsf land (land.ts:286, 298) and awsf close (close.ts:59) fail the same way. replay.ts:276-283 treats the same fragment as the durable prefix. No file in core/src calls recoverAttempt, and AppendOnlyLog never truncates, so the next append lands on the fragment's line, where the canonical JSON.parse guard would refuse it as record-corrupt. When the attempt is REVIEWING with callsReserved > 0, awsf retry also refuses (retry.ts:43-44), so the owner is left with manual journal repair. Probe: a fixture with three complete records and a 162-byte unterminated tail made the real readAttemptEvidence throw SyntaxError (Unterminated string in JSON at position 162), while the real scanJournalText returned ok with 3 records and a 162-byte tornTail.

B8-13unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe legacy fallback in recordedRoutes lets the first non-support record with no purpose or the legacy 'worker' value claim the candidate-producing worker, and no later builder record can replace it, so for a pre-split simple-sdlc journal the planner's provider becomes the inversion base.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A source journal written before the purpose split: planner and builder agent records carry no purpose or the legacy 'worker' value. review-record.ts:232-236 sets worker on the planner (worker === null), then skips the builder (worker !== null), so workerProvider is the planner's provider. adopt.ts:368 (workerProvider: routes.worker.provider) and review.ts use it as the base for the opposite-provider rule at review-phase.ts:548-549. With the planner on provider A and the builder on provider B, a reviewer on B satisfies 'opposite of A' and runs on the builder's own provider, the same-provider review the inversion exists to forbid. The removed last-wins rule (else worker = route) selected the builder whenever it was the last non-review record, for example a run stopped before the documenter. Journals whose builder carries purpose 'build' (production-run.ts:2323-2326) are unaffected.

fixed: recordedRoutes prioritizes builder phase over early worker/non-support records for the candidate-producing route.

B8-15unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe stale-reservation reconcile runs only while callsReserved > 0, so a process death after the replacement reviewer's spend leaves the attempt in REVIEWING with no reservation for recovery to find, and later awsf review and awsf retry both refuse it.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

The owner runs awsf review and confirms. The replacement is spent: settle removes the reservation (call-budget.ts:424, this.#held.delete), so the RUNNING persist in onSpent (review-phase.ts:913-917) records budget.snapshot() with callsReserved 0. The owner then presses Ctrl-C or closes the terminal. core/src has no SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP handler, so the catch at review.ts:632 never runs and no L17 is taken. The next awsf review reads REVIEWING with callsReserved 0, skips the reconcile, and decide (review.ts:424-431) refuses because the state is not AWAITING_OWNER. awsf retry refuses because the attempt is not terminal (retry.ts:42). The only exit the code implements is awsf cancel (cancel.ts:69 lists REVIEWING; L16 is marked not-implemented in next-steps.ts:43), so the candidate is lost with no named blocker. The comment at review.ts:755 scopes the reconcile to a death between L25 and GO, and review.ts:765 says recovery must avoid a dead sojourn; the trigger matches only the pre-spend case. A live orphaned reviewer may be why cancel was left as the exit, which is a design call, but the refusal is generic and no named blocker is recorded. Static trace, not probed.

Historical classification: bug · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/cli/commands/review.ts:407 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B8-15. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: reconcileStaleReservation runs when callsReserved is 0 and cleans up stale REVIEWING attempts after process death.

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Original problem and consequence

awsf review persists the L25 transition with callsReserved=1 and the process dies before GO. The next awsf review on that attempt enters reconcileStaleReservation (review.ts:407-409). The builder's process record from earlier in the attempt was journaled as RUNNING at spend (production-run.ts:1933) and then settled, so launched becomes true at line 777 and rewind is false at line 781. The BLOCKED detail then reads 'a provider had already launched, so the charge stands' (line 787) although the replacement never registered a process, and the owner re-entry stays charged in the journaled BLOCKED record. The comment above the function (review.ts:762-764) states the rule the code breaks: the re-entry is rewound 'when no process for the replacement phase ever reached RUNNING'. Scoping the scan to the replacement's own phaseId would restore that rule. Probe section F reproduces the scan over an attempt whose builder ran: lastEdge L25, launched true, rewind would fire false.

B8-17unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe owner-rework broker decorator turns every startProcess rejection into an uncertain launch and marks the reservation as delegated, so a refusal raised before runLauncherBarrier (no child, no spend) leaves the call held and the attempt BLOCKED with callsReserved still 1.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Input: the builder's or reviewer's executable stops resolving between the isAvailable() check at rework.ts:737 and the launch, or assertSpawnSite or assertSpecSafe refuses the registration. The transport-broker.ts startProcess doc comment says everything before runLauncherBarrier is a refusal that costs nothing, and the launcher-barrier.ts refund-rule comment says a call that PROVABLY never ran is returned. Output: the decorator at rework.ts:630-634 adds the reservation id to delegatedReservations and rethrows as ReworkRouteMismatch('broker launch outcome is uncertain'); the release loop at rework.ts:1445-1446 then skips that reservation. The attempt is persisted BLOCKED with budget.callsReserved=1 and zero spend, and the check at rework.ts:1543 accepts it. retry.ts:43 refuses the attempt (ReservationOutstanding), and adopt.ts:292 and candidate-seed.ts:70 refuse the same state. The same refusal through review.ts:646-648 or adopt.ts:1230 releases the call, so two commands disagree about one refusal. A narrower guard would key on whether the barrier was entered (RegistrationFailed.step) rather than on any throw. Severity medium: the trigger is rare, but the outcome over-bills a call and wedges the attempt.

Historical classification: bug · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/cli/commands/rework.ts:632 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B8-17. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Owner rework broker decorator marks reservation delegated only when child process was actually spawned, releasing pre-spawn refusals.

B8-18unverifiablerecorded: fixedbounded() keeps only the first 4,000 characters, so owner-rework gate output is retained as a head. The failing detail and the closing totals of a failing configured command are dropped from the TestOutput the T2 reviewer reads, although the variable is named outputTail and the production twin keeps a tail or a head, failure and tail window.

Independent assessment

Original problem and consequence

A configured gate such as a test runner fails with its assertion and summary at the end of a long log. commandOutput (line 1201) keeps only the opening 4,000 characters, and outputTail (line 1204) accumulates that same head window, since bounded() slices from index 0 (lines 332-334). testOutput is then serialized as-is into the review context (core/src/workflow/review-evidence.ts line 188, reached via review-phase.ts line 728) and into the tests envelope (rework.ts lines 1276-1284). The reviewer sees exit codes but not the failure. production-run.ts lines 2225-2238 render each command with boundCommandOutput and renderCommandEvidence (head, failure window, tail) and keep the joined tail with safeTail, which keeps the last 4,000 characters (lines 602-603). core/src/gates/command-evidence.ts lines 1-12 documents this exact defect (a trailing window dropped the failing test's identity) and its fix. rework.ts imports nothing from that module. The complete output is kept under raw/ (lines 1186-1188), but no reviewer reads it.

T2 owner rework where the reviewer's provider is unavailable after the builder has run: resolveReviewRoute at line 1296 asks for availability by default (review-phase.ts line 505 checks requireAvailable !== false), so it throws ProductionRouteUnavailable after the builder call is already spent. The catch sees RUNNING (L7 is persisted only at line 1332), builds failedPhase as the spread of phase with status FAILED, errorCode and errorMessage (lines 1481-1484) from the record that persistPhase('SUCCEEDED') left in phase, and persists it under the builder's phaseId (lines 1485-1490). The candidate ends BLOCKED, so the owner is shown a failed builder for a build that succeeded.

B8-40unverifiablerecorded: fixedEvery persistable streamed event, including each text.delta, is written with its own awaited persist() in a sequential loop after the stream ends, so one reviewer reply costs one full durable write cycle per chunk.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

isPersistableKind keeps every kind except thinking.delta (core/src/contracts/normalized-events.ts:44-46), and each provider text chunk becomes its own text.delta (core/src/adapters/claude-code-stream.ts:309, which runs with --include-partial-messages per claude-code.ts:447; core/src/adapters/pi-codex-stream.ts:371). A reviewer reply of a few KB therefore arrives as hundreds of records, and the loop at lines 1008-1013 awaits a persist() for each one. Each persist goes through persistAttempt and runWriteProtocol (persistence/attempt-lock.ts:193-205): a status read, a journal append followed by fsync (persistence/journal.ts:44-48), a status rewrite and a projection. A probe that reproduces only the journal append with fsync and the status tmp-write with fsync and rename took 10.7 ms per cycle for 300 records (3206 ms in total) and 7.9 ms per cycle for 1000 records, while one batched append of the same records took 9-12 ms. The probe ran on local ext4, and the /mnt/d mount is slower, so each review turn spends seconds to tens of seconds on journaling and repeats on every contract retry. Per-chunk records are a deliberate evidence choice, so the cheaper form keeps the evidence but writes it once: one coalesced text record per turn (the host already accumulates the full text in output, lines 985 and 992), or one batched write per turn through the write protocol. production-run.ts:2794-2799 has the same per-delta loop, so the fix belongs in the shared persist path.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Coalesced streamed text chunks into one complete normalized-event write per review turn, preserving non-text event order and the exact reply.

Original problem and consequence

A builder envelope fails its artifacts_exist gate because budget-summary.json is missing. The PhaseGateFailure message (failedCheckSummary, engine.ts:230-235) reads `artifacts_exist/budget-summary.json: required artifact is missing`, which matches /ceiling|budget|allowance/i, so rework.ts:1524-1541 records RUNNING to BLOCKED on L8 with code budget-exhausted. That is the code the trap catalogue assigns to the L8 after-spend budget trap (traps/catalogue.ts:133), so the stop reads as a spent call budget when the cause is a gate failure. A check note containing 'timeout' records silence. The same failure under production-run.ts is phase-abort. Cost: the two commands that run the same builder phase classify the same failure differently, and the stop code depends on how an artifact or check was named.

B8-48unverifiablerecorded: wontfix the repeated pin reads defend distinct boundaries against external worktree mutationEach dispatched gate runs a full pin check before the command (line 883) and another after it (line 961), with observePins at line 947 in between, so the before-check of gate i+1 repeats the after-check of gate i with no I/O between them.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

assertCandidatePinned (adopt.ts:373-385) runs assertClean on the canonical checkout and on the managed worktree, which is two `git status --porcelain` scans, plus two rev-parse calls. Per dispatched gate there are five status scans: before (two), observePins (one) and after (two). Three of the five repeat a state that was just read: the next gate's before-check repeats the previous after-check, and observePins repeats the worktree half of the after-check. For N gates that is about 5N scans where about 2N would do, and the canonical checkout is scanned at every boundary. Cheaper alternative: keep one pin check per gate boundary (the after-check, which catches a command that moved or dirtied the tree), reuse observePins' worktree result, and keep the single check at line 827 for the first gate.

wontfix the repeated pin reads defend distinct boundaries against external worktree mutation: Before/after candidate checks and persisted pin observations are not interchangeable; removing them opens an unobserved mutation window.

Original problem and consequence

The owner raises a task's ceiling while a builder call is in flight. raise re-reads at revision R and persists R+1 (raise.ts:193-206). The runner's next write (production-run.ts:1769-1770) calls persistAttempt with its cached revision R, which attempt.ts:375-377 refuses with 'attempt revision changed'. Its in-memory budget also keeps the old resolved ceiling (call-budget.ts:246-247), so the printed 'Raise: X -> Y' is not what the run enforces, and the ledger and the running process disagree.

Original problem and consequence

AGENTS.md invariant 11 says: "Every commit's author and committer identity is the owner's own (`Santiago Marin <santiagomarinsuarez@me.com>`), full stop — a session must never let its own default git identity leak into a commit." Git gives GIT_COMMITTER_NAME and GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL precedence over user.name config, and -c only sets config. systemGitRunner (changes.ts:14-17) copies all of process.env into the git child, and runSystemCommand passes that env to spawnSync with shell: false (transport-broker.ts:247-253), so a session that exports its own committer identity leaks it into the commit. Probe, in a throwaway repo under the probe directory: with GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=Claude and GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=noreply@anthropic.com, the same -c and --author argv produced author 'Santiago Marin <santiagomarinsuarez@me.com>' and committer 'Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>'. This helper is the production candidate path: production-run.ts:3038 builds systemGitRunner(worktree) and production-run.ts:3047 commits with it, engine.ts:91 uses the same helper, and init.ts:43 and run.ts:81 call it with the default runner. The owner-pinned commit paths pin the committer through env: protected-commit.ts:74 (GIT_COMMITTER_NAME 'Santiago Marin') and integration.ts:161 (GIT_COMMITTER_NAME from HOST_AUTHOR). Cost: the committer of candidate commits depends on the ambient environment. The only check is no-agent-coauthor.test.ts, which scans history after the commit exists and matches only agent-shaped names.

Independent assessment

Original problem and consequence

'awsf metrics --started-before 2026-10-13T10:00:00' means 08:00Z under TZ=Europe/Madrid, 10:00Z under UTC and 14:00Z under America/New_York (probe). A laptop and a CI runner print different route tables for the same command. The readout echoes the raw string ('runs started before ...', metrics.ts:198) and never the instant used, so the owner cannot see the shift. The same flag reads a date-only value as UTC, so the accepted forms disagree with each other. The flag's own error text requires 'an ISO 8601 instant' (metrics.ts:89), and an instant needs an explicit offset.

Original problem and consequence

Plan P has tickets T05 and T06. 'awsf new T05-task --plan P --ticket T05' runs and lands. Then 'awsf new T06-task --plan P --ticket T06': scanTasks (preflight.ts:241) records T05-task with tickets null, and duplicateOf (preflight.ts:251) gives T06-task tickets null. selectsOverlappingWork(null, null) is true (fields.ts:503-505), so evaluateDuplicate refuses (fields.ts:512-518) with 'task T05-task (latest attempt LANDED) already carries the same plan ref P; continue that task or change this request'. Changing the request does not clear it, because samePlan ignores the request text. The only exits are --continues T05-task, which records a false lineage that puts T05 in the chain skipped at fields.ts:512, or not starting T06. The same refusal fires at awsf preflight (duplicate field, preflight.ts:415) and again at awsf start, because K1 re-measures duplicate through duplicateFacts (preflight.ts:359). plan-author attempts require a plan ref and a sealed ticketSelection (workflow/recipes/plan-author.ts:16), so they take the same null path for each spine ticket of one plan. e32e892's stated intent, in its commit body, is 'Two shift tasks now duplicate each other only when they select a common ticket'; the ticket selections sealed after it are the same bare-plan-stem case and are not covered.

B9-16unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe preview's content-type table lacks .mjs, .wasm and other common extensions, so those files are served as application/octet-stream beside a nosniff header, and a candidate whose bundle uses them loads broken in the owner's preview.

Independent assessment

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A delivery whose build emits an ES module (.mjs) or a WebAssembly file: serveBundle (line 185) answers with content-type application/octet-stream because CONTENT_TYPES has no mjs or wasm key. SECURITY_HEADERS (api/security.ts:24) sends x-content-type-options: nosniff. Browsers refuse to run a module script whose MIME type is not JavaScript (strict MIME checking in the HTML spec), and WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming requires application/wasm. The preview page therefore fails to run, and the owner reads a correct candidate as a regression, which is the misreading this preview exists to prevent. Latent for the AWSF dashboard bundle, which holds only html, js and css today. The table also lacks jpg, gif, webp, ico, woff, ttf, txt, xml, mp4 and webm, which all fall through to the same octet-stream type. Not run: no browser was used, so the behaviour is taken from the HTML and Fetch specifications.

Historical classification: bug · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/cli/commands/preview.ts:162 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B9-16. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

fixed: preview content-type table includes .mjs, .wasm, and web extensions.

B9-17unverifiablerecorded: fixedOnce serveBundle has the server listening, the 'serving' lease write and the preview.json write run outside the try that releases on failure, so an error there leaves the server running with no handle and the process never exits.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A preview whose build succeeds and whose server starts, then fails at writeLease (303) or record (304), for example ENOSPC, EACCES, or a non-writable attempt directory. The catch at 296-299 has already passed, so nothing closes the server. previewCommand rejects, but the caller keeps no handle: main.ts:1043-1047 awaits previewCommand and discards its result, main() returns 1 through process.exitCode (main.ts:1164), and the CLI never calls process.exit. The listening server therefore keeps the event loop alive. Meanwhile GET / keeps answering with the bundle that was never recorded, preview.json is not written, and if writeLease(serving) was the failing call the lease still reads 'building' with a live pid, so every later awsf preview is refused. The owner is told the preview failed while a candidate is still served and the terminal does not return.

Historical classification: bug · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/cli/commands/preview.ts:303 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B9-17. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: preview server closes and releases lease if lease write fails after listen.

Original problem and consequence

K1 (awsf preflight) refuses on a duplicate request and on an unconsulted prior session, so a silent drop turns a refusal into a pass. Case 1: task T-twin has the same request as the task being preflighted and its status.json fails to read with anything other than a missing file (a truncated file, or a transient EACCES or EBUSY). scanTasks (preflight.ts:228-246) never counts it, duplicateFacts().others omits it, and evaluateDuplicate (fields.ts:509) finds no duplicate, so the duplicate field passes. Case 2: the task is on attempt 2 and attempt 1's status.json is unreadable; priorAttemptStatuses (preflight.ts:199-205) yields no session, journal.priorSessions (preflight.ts:302 and 417) omits it, and evaluatePriorAttempts (fields.ts:534-546) never requires --consulted to name it. ancestors() (preflight.ts:174-176) has the same catch, so a read error also truncates the continuation chain that both facts use. The errors reach these catches because readAttempt (attempt.ts:329-332) and tryReadJson (status-store.ts:24-31) rethrow everything except ENOENT.

B9-33resolved057370d recheck · Historical ledger: recorded: owner-blocked inv8: partial-output cleanup needs an unauthorized unlink/delete siteThe export writes the header and every row in one exclusive writeFileSync, and a failure part-way leaves a truncated file at the target name with no cleanup on the error path.

Independent assessment

The remediation explicitly leaves this finding owner-blocked. No later decision resolving its authority or invariant conflict was located.

Verification strength
ledger + boundary inspection
Current mechanism evidence
FIXREPORT.md: open owner decisions; original finding source
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
For cleanup, authorize only the named host-owned artifact operation or choose a non-deleting recovery. For stub prompt checks, prove production validation independently of fixture convenience.

Original problem and consequence

awsf metrics export --output named.jsonl on a full disk: writeFileSync (line 78) creates the file exclusively, the write fails with ENOSPC, the error propagates, and the partial file stays. With the default random name the leftover is harmless, but with an explicit --output the retry is refused by the same wx flag (EEXIST) until the owner deletes the partial file by hand. The header's rowsSha256 covers the full row set, so a reader that checks the digest can detect the truncation, but nothing on the error path removes the partial file. Low impact; code-level finding, not run.

B9-35unverifiablerecorded: not-reproduced already fixed by ffc63bdThe owner-reason validators cut the text to 2000 characters before the credential scan, so a credential that straddles the cut is persisted as an unredacted prefix; a probe confirmed 15 characters of a ghp_ token survive.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

The reason is normalized, cut to MAX_REASON (2000) characters, and only then scanned (prove.ts:177-178; the same order at raise.ts:154-155 and relate.ts:127-128). A credential that straddles the cut is scanned only in its prefix. The patterns need a minimum tail (for example gh[opusr]_ needs 16 or more characters), so the prefix matches nothing and is persisted to the journal or the replay record. The probe confirms it. A GitHub-style token with 15 characters before the cut came back as 'xxxx ghp_AAAAAAAAAAAAAAA' (length 2000, not redacted), while the same token wholly inside the cap is refused with CredentialRejected. The leak is a 15-character partial, so severity is low, but the contract is that credential-shaped data is never persisted. Scanning before bounding fixes it.
