Original problem and consequence

Two awsf preview runs for the same state root that start within a few milliseconds: both call livePreviewServer (282) before either reaches writeLease (290), and writeLease is a plain writeFile with no exclusive create (111-113). Both build and serve; the second lease overwrites the first, so the file names one server while two are live, which breaks the rule the file states, that exactly one runs. readLease (103-108) returns null for any read or parse error, so a torn lease caught mid-write reads as no server. processAlive (94-101) only checks that the pid exists and records no start identity, so a dead server whose pid is later reused makes every preview refused, with a message that tells the owner to stop a process that does not exist; only deleting preview-server.json by hand clears it. The execution controller already compares start identities for this purpose (operation-lease.ts:56-61). Code-level finding; the race window is small and needs two concurrent starts.

fixed: Serialize preview claims, atomically replace leases, fail closed on corruption, and compare process identities.

B9-42unverifiablerecorded: fixedA normal awsf close takes eight full registered-tree snapshots, and each snapshot spawns one synchronous git process per registered blob, so the same three commits are re-read and identical blobs are re-fetched on every call.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

readClosureSnapshot (core/src/git/closure.ts:25-59) runs git ls-tree plus one git cat-file per registered path, and the registered set covers every plan in the plans root (in this repository 22 plan HTML files, 22 build-prompt files and 432 ticket files), not only the plan being closed. A normal close calls it eight times: close.ts:145-146 (base, head), close.ts:232 through verifyClosureCommit (parent, commit), and close.ts:239 through finishClosureCheckout, which runs verifyClosureCommit again and then reads parent and commit once more (closure.ts:122-124). Only three distinct commits are involved (base, head, the new commit), and blob bytes are keyed by an immutable SHA yet re-fetched every time. Measured on this machine, one snapshot of 335a184 spawns 478 git processes (476 blobs plus two) and takes 15,975 ms cold and 9,842 ms warm, so one normal close spends roughly 80-130 s in snapshot reads alone, and the cost grows with every ticket added to any plan. Cheaper alternatives: memoize snapshots per commit within one close (three reads instead of eight), memoize blob bytes by blob SHA (on the order of 500 reads in total instead of about 3,800), and read all blobs with one git cat-file --batch process.

Historical classification: cleanup · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/cli/commands/close.ts:239 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B9-42. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: readClosureSnapshot memoizes snapshots by commit SHA and blobs by blob SHA.

Original problem and consequence

An owner reason of 1,985 characters, a space, then a GitHub token (ghp_ plus 20 characters) is accepted by assertDegradeReason, assertProveReason, assertGrantReason and assertRelateReason. Each returns the first 2,000 characters, which end in ghp_AAAAAAAAAA (probe-reasons.mjs). That text is journalled as the attempt's degradation, grant, relation or lastActivity record. B9-46unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe attempt-to-recipe mapping, including the plan-author same-provider-degradation refusal, is written out in four places, and next.ts resolves shipped recipes only, so grantOwedNow reports no owed grant for any compiled workflow even though preflight measures the writing phases of exactly those workflows.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost

Original problem and consequence

Four resolvers already disagree: start.ts:246-263 and preflight.ts:113-130 both throw CompiledWorkflowUnbound for an unbound shift or prove attempt, production-run.ts:308-328 looks up SUPPORTED and returns undefined instead, and next.ts:45-46 returns null for every compiled id because workflowRecipe reads only shipped recipes (catalog.ts:113-115). For a shift, prove or plan-author attempt the grant step is therefore never measured by awsf next, while preflight.ts:395 and 407-432 compute the writers and protectedPlan for the same attempt. The K1 exemption is a workflow-id array consumed by start.ts:198 and next.ts:30 instead of a property of the workflow, and the plan-author degradation rule is restated by name at start.ts:255, preflight.ts:120, production-run.ts:313 and degrade-review.ts:137. Adding or changing a compiled workflow means editing every copy, and a missed copy fails silently. Simplest general fix: one resolveAttemptRecipe in core/src/workflow used by all four callers, with the K1 exemption and the same-provider-degradation rule declared on the workflow definitions.

B9-49unverifiablerecorded: fixedpreview.ts lists the candidate's changed paths with a plain git diff, which reports a renamed file under its new path only, while the same listing in git/changes.ts passes --no-renames for exactly that reason, so a declared preview source moved out of its directory is judged unchanged.

Independent assessment

Original problem and consequence

A candidate moves a declared preview source out of its directory with identical bytes. Git's default rename detection lists only the new path, so planPreview returns the diff-readout posture with 'no changed path is under this web repository's preview sources, so there is nothing new to look at' and never builds the preview. The same candidate listed with --no-renames gives serve, with the old path visible as a changed visual path. The owner's gate therefore never shows the rendered change that the removal caused. The fix is the convention already in git/changes.ts: add --no-renames to this argv.

Original problem and consequence

statusCommand (status.ts:228-234) starts readAttemptEvidence unconditionally inside its Promise.all. Its result feeds formatRouteProvenance (line 238, agent-start and agent records only), shiftReadout (line 248), and formatStatusEvidence only when --evidence is passed (line 261). Measured on the 21 MB probe attempt: 1,733 and 1,871 ms per call for 1,102 evidence records. Because 1,102 of its 1,108 lines carry evidence, a text pre-filter would skip little. Scaled to the 332 MB landed shift journal (v3-w02-m4m5-shift/1), one plain awsf status costs roughly 28 s and repeats on every poll. For non-shift attempts the default readout could avoid the journal entirely; shift readouts still need the accepted-envelope records. Cheaper alternatives: write the route provenance onto status.json at the write that records it (status.json is already rewritten at every revision), so the default readout reads status.json only; and keep a summary of accepted envelopes and gates, updated on append, for shift readouts.

B9-51unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe survivor refusal on cancel is keyed to the RUNNING state alone, so cancelling a REVIEWING, GATING, PREPARED or AWAITING_OWNER attempt whose recorded process tree did not terminate still seals it CANCELLED with its process cleared; the ghost-process rule should attach to the recorded process, not to one lifecycle state.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

A REVIEWING attempt's reviewer process (recorded at review-phase.ts:905) survives TERM and KILL, so terminate returns terminated:false with survivors [pid]. cancel.ts:106 does not throw because the state is not RUNNING; the L18 guard (guards.ts:329, humanInput only) accepts the human reason with no tree evidence, while L9 (guards.ts:179-184) requires treeTerminated and survivorsReported. persistAttempt then writes CANCELLED with process null (cancel.ts:124), so the sealed attempt no longer names the live pid, and awsf retry mints attempt n+1 with the survivor recorded only in a lastActivity string. doctor.ts:60 already reports this exact state as an orphan pid, so the defect is caught only after the fact. Simplest general fix: require treeTerminated and survivorsReported on every CANCELLED edge from a process-holding state, or refuse in cancel.ts whenever current.process is non-null and !report.terminated, whatever the state.

B9-55unverifiablerecorded: fixedawsf preflight parses the attempt's own journal three times (through pinnedBase, journalFacts and attemptConfirmations) and reads every task's status file one at a time to build the project scan.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

preflightCommand reads the current journal through pinnedBase (preflight.ts:400, which calls verifiedTargetSeed at preflight.ts:134 and therefore readVerifiedAttempt, a full parse of every record); through journalFacts (preflight.ts:401), where the current task's attempts are related and line 288 parses each journal; and through attemptConfirmations (preflight.ts:423), which calls readAttemptEvidence again (lines 312-313) on the same unchanged file, repeating the second read. Separately, scanTasks (preflight.ts:233-239) awaits attemptStatuses for every task of the project in sequence, and gatherLandingClosures (preflight.ts:416, core/src/closure/readout.ts:50-55) walks every attempt again one readAttempt at a time, so the project's status files are read twice per preflight. At the measured rates (about 1.8 s per 21 MB for an evidence parse, 2.5-3.1 s for a verified read), a preflight of a shift attempt with a 332 MB journal spends roughly 1.5-2 minutes re-parsing the same file. Cheaper alternatives: parse once in preflightCommand and pass the records into pinnedBase, journalFacts and attemptConfirmations (readEvidence is already injectable at line 401); build the project status scan once and share it between scanTasks and gatherLandingClosures.

Original problem and consequence

A project whose build does not empty its output directory exits 0 on a second preview of the same candidate, but every pre-existing file the build did not rewrite has an mtime no greater than the newest pre-build mtime (preview.ts:226), so preview.ts:241-242 throws PreviewBundleStale and nothing is shown although the build succeeded. The root is that the bundle is not the build's to keep: deleting the bundle directory inside the managed worktree before the build makes every served file fresh by construction and removes the timestamp heuristic. Separately, two concurrent awsf preview runs can both pass livePreviewServer (preview.ts:282) and both overwrite preview-server.json through a plain writeFile (preview.ts:112), so the one-server rule is a check-then-act rather than an exclusive create.

Original problem and consequence

No current publication is wrong, because the push is authorized first (git/publish.ts:197) and a valid push cannot fail the L27 transition. The defect is that the lifecycle check is a rubber stamp built from the values it claims to verify: publish.ts:280 passes true for confirmed and the checkout fact into the fast-forward slot, L27 never reads the fast-forward or verdict facts (guards.ts:492-508), and the verdict rows reach the journal only as display text inside the envelope (publish.ts:296), never as lifecycle evidence. A future edit to the verdict rows (publish/authorize.ts:127-145) or a second caller of the publication step would not be stopped by the lifecycle guard. Simplest general fix: feed L27 the same authorization plan or verdict that the push used, so the transition and the push share one decision.

Scrubbing the whole output before windowing would have redacted all 40 characters.

B10-02partially resolved057370d recheck · Historical ledger: recorded: fixedPermissionSession.enforce() cannot see gitignored files, so a seeded node_modules/.bin tool rewritten inside an attempt worktree passes the path policy and is then run host-side by the configured gates, which can record a forged green result.

Independent assessment

Read-only seed mounts protect the bwrap path. The fallback compares size, mtime and inode, not bytes. A synthetic same-inode/same-size rewrite with restored mtime passed enforce().

Verification strength
reproduced residual
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/policy/sandbox-broker.ts:190-231
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Keep the OS-enforced path as the assurance boundary. A fallback claim requires a mutation test that detects this rewrite. No production tampering was observed.

Original problem and consequence

On a bwrap host the builder's worktree is bound read-write (sandbox-broker.ts:179). The builder (awsf.config.yaml:56 allows exec) overwrites node_modules/.bin/tsc, a copy of the repo's node_modules that start.ts:344 seeds into every attempt worktree (awsf.config.yaml:24, seed_paths: [node_modules]). enforce() takes its after-snapshot through captureChangeSet, whose untracked scan uses --exclude-standard (git/changes.ts:64), so the ignored file never appears and enforce() returns changedPaths=[] with no PermissionBreach. The gate dispatch plan runs each configured argv with cwd set to the attempt worktree (production-run.ts:267), and the configured gates are npm run typecheck and npm run lint (awsf.config.yaml:142-143). npm prepends node_modules/.bin to PATH, so the rewritten binary runs on the host and can exit 0 without checking anything. The gate evidence is then recorded as passing, and git add --all (git/commit.ts:14) leaves the ignored file out of the commit, so the landed diff holds only the builder's tracked edits. The baseline worktree already treats the same seed as an execution input and digests it against the repository (baseline-worktree.ts:120-128, TR-18); attempt worktrees get no equivalent check. Verified by probe: the enforce() blind spot and the exit status of the rewritten binary. Verified by code reading only: the npm PATH step and the gate dispatch cwd.

Historical classification: bug · high · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/policy/sandbox-broker.ts:454 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B10-02. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: (broker half a78bc72, callers f8d5710) seed_paths ro-bound under bwrap and size/mtime/inode-fingerprinted without an OS sandbox (a78bc72); production-run, review-phase, rework and grant now pass config.runtime.seed_paths to openPermissionSession (f8d5710)

B10-03resolvedrecorded: fixedcheckoutRoot returns the start directory when neither it nor any ancestor holds a .git entry, so a non-git directory that contains awsf.project.yaml is treated as the plan checkout and self-placed.

Independent assessment

A non-Git directory cannot silently self-place its plan root. The resolver raises a named failure.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/registry/plan-source.ts; core/test/unit/registry/plan-source-no-git-b10-03.test.ts
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Hard failure is correct at this boundary. Read-only surfaces should show the reason, not an empty board.

Original problem and consequence

cwd is a directory that holds awsf.project.yaml and specs/*.html but has no .git in it or any ancestor, such as an unpacked export or a parent folder that is not itself a repository. checkoutRoot returns that directory (line 254), isInside is true for every catalog under it, and the plan root becomes <cwd>/specs, so the placement that registers the real plan checkout is ignored. Probe case D resolves <cwd>/specs/gamma.html while the placement registers the plan checkout that holds alpha.html; probe case E, with no specs/ under cwd, throws ENOENT instead of falling through to the placement. The doc comment above resolvePlanSources (line 282) says every plan resolves 'to its self checkout or explicit foreign placement', and a directory with no .git is not a checkout, so this fallback contradicts that contract.

Historical classification: bug · high · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/registry/plan-source.ts:254 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B10-03. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: checkoutRoot throws PlanCheckoutUnresolvedError instead of self-placing a non-git cwd; ticket CLI candidates fixture gains a .git dir

owner decision + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/cli/main.ts; HANDOFF.md:226-237

Two distinct conditions have distinct behavior. The scope decision must not be simplified back into one silent fallback.

Original problem and consequence

AGENTS.md invariant 12 says "Every ticket set belongs to exactly one plan." and that the flat intake store, specs/tickets/Tnn.md under the plans root, "belongs to no plan". With catalog plans.default = P, no ticket directory for P, and a flat light ticket present, awsf ticket list, awsf ticket show and awsf backlog (through ticketStoreForList) show the flat T01 as P's ticket set, so the plan and its ticket set disagree. For a catalog whose plans.root is not specs (for example docs/plans), the fallback reads specs/tickets while the light store reads docs/plans/tickets. Latent in this repo: specs/tickets/awsf-plan exists and specs/tickets holds no flat T*.md today. The fallback is marked temporary by its own comment, and no invariant text carves it out.

B10-05unverifiablerecorded: fixedbuildMinimalConfig, which awsf init commits as each new project's awsf.config.yaml, sets the runtime limits and the risk ceilings to schema floors, so a new project's provider turns are cancelled after one idle second and its output budgets discard everything after the first byte or event.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

awsf init writes buildMinimalConfig() as awsf.config.yaml and commits it as 'chore: awsf init baseline' (init.ts:42), and the init output gives no warning to edit it. The file loads with silence_timeout_seconds 1, process_grace_seconds 0, max_output_bytes 1, max_event_count 1, risk.default T0, call_ceiling T0/T1/T2 all 1, and correction_allowance auto 0 and owner 0. The idle timer armed at production-run.ts:2719 uses silence_timeout_seconds times 1000 and cancels the turn through transport.cancel when no provider activity arrives inside that window, so any gap of more than one second cancels the turn. output-budget.ts:167 and :250 discard the remainder after the first event or byte. Every tier allows a single model call with no correction, so no multi-call workflow can complete. The shipped config uses 2700, 2, 67108864, 100000, T1, T0/T1/T2 = 1/3/5 and auto 1 owner 1 (awsf.config.yaml:18-21 and 148-150). This is separate from D-6, which covers the protected_paths list in the same template.

Historical classification: bug · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/config/init-template.ts:38 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B10-05. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: buildMinimalConfig sets practical production defaults rather than schema floors.

Original problem and consequence

awsf.config.yaml lists two agents named builder, the first with writes ["src/**"] and the second with writes []. The loader accepts it. candidate-seed.ts:389 checks inherited seed diffs against the first definition (Array.find). The execution route is resolved from the last definition (new Map(...) at production-run.ts:1380-1384, agents.get at 1467), and its agent.writes feed the sandbox (production-run.ts:1567) and the write gate (production-run.ts:2397). The resume quota check (production-run.ts:3999, find) takes the adapter, and therefore the stop threshold, from the first definition while the resumed phase runs on the adapter of the last. No config error is raised, and the write boundary or quota threshold applied can belong to a different definition than the one that runs.

Original problem and consequence

A candidate whose only deletions are '--'-prefixed lines, such as dropping a '-- legacy index comment' line from a migration or removing a '--primary: #fff;' custom property. selectionOrder and the passes in boundReviewDiff (review-diff.ts:99-104 and 170-183) file those hunks as additions, so an addition-only hunk is admitted in file order while the deletion hunk is dropped. That breaks rule 2 (deletions are never dropped before additions) and the file-level rule that a file whose removals did not fit shows no additions. The reviewer sees '+' lines and a partial marker, not the removal. core/src/workflow/review-evidence.ts:195 computes fullDiffRemovesLines with the same function, so it is false for these candidates and the 'deletions survived bounding' guard (review.ts:307-313) is skipped.

Original problem and consequence

A candidate touches a file whose delivered per-path diff is longer than the reviewer reads, for example a 3000-line generated file, and the Read tool's default window is 2000 lines. Line 99 keeps the tool.requested event, line 107 adds the path to `read` on the request alone, line 121 drops it from `paths`, and line 123 sets required=false because omitted.length > 0 and paths is empty. verdictConsistent then reports 'the supplied diff is complete', and an accept verdict with limitations: [] passes verdict_consistent. Hunks past the read window, or everything past line 40, were never reviewed, and no limitation records that. Original problem and consequence

A provider text output or an API payload containing one unbroken run of letters, digits, '+', '.' and '-' of tens of kilobytes (for example hex without separators) blocks the event loop. Probe P2 timed containsCredential on runs of 10000, 20000 and 40000 characters at 296, 1040 and 3092 ms. The scrubber is reached at cli/commands/rework.ts:1000 (scrubCredentialString over the whole accumulated provider output) and at api/responses.ts:49 (publicApiValue, on every API response). Growth is quadratic, so about 50 s at 160000 characters is an extrapolation, not a measurement. Severity: medium for availability; needs an unusually long unbroken run.

fixed: anchor URL credential pattern with word boundary to eliminate quadratic regex backtracking on long character runs.

B10-27unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe canonical-versus-runtime disjointness check runs in one nesting direction only, so a session runtime that contains the canonical checkout is accepted, and under worktree confinement the checkout becomes writable.

Independent assessment

Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

sessionRuntime = <state> and canonicalRepository = <state>/repo. assertSandboxRoots accepts this: the worktree-versus-runtime check at line 125 tests both directions, but line 128 tests only runtime-inside-canonical. Under confinement "worktree" on a bwrap host, confinedSpec binds the runtime writable with --bind (line 348) and binds nothing for the checkout, so the checkout lies beneath a writable mount inside the namespace. The function's own message says the session runtime may not make part of the canonical repository writable, and this breaks it. Host-mode bwrap is not affected, because the later --ro-bind of the canonical repository (line 181) re-protects it. Reaching this needs a runtime that is an ancestor of the checkout, which owner placement would have to produce. The worktree-confinement mode is the one the W18 prove replay uses (sandbox-broker.ts:67-73).

Original problem and consequence

A flat-store ticket T01 has depends_on: [T99], where no ticket T99 exists (a typo or a deleted ticket). lightTicketAgreement returns no violations because it checks vocabularies and cycles only, and lightTicketCycle returns null for unknown ids. backlog.ts:110 computes ready as ticket.depends_on.every((id) => byId.get(id)?.state === 'done'), which is always false for a missing id, so T01 never becomes ready and no check reports why. The plan tier rejects the same shape (ticketDependencies, plan-agreement.ts:184: 'depends on X, which does not exist'), so the two tiers disagree.

Original problem and consequence

A plan such as specs/linked-plan.html that is a symbolic link (for example a plan shared between repositories) reports Dirent.isSymbolicLink() and fails isFile(), so resolvePlanSources drops it without an error. Its ticket set specs/tickets/linked-plan/ is then never checked against a plan, and the dashboard, backlog and ticket selection omit the plan. The fence's orphan check (ticket-plan-sync.test.ts:57-74) reports the leftover ticket set only when another resolved plan shares its tickets root, so a symlinked plan that is the only plan in its root passes silently. AGENTS.md invariant 12 says 'a ticket set whose plan cannot be resolved is a hard failure, not a skip'.

fixed: planStems follows a symlinked plan HTML that resolves to a file; a dangling link throws.

B10-48unverifiablerecorded: fixedProtected-path and risk-glob matching is case-sensitive on Linux by default, and each call site picks its own case policy, so a case variant of a protected path or risk glob is not matched on a case-insensitive worktree.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength

Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.

Original problem and consequence

On a case-insensitive mount such as the owner's /mnt/d worktrees, a phase whose writes glob already covers the variant (for example writes ['**']) creates a file under a case variant of a protected directory, such as Core/Src/Config/x.ts against protected core/src/config/**. evaluatePathPolicy() reports no violation, enforce() passes, and the file lands in the protected directory. Separately, risk.paths is matched with the platform default and no case flag, so a Migrations/0001.sql change against migrations/** classifies T0 and passes risk_tier_sufficient at T0. The case flag is forced off only when a protected capability is present (line 129), so the ordinary path gets the weaker matching, and grant-plan.ts:54 matches case-insensitively, so the grant planner and the enforcer disagree. Simpler mechanism: one filesystem-derived case decision carried on PathPolicy and used by every matcher, or always case-insensitive matching for protection, which can only over-match.

B10-52unverifiablerecorded: fixedomittedEvidencePaths rebuilds and re-sorts the delivered-file list for every omitted-hunk marker in the diff, and observedDeliveredReads joins every delivered path against every read event, so both costs scale with the product of delivered files and markers or read events instead of being computed once.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

A review whose bounded diff carries R partial-file markers and F delivered files pays R sorts of F strings, which is O(R F log F). For each read event in the run, observedDeliveredReads performs F path joins, so a reviewer that opens every delivered file pays on the order of F squared joins. This repeats on every verdict. Code reading only; no probe was run. The cost is small per review but avoidable.

fixed: Sorts delivered paths once and pre-indexes joined read paths, preserving duplicate keys while avoiding repeated sorts and joins.

B10-53unverifiablerecorded: wontfix repository-relative validation must admit literal tracked tilde pathsnormalizeRepositoryPath inlines its own absolute-path test (startsWith('/') or a drive letter) instead of calling isAbsoluteMachinePath from config/machine-path.ts, which the config and catalog loaders use for the same concept; the narrower test lets home-relative spellings such as '~/notes.md' pass as repository-relative paths.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

An owner or agent supplies a --where or --read entry of '~/notes.md'. config/machine-path.ts isAbsoluteMachinePath refuses this spelling (it matches ~ as a machine path), so the config loader rejects the same string in awsf.config.yaml. normalizeRepositoryPath accepts it and returns '~/notes.md' as a repository path, so the write-boundary and protected-path checks evaluate a path that names a home-directory file. Git change sets never contain '~', so an out-of-worktree write made through shell expansion would not show up in the post-run path check. Impact is limited because git cannot record a literal '~' outside the worktree, but the validator now disagrees with the machine-path rule it is supposed to enforce.

Historical classification: cleanup · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/policy/path-policy.ts:47 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B10-53. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

wontfix repository-relative validation must admit literal tracked tilde paths: normalizeRepositoryPath validates Git-facing paths, where a literal top-level `~/notes.md` is valid and covered by a test. isAbsoluteMachinePath is for machine-local config values and intentionally interprets a leading tilde as machine-relative; applying it here would reject a legal tracked path.

Independent assessment

Current mechanism evidence

Original problem and consequence

Measured on the pattern at dashboard/shared/credential-patterns.ts:16: a 16,000-character run takes 797 ms in containsCredential and 1,038 ms in scrubCredentialString; a 32,000-character run takes 4,222 ms and 3,112 ms. The same length of ordinary prose takes about 2 ms and a 4,000-character run about 50 ms. A long hex or lowercase dump inside a persisted envelope or snapshot therefore stalls the scrub for seconds per call; by quadratic extrapolation a 96 KB run would take about 28 s (extrapolated, not measured). The trigger is an unbroken run of those characters, which ordinary prose and most source text do not contain.

Original problem and consequence

For a preserve-kind capability, noProtectedPaths (git-diff.ts:59-60) matches protected globs case-insensitively and exempts listed paths for purpose 'gate', while evaluatePathPolicy (path-policy.ts:129) uses the policy's own case setting (protectedWriteContext is non-null only for kind 'write') and exempts only for purpose 'write'. wontfix gate and write checks intentionally have different authority purposes: noProtectedPaths uses gate-purpose protected/preservation and plan-admission exemptions; evaluatePathPolicy accepts write authority only and calls protectedExemptionAllows with purpose `write`. A preserve capability is deliberately not write authority. Gate matching is fail-closed and can reject extra case variants; unifying these rules risks broadening runtime write authority or weakening the gate. No current bypass is reproduced.

B11-01resolvedrecorded: fixedparse() waits for stderr to close, with no bound, before it measures the exit or yields the held terminal, so a stderr pipe that stays open after stdout ends keeps a finished run from ever terminating.

Independent assessment

Both adapters await stderr through a bounded helper. Continuing to drain in the background avoids pipe-buffer deadlock.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/adapters/pi-codex.ts:794,818; core/src/adapters/claude-code.ts:606,631
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
A bounded wait does not prove that every descendant was killed. Process-tree cancellation is a separate mechanism.

Original problem and consequence

The provider writes its terminal (agent_settled) and closes stdout, so the decoder holds run.completed. A descendant that inherited the stderr descriptor keeps that pipe open. The await at L809 never resolves, so the held terminal is never yielded, and the 5 s exit bound in awaitExit (L726) is never reached because it runs after L809. parse() returns only when that descendant exits, and nothing in parse() bounds the wait. The exit promise resolves from the child 'exit' event (transport-broker.ts:757), which fires before stdio closes, so stderr closure is a separate condition and parse() waits on it without any bound. The same await appears at claude-code.ts:598 and :620 and stub.ts:236 and :243; those files are not analysed here.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: pi-codex parse() bounds the stderr wait on both paths via awaitStderr with the adapter's exit wait

B11-02resolvedrecorded: fixedwriteSystemPromptFile opens the prompt path with writeFile and then chmods it, and both follow a symlink already at that path, so a link planted in the provider-writable session runtime redirects the host's write, and its 0600 chmod, to an arbitrary file.

Independent assessment

The writer refuses symlinks and hard links, opens without truncation, validates the descriptor, then chmods and writes it. This fixes the reported prompt-slot overwrite.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/adapters/system-prompt-file.ts:46-103
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The named final-component and relaunch cases are covered. No native-Windows or arbitrary directory-rename adversary audit was performed.

Original problem and consequence

The phase runtime is bound writable into the provider sandbox (sandbox-broker.ts:180 and :348), so a write-capable agent (a managed-worker agent with Bash, or pi with bash or write) can create <runtime>/system-prompt.md as a symlink to a host file. production-run.ts:2369-2371 rewrites the prompt into that directory whenever the phase is launched without a saved result, and review-phase.ts:757 writes into its runtime unconditionally. So a phase resumed in the same attempt follows the link: writeFile truncates and writes the target as the AWSF user, and chmod sets the target to 0600. The containment check that would refuse a link (review-phase.ts:316-319, realpath outside the runtime) runs only after the write, from validateMaterializedSystemPrompt (called at review-phase.ts:758), so it reports E_REDACTION after the host file has already been overwritten. Reachability needs a write-capable agent and a re-entry into the same runtime directory. An lstat refusal, or an unlink followed by an exclusive create before the write, would close it.

B11-03resolvedrecorded: fixedparse() waits for stderr to close with no bound before it can yield the held terminal, while the exit wait is bounded; a stderr pipe kept open by a surviving descendant stalls the run's terminal indefinitely.

Independent assessment

Both adapters await stderr through a bounded helper. Continuing to drain in the background avoids pipe-buffer deadlock.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/adapters/pi-codex.ts:794,818; core/src/adapters/claude-code.ts:606,631
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
A bounded wait does not prove that every descendant was killed. Process-tree cancellation is a separate mechanism.

Original problem and consequence

After stdout ends, line 620 (await stderr.done) and line 598 on the error path wait on drainStderr's done promise (transport-loop.ts lines 60-89), which resolves only when stderr closes and has no timeout. If a process the provider CLI started inherits the stderr pipe and outlives it, stderr never closes and no terminal is yielded. The adapter's exit wait is bounded (awaitExit, transport-loop.ts lines 104-122, DEFAULT_EXIT_WAIT_MS 5000), so the two waits disagree. Probe: a run whose exit never resolves yields run.completed with exitCode null within the 50 ms test bound, but a run whose stderr never closes produced no terminal within 1500 ms. The production loop's silence timer (production-run.ts lines 2713-2719, re-armed per event at line 2791) is what eventually ends such a run, so the hang is bounded by the caller, not by the adapter, and the run's real outcome is replaced by a silence cancel. Low-to-medium.

Original problem and consequence

A rate_limit_event with status allowed_limit_reached takes the prefix exemption at line 442, because QUOTA_SHAPED (lines 569-570) only matches 'usage limit', 'rate limit', 'quota', or '<usage|plan|subscription|account> limit reached'. The normalized string 'allowed limit reached' matches none of them. The decoder emits only a quota observation and the run keeps going: the stream yields run.completed instead of E_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED. A phase therefore keeps issuing provider calls after its window reports the limit reached, and stops only when a later API call fails and #result maps that failure to E_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED. The comment at lines 433-438 says this shape must not be exempt. The only prefix test (core/test/unit/adapters/claude-code.test.ts lines 962-972) uses allowed_usage_limit_reached, which does match, so the gap is untested.

B11-09resolvedrecorded: not-reproduced drainStderr consumption bounded by awaitStderr in adapters; background drain must remain unbounded to avoid full-pipe deadlocksdrainStderr's done promise has no bound, so a descendant that outlives the provider and still holds its stderr pipe keeps parse() waiting after the provider's exit is already observed, which defeats the bounded awaitExit.

Independent assessment

Both adapters await stderr through a bounded helper. Continuing to drain in the background avoids pipe-buffer deadlock.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/adapters/pi-codex.ts:794,818; core/src/adapters/claude-code.ts:606,631
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
A bounded wait does not prove that every descendant was killed. Process-tree cancellation is a separate mechanism.

Original problem and consequence

The provider prints its result and exits 0 while a background descendant that inherited its stderr keeps running. stdout reaches EOF and transport.exit has resolved, but parse() is parked on the unbounded await stderr.done (claude-code.ts:620, stub.ts:243) before the exit is consulted, and that promise settles only when the descendant closes the pipe. Only an outer liveness trip (silence window or run timeout; liveness-monitor.ts #trip, which calls terminateTree) can end the stall, and it then records a silence or timeout outcome for a run whose provider had already completed. The awaitExit doc (transport-loop.ts:35-43) says a parser that never returns is worse than a terminal with no exit code, and this unbounded wait breaks that rule. Precondition: a descendant that inherited the provider's stderr and outlives it.

Historical classification: bug · medium · PLAUSIBLE. Original location: core/src/adapters/stream/transport-loop.ts:66 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B11-09. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

not-reproduced drainStderr consumption bounded by awaitStderr in adapters; background drain must remain unbounded to avoid full-pipe deadlocks: drainStderr must read to EOF to prevent child pipe-buffer stalls; bounded waiting is enforced at consumption via awaitStderr(drain, waitMs) (fixed in B11-01/B11-03 commit 90d0430); verified by transport-loop-b11-09.test.ts

B11-10unverifiablerecorded: fixedOptional JSON objects are guarded with === undefined only, so a JSON null reaches a property access and throws; one such line turns a successful run into run.failed.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence

Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Lines 299-300 do `const event = line.event; if (event === undefined) return [];`, and lines 306-307 do the same for delta. A provider line {"type":"stream_event","event":null} passes that guard and throws a TypeError at event.type (line 301). The same defect applies to an assistant line with content [null] (block.type at line 351) and to a user line with content [null] (line 371). The throw is caught by the parse catch (claude-code.ts:594-617), which records E_BACKEND_FAILURE and never decodes the lines after it, so a stream whose final result is a clean success ends as run.failed. The decoder's own rule, that a line it cannot read is a notice and never silently discarded (claude-code-stream.ts:142-143), is what this breaks.

fixed: Claude decoder reads a JSON null event, delta, or content block as absent instead of throwing.

B11-12unverifiablerecorded: fixedparse() substitutes the literal string "unknown-model" for a missing requestedModel, and the decoder journals that string as the requested model on run.started and model.resolved, so a caller that reaches the adapter through the public parse(transport, signal) method gets a model name the host never asked for.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

HarnessAdapter.parse (interface.ts:472) takes no options, so a caller that goes through the interface reaches claude-code.ts:563 with options = {}, and the sentinel is written into the journal. The probe run shows run.started and model.resolved with requestedModel "unknown-model" on a successful run. The sentinel matches REPRESENTABLE_IDENTITY (model-identity.ts:27), so no check rejects it, and the decoder does not compare it with the model the host requested. The same default is at pi-codex.ts:755. Latent: execute() always passes requestedModel (claude-code.ts:506, pi-codex.ts:697), and no production code calls an adapter's parse directly (the only callers are execute and the stub's own execute path), so the default is reached only by tests and any future direct caller. A refusal or a required option would match the adapters' refuse-rather-than-guess rule, since permissionArgs and selectorFor throw rather than substitute.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/adapters/claude-code.ts:563 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B11-12. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

fixed: Claude and pi parse() refuse with E_INVALID_REQUEST when no requested model is given, instead of journaling unknown-model.

B11-15unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe decoder's object guards test `=== undefined`, but JSON.parse yields null for an explicit null, so a valid line such as {"type":"turn_end","message":null} makes decode() throw a TypeError instead of emitting a notice.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A provider line whose message (or assistantMessageEvent) is null escapes decode(): L485 for turn_end, L308 for message_start, L368 for message_update, and L505 through #noteStop for message_end and error events. parse() catches the TypeError as a stream failure, so the run ends as run.failed E_BACKEND_FAILURE with the raw JS error text as its message. The rest of stdout is not decoded, and a real terminal that follows (agent_settled or a quota refusal) is lost. The decode contract at L185-187 says an unreadable line is recorded as a notice and never silently dropped; a throw is neither.

B11-16unverifiablerecorded: fixedRESET_IN_MINUTES has two adjacent unbounded whitespace quantifiers, so a long whitespace run after 'try again in' backtracks quadratically on the event loop when no minute count follows.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A quota-shaped refusal (it passes QUOTA_SHAPED, for example 'usage limit') whose text reads 'try again in', then a long run of spaces, then no digit, reaches #resetFrom (L571), which calls exec() on the full message. Probe probe-redos.mjs: 5,000 spaces take 45 ms, 10,000 take 177 ms, 20,000 take 665 ms, and 40,000 take 3,318 ms, so a 40 KB run stalls the decoder for about 3 s. The message length is provider-controlled (see the unbounded-text candidate). Bounded counts such as \s{0,8} make the match linear.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/adapters/pi-codex-stream.ts:707 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B11-16. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: The reset-time pattern has no adjacent whitespace quantifiers, so a long space run is read in linear time.

Original problem and consequence

The call at production-run.ts:2682 has no catch visible around it in the displayed block, so the correction path receives an unclassified TypeError instead of an E_BACKEND_FAILURE refusal. A file whose first line is not a session header is refused correctly, so only this shape is affected.

Independent assessment

Original problem and consequence

A refusal whose errorMessage is N MiB is stored with only a trim (pi-codex-stream.ts L509-510) and passed to fail() (L543-550), so the whole text is journaled as run.failed.message. output-budget.ts describes max_output_bytes as how much provider text a run may put into the journal, so this path breaks that bound. The tool-result path is bounded (summarize() caps at 400 characters), which makes the terminal path the outlier. Probe probe-unbounded.mjs with max_output_bytes=4096: a 1 MiB errorMessage yields run.failed with a 1048576-character message, while a 1 MiB text_delta is cut to 4096 characters.

fixed: Terminal, cancel, notice and quota text is capped at 4096 code units on a surrogate-safe cut.

B11-20unverifiablerecorded: fixedLineFramer keeps an unterminated line in #pending with no ceiling, and the decoders JSON.parse the whole line, so a single provider line that exceeds V8's maximum string length makes push() throw a RangeError that parse() reports as a generic E_BACKEND_FAILURE.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

The framer's own header says framing 'bounds nothing', and OutputBudget bounds only what is emitted (output-budget.ts header), so no stage caps one line's bytes. Once the pending line passes V8's maximum string size, `this.#pending += text` throws inside parse's try block (claude-code.ts:577-594). The catch maps it to E_BACKEND_FAILURE with the stream-failure text (claude-code.ts:613-615), so an oversize event is reported as a provider stream failure. Below that size the whole line is held in memory and JSON.parse'd (claude-code-stream.ts:140, pi-codex-stream.ts:183) before the budget applies. The threshold was not probed.

Historical classification: bug · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/adapters/stream/line-framer.ts:78 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B11-20. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: The framer caps one unterminated line at 32 Mi code units, so an oversized line no longer makes push() throw a RangeError.

B11-26unverifiablerecorded: fixedUsage that the stream reported on message_delta is never emitted when the stream's own result line carries no usage block, so a failed or quota-stopped Claude run loses the tokens of every API call it already made; the flush is decided by parse() control flow instead of inside the decoder that owns the double-count guard.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

Claude makes one or more API calls, so message_delta usage accumulates in #deltaUsage. Then either a result line arrives with is_error true and no usage block (the comment at lines 466-472 says an error result normally carries none), or a rate_limit_event ends the run through fail (lines 445-452), or a successful result carries no usage block. #result emits only the terminal, so no usage event exists for the run. parse() calls decoder.flushUsage() only on paths where no terminal was decoded (claude-code.ts:610 and claude-code.ts:631), so the deltas' tokens are dropped. Per-role token totals, which are summed from usage events, under-report every such run. flushUsage() called after the stream's own terminal is also a silent no-op, because EventSequencer.usage() returns NO_EVENTS once a terminal is set (event-sequencer.ts:327-328), so the parse-level call sites cannot emit for a stream-decoded terminal at all. The simpler general fix is for #result to emit the owed usage through flushUsage (which already guards on #usageReported) before its own terminal whenever the terminal carries none, so the rule lives in one place. Test gap: claude-code.test.ts:785-793 covers a terminal with no usage only when there was no prior message_delta, and the cancel test at lines 903-925 covers only the no-terminal path.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Flush accumulated Claude message-delta usage before any terminal lacking an authoritative usage block, including quota failures; retain the one-report guard.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

The same fact gets different evidence by route. A process that ends without a terminal and exits with code 3 is recorded by the Claude route as 'the process exited with code 3; the provider wrote to stderr: boom', but by the pi route as 'the provider's stream ended without a terminal event; the provider wrote to stderr: boom', so the exit code that the transport headers call measured truth is lost from pi-route evidence. No test pins pi's wording: pi-codex.test.ts:654 and :1062 assert only the errorCode. The copies are the same code in three files: the parse() loops at stub.ts:205-252, claude-code.ts:549-647 and pi-codex.ts:741-831; isCancellation, cancellationReason and describe are identical in stub.ts:316-340, claude-code.ts:660-682 and pi-codex.ts:834-856; #settleHeld is identical in claude-code.ts:530-536 and pi-codex.ts:722-728; and execute()'s session copy-back is in claude-code.ts:490-514 and pi-codex.ts:676-706. The exit patch is a symptom: the decoders hard-code complete(null) (claude-code-stream.ts:486, pi-codex-stream.ts:541), the Claude decoder comment at claude-code-stream.ts:478-485 still describes the exit-await shape change as pending, and the adapters rewrite the minted terminal instead. The transport-loop.ts header says two copies of a pipe rule are two places for it to be subtly wrong. Simpler general fix: one driver in transport-loop.ts that awaits the exit before the terminal is minted (sequencer.complete(exitCode)), used by all three parse() methods, with execute() sharing the copy-back.

Original problem and consequence

A 1-byte PNG delivered as data 'QQ==' is reported by redactToolImages as bytes 3. That redacted value is what summarize() writes into the snippet at claude-code-stream.ts:380 and pi-codex-stream.ts:627. toolResultImages reports bytes 1 for the same payload, and that figure goes into ObservedToolImage.bytes. A 2-byte payload 'QUI=' gives 3 versus 2. The doc at tool-images.ts:74 promises the 'decoded size'. The unit test at image-tool-results.test.ts:61 pins only the unpadded 'AAAA' (3 bytes), so padded payloads are untested. B11-32unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe Claude decoder keeps its own #openTools set that mirrors the EventSequencer's open-tool map, which already dedupes and tracks the same ids; the decoder cannot query the sequencer by id, so it keeps a second source of truth. pi-codex-stream.ts:148 does the same.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

The two sets are updated at different points: the decoder adds the id (claude-code-stream.ts:353) before calling toolRequested, which can refuse under the event budget and return nothing, while the sequencer keeps no entry. After such a refusal the decoder believes the call is open and the sequencer does not. Today nothing visible results only because OutputBudget.offer() latches the cap, so the later 'settled a tool call the host never opened' notice is dropped as well; that masking is accidental, not designed. Cost: duplicated bookkeeping in two decoders that must stay in sync with the sequencer's rules. Simpler form: add hasOpenTool(providerToolId) to EventSequencer (its toolRequested already returns no event for an open id, event-sequencer.ts:270), and let both decoders ask it instead of keeping #openTools.

Original problem and consequence

PERMISSION_PROFILE_NAMES (policy/permission-profiles.ts:3) is the policy list, and resolvePermissionProfile validates against it (permission-profiles.ts:43-45). The adapters call it only when configuredTools is set (claude-code.ts:137-139, pi-codex.ts:207-209). Otherwise each adapter's own switch default (claude-code.ts:190-196, pi-codex.ts:220-226) is the only validator. A profile added to the policy list is therefore accepted by resolvePermissionProfile and then refused by both adapters with E_INVALID_REQUEST until their own lists change too. The gate-execute literal (claude-code.ts:127, pi-codex.ts:183) is not in the policy vocabulary at all, and the identical host-only refusal block is written twice (claude-code.ts:130-136, pi-codex.ts:200-206). PI_READONLY_TOOLS (pi-codex.ts:155) re-declares the readonly ceiling PROFILE_CEILINGS.readonly (permission-profiles.ts:12), which is not exported, so the pi read-only tool list can drift from the policy ceiling.

Original problem and consequence

A future change to the rule (for example comparing costUsd, relaxing the model comparison for route-attributed identities, or changing one code) lands in one adapter and not the other, and the two routes then accept different corrections for the same pair of records. The copies are visible by comparison: claude-code.ts:281-298 and pi-codex.ts:381-398 each check resolvedModel first with E_MODEL_MISMATCH, then sessionId null or unequal with E_BACKEND_FAILURE, differing only in the adapter constant. Both adapter wrappers (claude-code.ts:483-488 and pi-codex.ts:669-674) only reshape records to call their copy. Simpler general fix: one assertSameSessionRecord(adapterId, first, next) in interface.ts, which already owns ContinuityCapableAdapter and isContinuityCapable, with both routes delegating to it. Both copies are pinned by their own tests (claude-code.test.ts:685-704 and pi-codex.test.ts:774-793), so nothing checks that the two agree.

B11-36unverifiablerecorded: wontfix cumulative snapshot behavior is inferred and no lean mode is evidencedEach pi message_update line carries the whole accumulated assistant message twice, and the decoder parses all of it while reading only the delta text, so stream cost grows with the square of the answer length.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

The captured fixture core/test/fixtures/providers/codex/probe-readonly-tool.jsonl has six message_update lines, and all six carry assistantMessageEvent.partial; the text_delta line also repeats the message at top level. The decoder reads neither snapshot (the PiLine type at lines 81-92 has no partial field) and takes text from event.delta (line 371). Each line is still parsed in full (JSON.parse at line 183). If the snapshot grows with the answer, a 60 KB answer streamed as 3000 deltas of 20 characters moves about 174 MiB of JSON through the parser for 0.3 MiB of text. Measured on the real PiStreamDecoder, timed around decode() only: 529 ms with the snapshots against 19 ms with delta-only lines, and 106 ms against 13 ms at 1000 deltas. Real deltas may be smaller than 20 characters, which would raise the cost further. Cheaper alternative: extract the delta without parsing the partial and message subtrees, or ask pi for a leaner output if the installed CLI offers one. I did not confirm that such an option exists; the owner's specs reference only --mode json. Caveat: the capture holds a single text delta, so the cumulative content of longer snapshots is inferred from the field's meaning, not captured.

Original problem and consequence

'billing details required', 'insufficient_quota' and 'out of budget' end a pi run as E_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED (pi-codex-stream.ts:704 matches billing, insufficient_quota and out of budget) but end a Claude run as E_BACKEND_FAILURE, while 'rate limit exceeded' ends a Claude run as E_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED (claude-code-stream.ts:570 matches rate limit) but ends a pi run as E_BACKEND_FAILURE. Quota-shaped text ends the phase with a quota event rather than a backend failure, so which copy a route carries decides whether the phase is lost. The comment at pi-codex-stream.ts:679-680 says the first alternation is carried unchanged from the Claude rule, which is no longer true. The rate-limit removal is documented at pi-codex-stream.ts:693-697, but the added terms are not reconciled with the Claude copy. The reuse fix is one host rule in stream/ with a route-scoped extension, imported by both decoders.

B11-38unverifiablerecorded: wontfix measured low cost preserves full diagnostic countassertResumable reads and fully parses every session file in the host store, synchronously, on every correction, including files whose session id does not match.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength

Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost

Original problem and consequence

readPiSessionFile reads each file in full (line 337), including files whose header id does not match, which the first line alone could reject. Before the header is checked it also JSON-parses every line. assertResumable calls it for every .jsonl in the store (line 579), so a correction re-reads each transcript on the event loop. The checks need only the header line and a count of assistant turns. Measured on the real adapter with one session file: 1 MiB 20 ms, 5 MiB 58 ms, 20 MiB 292 ms (21,226 assistant turns). The magnitude is low, because corrections are rare and typical sessions are small. Cheaper alternative: read a bounded prefix for the header, and stop the turn count at the first assistant turn if only presence matters; the detail string currently reports the full count, so that wording would change too.

B11-40unverifiablerecorded: wontfix bounded custom serialization risks output compatibilitysummarize() serializes the whole tool input or result to JSON before it keeps 400 characters, so every large tool payload costs an extra full pass.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

For any non-string value, summarize() builds the whole JSON string on line 20 and only then slices it to SNIPPET_LIMIT on line 21. Callers pass whole payloads: claude-code-stream.ts line 359 (inputSummary: summarize(block.input), for example a Write tool's full file content), line 380 (resultSnippet: summarize(redactToolImages(block.content)), an array of text blocks), and pi-codex-stream.ts line 431 for tool arguments. Measured through the real Claude decoder: a 4 MB array-content tool result decodes in 32.0 ms against 10.9 ms for JSON.parse of the same line, so summarizing adds about 21 ms. summarize() alone on a 4 MB Write-style input takes 17.6 ms, against 0.07 ms for a bounded serializer that stops once its 400-character budget is spent. The magnitude is modest and is paid per large payload. The Codex result path does not show the cost (decode 10.3 ms against parse 8.7 ms), so this claim covers the Claude result path and tool inputs on both routes. Cheaper alternative: a serializer that stops at the budget, for example a JSON.stringify replacer that aborts once 400 characters have been produced.

B11-42unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe env allowlist is applied inside each adapter's buildSpec rather than at the spawn point, and the stub's buildSpec forwards the caller's whole environment, so the invariant holds only because each production adapter remembers to call filterEnv.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

StubAdapter.buildSpec returns env: request.env (stub.ts:187) with no filterEnv, while ClaudeCodeAdapter.buildSpec (claude-code.ts:469) and PiCodexAdapter.buildSpec (pi-codex.ts:652) both call filterEnv. The broker copies whatever spec.env says (transport-broker.ts:615, env: { ...spec.env }) and does not filter it. Probe E: the stub spec's env keys are PATH, HOME and SECRET_TOKEN, while the Claude spec's keys are PATH, HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, TZ, NO_COLOR and TERM. Reach is limited: registry.ts:32-34 returns null for kind fixture, so the stub is test-only and the realistic impact is a test child seeing an ambient secret. The altitude point is where the rule lives: a new adapter that omits filterEnv leaks the same way, and adapter-fence.test.ts checks only child_process and fetch, so nothing catches it. Simpler general fix: apply the allowlist once at the broker, keyed by registration.adapterId, which is idempotent for the existing routes.

Original problem and consequence

A Claude tool result whose content is an array of text blocks is shown in the journal as the JSON scaffolding of that array (type text, the text field, brackets and braces) instead of the answer. The array form is confirmed for image results (derived-image-read-tool.jsonl), so array-form text is plausible but not captured.

B11-45unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe Claude quota reset parser falls back to returning the raw text after 'reset' when no epoch form matches, which contradicts the function's own documented contract that unmatched input stays null, and lets a non-timestamp reach the quota event's resetAt.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

An error text such as 'Claude AI usage limit reached. resets 5pm (Europe/Madrid)' yields quota.resetAt '5pm (Europe/Madrid)'. The schema (normalized-events.ts:186) accepts any non-empty string, so nothing rejects it. The file's own comment at lines 586-596 says a non-timestamp reset makes Date.parse return NaN for anything scheduling a resume, and the provider-side quota parser (quota/parse.ts:130-132) faults on a resetsAt that is not an instant. The raw-text fallback re-admits the non-timestamp shape that the regex-group fix removed. Simpler general fix: return the epoch-derived ISO form or null, and recognize only the reset forms the CLI actually emits. Confidence is medium: the behaviour is probed, but whether the live CLI prints zoned or relative resets is not captured.

ELI B11 · Connecting AWSF to AI tools

These connectors send requests to AI tools and collect their replies. The checked repairs stop a prompt-file link from redirecting a write to another file and limit how long the connector waits for error output after a tool exits. That addresses the specific overwrite and hanging cases reviewed here. It does not prove every operating system or every possible file-access race is safe.

Carried scoped judgments: 4 of 45 findings. The other 41 remain unverified. No new connector mechanism audit is claimed.

B12-01resolvedrecorded: fixedclosureReadout matches a closure record only when every sealed ticket is in record.tickets, but closeCommand writes record.tickets from the closable subset only, so a partial-shift closure (an unbuilt ticket recorded in notClosable) never reads back as closed.

Independent assessment

A closure record covers built tickets plus not-closable tickets and can read as open by choice, instead of being treated as missing.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
core/src/closure/model.ts:33-54
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Semantic closure is distinct from completing every ticket. The owner still decides which offered rows earned completion.

Original problem and consequence

Post-cut partial shift: the sealed selection is T01,T02 and only T01 has a host-recorded build. `awsf close <task> --project P --attempt N` offers the T01 rows and writes a closure-record with tickets [T01] and notClosable [T02] (close.ts:226 tickets: [...primary.tickets]; close.ts:230 notClosable). readTailClosure (closure/readout.ts:19-20) and the callers that use it return state 'not closed' with record null. unclosedLandings (closure/model.ts:34-36) keeps the attempt, so preflight evaluateClosure (preflight/fields.ts:587-588) blocks every run with the advice 'owner closes it with awsf close ...'. Rerunning close takes the completed branch (close.ts:119-126) and returns confirmed:true without changing the readout, and next-steps keeps offering close (lifecycle/next-steps.ts:160). The notClosable arm of closureReadout (model.ts:30) can never be reached by a matching record, because a notClosable ticket is by construction absent from record.tickets. Owner-commit mode has the same mismatch for any sealed ticket with no checked row, because its primary.tickets filter drops it.

B12-02unverifiablerecorded: fixedprojectedCost joins session task ids against plan-qualified uids (plan-aware path) or a synthesized plan-dir/id key (legacy path), but every session task_id is a bare path-safe id, so the join never matches and projected cost is always reported as unavailable.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.

Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Removed behavior: commit 2fb0bc6 replaced the bare-id join (const ticketIds = new Set(tickets.map((ticket) => ticket.id)) matched with ticketIds.has(session.taskId)) by a uid join. The replacement is dead for real data. The legacy queryBacklog caller (line 153) builds the key plan-dir/Tnn, which contains a slash, and no current session task_id can contain a slash: every task id passes validateComponent (attempt.ts:242 regex ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$, invoked at attempt.ts:425 through taskRoot). The plan-aware caller (line 128) gets its sessions from api/routes.ts:560-562, which maps only row.task_id and drops sessions.plan_ref, so its uids never match a bare session id either. Result: awsf backlog (cli/commands/backlog.ts:13, reached from cli/main.ts:366) and GET /api/v1/tickets report projectedCost {usd: null, authority: unavailable, partial: true} even when every ticket has one single-authority session cost. Probe: tickets T01 and T02 with provider costs 1.5 and 2.5 give unavailable on the current code, while the pre-2fb0bc6 join reconstructed from the removed lines gives usd 4, provider, partial false. The existing tests do not catch it: backlog.test.ts:44 uses mixed authorities (provider and catalog-estimate) and backlog.test.ts:98 uses colliding bare ids, so both expect unavailable for reasons unrelated to the key. Invariant context: none of AGENTS.md 1, 2, 12 is breached; this is a silent wrong output in the planning dashboard and CLI readout.

fixed: projectedCost accommodates bare task ids, qualified uids, and slash suffixes while refusing bare collisions.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only

The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
