Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A post-cut attempt is landed with a ticket selection and then published before the owner closes it. LANDED to PUBLISHED seals the attempt (cli/commands/publish.ts:84-97 and :200-203). gatherLandingClosures admits PUBLISHED (closure/readout.ts:56) and landingJournalTail admits PUBLISHED successors (persistence/closure-tail.ts:31), so unclosedLandings (closure/model.ts:34-36) lists the attempt and evaluateClosure (preflight/fields.ts:587-588) blocks with 'owner closes it with awsf close <task> --project <p> --attempt <n>'. That command is refused at close.ts:78 with E_CLOSURE_NOT_LANDED. The completed and interrupted-intent recovery branches (close.ts:119 onward) come after that refusal, so an interrupted closure on an attempt that has since been published can never be finished through the attempt route. The only working route is the owner-commit form `awsf close --commit <sha> --plan <stem>` (cli/main.ts around lines 754-771), and the advice never names it. Preflight stays blocked with advice that cannot succeed.

Original problem and consequence

A project with no tasks directory yet (for example, before any attempt has run under it) has an owner-accepted unit with a valid contract-null acceptance. Line 45 (readdir with no ENOENT handling) throws; the catch at lines 144-147 sets delivery to unknown and adds 'evidence lookup incomplete'; the owner-accepted branch at lines 128-133 never runs, so the accepted unit is not shown as done. The same unit with a tasks directory but no directory for its task returns [] at line 46 and reaches the branch, showing done. A task directory with no attempt subdirectories throws at line 51 and shows unknown. Probe (probe-owner-accepted.mjs): no-tasks-root gives unknown, tasks-root-no-task-dir gives done, task-dir-no-attempts gives unknown.

Original problem and consequence

Owner accepts unit U1 at revision 1 for contract C with evidence E (acceptance A1). E then changes, so verification fails with 'stale evidence reference'. The owner re-accepts U1 at revision 1 for contract C with the new evidence (acceptance A2). applyChanges (model.ts:244-251) appends the second acceptance, and neither validateGraph nor applyChanges rejects a duplicate (unit, revision, contract). Line 161 still returns A1, lines 163-165 verify A1 and fail, so satisfied is false, line 167 adds 'blocked prerequisite: interface U1@1: C', and line 169 turns a todo row for U2 into 'blocked'. Probe (probe-acceptance.mjs, under the B12-A1 probe directory): stale-then-fresh yields the blocked prerequisite condition, fresh-then-stale yields none, fresh-only yields none, and stale-only yields the block. The outcome depends on array order, not on which evidence is current.

B12-13unverifiablerecorded: fixedA project that is registered but has no workflow session (S2 done, S3 not started) resolves to 'before S1' with owner command 'awsf init', because registration is session-less and resolveStage receives only the project slug.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

The owner runs awsf project register, which writes a placement. stage.ts reads that placement before resolving (`const placement = await readPlacement(input.stateRoot, catalog.project.slug);`), so the project is registered. No design-to-plan session exists yet. resolveStage returns {current: 'before S1', next: 'init', ownerAct: 'awsf init'}, and the renderer prints 'not started; owner types: awsf init'. That tells the owner to run a command whose precondition (an empty or absent target path) is false for a registered repository, and never names the real next act, awsf new --workflow design-to-plan. The project register command is session-less and not stored, so the journal can never show S2 complete. The 'before S1' answer is reachable only for a registered project, because readPlacement throws ENOENT before resolveStage runs for an unregistered one. The spec's acceptance line 'no session at all resolves to before S1' was written for the unregistered case, so it does not cover this path.

Original problem and consequence

A design-to-plan attempt ends BLOCKED after a failed planner phase, so no valid document-output envelope exists. Journal rows: one session design-to-plan BLOCKED, one FAILED phase, zero envelopes. resolveStage returns {current: 'design-to-plan', next: 'build', ownerAct: 'awsf new --workflow plan-build-test', evidence: null}. The renderer in core/src/cli/commands/stage.ts then prints 'stopped - design-to-plan is complete; nothing advances this; owner types: awsf new --workflow plan-build-test' next to 'evidence: none recorded'. The owner is sent to a build whose entry precondition (the S3 plan on the default branch) is not met, and the readout calls a stage complete that has no evidence. The same path applies to a build session that is BLOCKED before a valid test-output envelope exists, which advises 'awsf publish'. The spec (specs/awsf-v2-w11-five-stage-ladder.html) makes evidence the basis of the current stage: the evidence 'establishes the current stage'. resolve.test.ts rowsFor() builds every stage session with the default lifecycle AWAITING_OWNER (lines 19 and 125), so no test covers a stage session that did not complete.

Original problem and consequence

An owner's first input line is longer than 180 UTF-16 units and has a supplementary-plane character (for example an emoji) straddling indices 178-179. slice(0, TITLE_BUDGET - 1) keeps the high surrogate and drops the low one, so the title ends in an invalid half-character followed by an ellipsis, which renders as a replacement glyph. Original problem and consequence

AGENTS.md invariant 12: 'A ticket set whose plan cannot be resolved is a hard failure, not a skip.' Input: a group unit whose plan reference names a stem and task T05, where the plan HTML was renamed or its placement is missing, so resolvePlanSources returns no source. registeredPlan throws 'registered plan source unresolved' at line 78; the catch at lines 144-146 sets delivery to 'unknown' and appends 'evidence lookup incomplete: refresh execution and source references'; checklist() returns normally. A landed unit never reaches its done branch (line 126 runs after the call at line 116), and the owner is told to refresh execution instead of being told the plan is unresolved. A ticket in state done over an unchecked plan box throws 'registered plan/ticket status mismatch' at line 98, and the regex on line 145 maps that to 'stale' because the message contains 'mismatch'. The view is read-only, so the damage is a misreported unit rather than a wrong landing, but the hard failure the invariant requires does not occur on this path.

B12-23unverifiablerecorded: fixedEvidence is ordered by phase ordinal before time, but the ordinal is unique only within one session (UNIQUE (session_id, ordinal)), so the chosen evidence can come from an older session.

Original problem and consequence

Two design-to-plan sessions each hold a valid document-output envelope. The older session's envelope sits at phase ordinal 6 and the newer one at ordinal 2, which can happen if the recipe's phase layout changes between attempts. compareEvidence sorts by ordinal first, so the older session's phase is returned as the evidence. The probe returned phaseId 'ph-a' when the newer session's phase is 'ph-b'. The displayed readout shows only the schema id, so the impact is limited to evidence.phaseId, which is the field that names the phase the stage rests on. Fix: order by envelope created_at (or session started_at) first, then by phase ordinal within a session.

Lines 50-57 loop over every registered plan, prompts file, ticket and light ticket and call runGit(git, ["cat-file", "blob", blob]) for each. runGit (git/changes.ts:37-41) calls the runner synchronously and returns its stdout, so each registered file costs one process spawn. cli/commands/close.ts:145-146 builds two snapshots (base and head), so a close run pays about two times P spawns, where P is the number of registered paths. Unchanged files share blob ids across the two snapshots (the blobs map at lines 35-36 records them), so a per-blob cache would skip their repeated spawns. Cheaper alternative: one git cat-file --batch process per snapshot, or a cache keyed by blob id. Outside the B12 target list; reported because it produces the trees that closure/delta.ts and closure/asked-for.ts consume.

GET /groups (api/routes.ts:574) runs listGroupSummaries (api/planning-route.ts:35-37), which calls readGroupTree for each group id. readGroupTree replays the whole group journal (views.ts:396), and replay reduces every event with a full structuredClone (model.ts:279). decisionTree then copies every input's full text into asks (views.ts:336) and copies the first input again as title.full (views.ts:362), while firstLine (views.ts:278-281) splits the entire first input into lines only to read its first non-empty line. groupSummary (views.ts:400-405) keeps just group, project, revision, closed, the title text, at and counts. Each request therefore costs groups times events times accumulated input bytes, rebuilt from scratch, and most of that work is discarded. Cheaper alternative: a summary projector that replays once and keeps only the summary fields, cached by group.head (which changes with every event), and dropping the duplicate title.full, which equals asks[0].text.

fixed: Added a summary-only replay projection and routed the groups list through it; planning.test.ts checks parity with the tree-derived summary.

Original problem and consequence

The closure locates the single `state` scalar with its own regex (light: `/^---\r?\n([\s\S]*?)\r?\n---\r?\n([\s\S]*)$/`, plan: `/^---\n...`). The store's parseStoredTicket uses the same light regex through splitFrontmatter (ticket-store.ts:50), and plan-ticket-body uses the non-CRLF regex. If the store's split is ever tightened or loosened (for example to refuse CRLF), the closure can rewrite a state span in a file that the store parses differently, so a closure could mark a ticket done that the store reads as invalid. Reusing one splitter for both offset computation and parsing removes that risk.

The doctor probe hand-writes a second argv: `--die-with-parent --ro-bind / / --proc /proc --dev /dev --setenv QUOTA_AXI_CODEX_BINARY /dev/null -- <exe> <argv>`. If bwrapSpec later adds a mount or namespace restriction (for example an unshare or env-clear flag), the doctor probe keeps the older profile, and a change to the sandbox argv would not be seen by the quota probe. This is a reuse gap against the sandbox owner module, not a demonstrated escape: I did not read bwrapSpec's full argv to confirm which flags differ, so the divergence is unverified.

wontfix the doctor quota probe is not a sandboxed build launch: quota/probe.ts owns a dedicated read-only bwrap profile and environment contract; replacing it with the general launch builder changes isolation without a demonstrated probe defect.

B12-44unverifiablerecorded: wontfix replacing the current stale delivery result with typed classifications broadens the readout error contract without fixing a demonstrated landing decisionThe checklist assigns each row's delivery state by testing the thrown message against /stale|changed|concurrent|mismatch/, so plan/ticket disagreements and unresolved plans land in different states with the same refresh advice.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

A plan/ticket disagreement thrown as 'registered plan/ticket status mismatch' (evidence.ts:98) or 'registered plan/ticket compatibility mismatch' (evidence.ts:92) becomes delivery 'stale', while 'registered plan source unresolved' (evidence.ts:78) becomes 'unknown'. All of them get the condition 'evidence lookup incomplete: refresh execution and source references' (evidence.ts:146), which cannot repair a ticket that disagrees with its plan; invariant 12 treats that disagreement as a hard failure, not a skip. The state depends on substrings of prose rather than on the error's kind. B12-45unverifiablerecorded: wontfix changing reduceEvent from an immutable reducer to a mutable replay accumulator would alter the replay ownership boundaryreduceEvent deep-clones the whole accumulated group for every event, so replaying a group journal copies a growing state once per event.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

The replay loop in store.ts (lines 94-109) calls reduceEvent once per journal record, and reduceEvent starts with a full structuredClone of the group (line 279). The copy includes every captured input's full text (schema.ts:43 admits up to 1,048,576 characters each), every stage narrative, every proposal and every unit record. The total copy volume is the sum of the prefix sizes, so E events cost on the order of E squared times the average event size, and propose and apply events clone a second time inside applyChanges (line 210). append (store.ts:142) replays the whole journal under the group lock before every write, and readGroupTree replays it before every read, so the quadratic cost is paid on every write and every read. Cheaper alternative: clone once per replay and reduce into that single owned accumulator, keeping a copy only where append needs the prior state for its checks.

Historical classification: cleanup · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: core/src/planning/model.ts:279 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B12-45. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

wontfix changing reduceEvent from an immutable reducer to a mutable replay accumulator would alter the replay ownership boundary: planning/model.ts clones reducer input; the finding shows possible cost, not incorrect output, and realistic groups have few events.

B12-46unverifiablerecorded: wontfix the digest domains have incompatible canonicalization contractsplanning/store.ts canonical() is byte-identical to the exported canonicalJson in contracts/owner-amendment.ts, and closure/asked-for.ts stable() is a third copy with different undefined handling.

Independent assessment

Current mechanism evidence

Original problem and consequence

Three canonical-JSON implementations exist. planning/store.ts canonical() feeds journal event digests (eventHash), proposalHash and the packet hash, while contracts/owner-amendment.ts canonicalJson feeds the owner-amendment, attribution and command-ledger digests. The two produce the same bytes today, but nothing ties them together: if one is changed (for example a number or key-order rule), planning digests and contract digests silently diverge, and the closure's asked-for comparison (stable) can call two equal values different when one side is undefined. Reusing canonicalJson removes the duplicate; stable() needs its own undefined rule, which should be a parameter, not a copy.

routes.ts:488 loads the session row with `const session = requireSession(readDb, sessionId);` and routes.ts:517 sets `usage: usage(session),`, so every phase response carries the run-wide totals. The phase drawer is mounted live (App.vue:258 mounts SessionRoute, SessionRoute.vue:60 mounts PhaseDetailDrawer, PhaseDetailDrawer.vue:30 mounts PhaseInspector), and its 'usage' section prints total tokens, input / output and cost straight from detail.usage with no phase filter (PhaseInspector.vue:100-102). Opening the builder phase of a multi-phase run therefore shows the whole run's spend as that phase's spend, so a cheap phase reads as the largest consumer. The gates and processes in the same response are phase-scoped (routes.ts:516 and 519), and the contract PhaseDetailResponse.usage: UsageTotals (dashboard/shared/types.ts:379) has no scope note, which is why the mismatch only shows across files. routes.test.ts:212-222 asserts phase identity and envelopes but not usage, so no test pins the behavior. Event rows carry phase_id and per-event token columns (EventItem, types.ts:384-406), so a phase-scoped total is derivable; otherwise the section must be relabelled as run totals.

fixed: phaseDetailResponse computes phase-scoped usage from phase events rather than whole-session totals.

B13-11unverifiablerecorded: fixedretainedPins drops every stored position whose node is missing from the graph it receives, but CanvasMap passes it the kind-filtered graph, so the saved arrangement of a hidden kind is erased from localStorage the next time any dot is dropped.

Original problem and consequence

The reader drags run dots (saved under awsf.canvas-layout), then turns the runs kind off. canvas.vue:68 filterGraph removes every run node, and CanvasMap.vue:68 computes pins = retainedPins(props.graph, props.pinned) against that filtered graph, so the run pins are dropped. The reader then drags a plan dot: CanvasMap.vue:197 emits new Map([...pins.value, [plan, dropped]]), and keepPins (canvas.vue:82-84) writes that map over the stored layout. Turning runs back on re-settles every run dot from the deterministic start, and the arrangement is gone after a reload as well. Probe with the real modules: 'run pin after re-enabling runs: lost', while retaining against the full graph keeps it. The retainedPins contract is to drop only nodes the projection no longer has (archived tasks, renamed groups), and filterGraph documents a kind switch as a filter that takes dots off the map (canvas-view.ts:114-122), not as a removal of the runs themselves.

Original problem and consequence

routes.ts:308-313 gives hints for DRAFT, PREPARED, AWAITING_OWNER and the running states, and falls through to `return [];` for every other state, including LANDED. The canonical table allows a human to publish from LANDED (task-machine.ts:122), and nextSteps() (core/src/lifecycle/next-steps.ts:126-165) walks the legal edges from the current state and emits the publish step with who owner for LANDED (publish is in OWNER_ACT_COMMANDS, next-steps.ts:7). So SessionDetailResponse.allowedNextActions (routes.ts:481) reports no next action for a landed run that the owner can publish. The impact is low: no file under dashboard/src reads allowedNextActions and no test covers it, so nothing visible breaks today. The fix is to derive the hint from nextSteps() instead of keeping a second table, which is the duplication that let the two diverge.

B13-18unverifiablerecorded: fixedverdicts() treats a zero-cost route as an overkill comparator and divides by its zero x, so a verdict can read 'costs NaN× less' or 'costs Infinity× less' and can flag two equal-cost routes as overkill of each other.

Original problem and consequence

A route whose rows report zero (non-null) token usage is priced at 0 by rate-card.ts, because priceRow returns no-usage only when every token kind is null, so its listPerRow is 0. The overkill test other.x * 1.5 <= point.x is then true for x = 0 against any point, and the ratio on line 677 is 0/0 = NaN or n/0 = Infinity. With two zero-cost routes each is flagged as an overkill candidate of the other, which is false. The degenerate ratio is written into the verdict text the owner reads as a recommendation.

Original problem and consequence

The URL #/metrics?view=ledger&cols=bogus (or cols=) parses to families [] and the ledger built from it has no metric columns: visibleColumns([]) returns nothing (metrics-ledger.ts:206-208), so the headers hold only the row-count header and every family pill in MetricsLedger.vue:53-62 is unpressed. The owner can recover by clicking a pill, so the cost is a degraded, unexplained ledger rather than lost data. Severity low.

Original problem and consequence

A hand-edited or truncated hash such as #/backlog/%E0%A4%A reaches App.vue:140; decodeURIComponent throws URIError: URI malformed and readRoute aborts there, so canvasRoute, metricsRoute, groupsRoute and selectedId keep their previous values and load() is never reached (App.vue:159). If the page loads with such a hash, onMounted aborts before addEventListener('hashchange') (App.vue:160), so later navigation is ignored until a reload with a well-formed hash; a malformed hash reached after load aborts only that one update. The same bare call at App.vue:153, 156 and 157, and at canvas-view.ts:84 inside parseCanvasRoute (called from readRoute at App.vue:146), fails the same way for group, session and canvas hashes. Fix caution: metrics-lens.ts safeDecode also rewrites '+' to a space, which these sites do not do, so calling it verbatim would change any id that contains '+'; export a non-throwing decode that keeps '+'.

B13-29unverifiablerecorded: fixedEvery poll replaces the whole sessions payload with a new object, so the identity-keyed watchers in routes/canvas.vue re-fetch the full ticket set while a plan node is open and a continuation run's event log while that run is shown, once per poll.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

With a plan node open, each poll (every 500 ms in live mode, 2 s in grid mode) issues GET /api/v1/tickets, which returns the full ticket set. openedPlan is a find() over props.plans, App.vue hands that array down as a new object on every poll, and canvas.vue:207 watches the result by identity, so it fires every time. With a continuation chain open, each poll issues GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>/events, because middle and relation are recomputed from the fresh props.sessions (canvas.vue:120-131) and canvas.vue:143 watches them by identity. The reason line also blanks to its fallback text on every one of those round trips, because canvas.vue:144 clears it before the fetch and canvas.vue:354-355 shows the fallback while it is null. Cheaper alternative: keep the previous sessions object when the new payload serialises identically (structural sharing at App.vue:213), and key the canvas.vue watchers on primitives (openedPlan id, middle sessionId, relation kind) so they fire only on a real change.

Historical classification: cleanup · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: dashboard/src/App.vue:213 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B13-29. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Reuse unchanged session and plan collection arrays across polls to prevent identity-driven re-fetches.

Original problem and consequence

settle() calls stepSimulation 260 times on an unchanging graph (canvas-layout.ts:350), and each call runs replayFamilies (lines 68-78: a clusters.find, an edges.find and an edges.filter per pair node) plus the replayIds set and the ids array (lines 167-170). Probe layout-probe.mjs on a 57-node synthetic graph with 12 replay pairs: the replay-only settle takes 24.4 ms, of which the prelude is 0.071 ms per step, about 18 ms, so most of that settle is recomputing the same structure. layoutGraph totals 40 to 52 ms over two runs. The drag path is cheap: a 3-step settle is 0.6 ms per pointer move (CanvasMap.vue:180). Cheaper alternative: compute families, replayIds and ids once per settle and pass them into a step that takes them as arguments.

Independent assessment

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.

Original problem and consequence

EventLog.vue:19 recomputes foldTextDeltaRuns over the phase's whole event list whenever that list changes, and EventLog.vue polls every second (EventLog.vue:50), so a streaming run is folded again on each poll that adds chunks. Probe on a 5,000-chunk run (218,890 characters): one fold takes 14.3 ms, of which the credential scrub is 9.0 ms, and folding again after each 200-chunk page costs 187 ms across a 25-page stream, against 14 ms for a single fold of the finished run. A completed run is immutable, so its folded row can be memoised by first and last event id, with only the trailing open run re-folded. Redaction still runs on every text the fold emits, so the credential scrub is not weakened.

B13-39unverifiablerecorded: fixedsummarizeNotice joins code and message with a middle dot and then rewrites the first ' · ' to ': ', so a message that itself contains ' · ' is altered whenever no code is present; joining the non-empty parts with ': ' does the same job without the string rewrite.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

A notice whose payload is {message: 'disk · full'} with no code renders as 'disk: full', and {code: '', message: 'a · b'} renders as 'a: b', because join drops the empty code and the replace then rewrites the separator inside the message text. Filtering the two parts and joining them with ': ' keeps 'E_DISK: full' for the coded case, keeps 'disk · full' for the message-only case, and keeps the dash fallback, so the replace can be deleted without changing any other output.

Original problem and consequence

shared/rate-card.ts:74-80 is the single list-price formula: priceRow and listPrice use it, and every list total is built from it. metrics-run.ts:181-187 copies its reasoning rule, its four rate fields and its /1_000_000 divisor, and the only thing keeping the two in step is the comment at metrics-run.ts:173-174 ('as listEquivalentUsd counts it'). A change to one side (a new token kind, a different reasoning rule, a renamed rate field) leaves the per-kind shares summing to a different USD from the list total printed for the same row, and nothing fails. Today they agree only to float rounding: the probe gives byKindTotal 0.053750000000000006 against listEquivalentUsd 0.05375, and 0.035 against 0.035. Fix: export listEquivalentByKind(tokens, rate) from rate-card.ts, have listEquivalentUsd sum it, and have listByKind call it.

B14-01resolvedrecorded: fixedloadSettingsOnce caches its first request forever with ??= and has no catch, so one failed GET /api/v1/settings makes every later load() reject and the dashboard never refreshes again until a page reload.

Independent assessment

The shared memo drops a rejected request so the next poll can retry settings.

Verification strength
inspection + regression tests
Current mechanism evidence
dashboard/src/App.vue:149-154; dashboard/src/memo-loader.ts
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
The helper is tested. No interactive browser test of the running dashboard was performed in this assessment.

Original problem and consequence

The dashboard tab is opened while the awsf dash server is restarting, or the first settings GET fails once. settingsRequest keeps the rejected promise. load() awaits a Promise.all that includes loadSettingsOnce() (App.vue line 194), so every usePolling tick rejects, health and every route stop updating, and the poll backs off to 30 s even after the server recovers. The settings GET is never retried. Probe P1: the settings fetch ran once and three later load() calls all rejected with the first error.

Historical classification: bug · high · CONFIRMED. Original location: dashboard/src/App.vue:123 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B14-01. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: loadSettingsOnce memoized a rejected settings GET; memoizeUntilRejected drops the memo on rejection so the next poll retries

Original problem and consequence

The hash moves directly from #/sessions/A/phases/P to #/sessions/B/phases/Q (history back/forward or a typed URL). App.vue's load() replaces detail for a session read without clearing it (App.vue:215-218), so SessionRoute (App.vue:258, no key) is reused, and its PhaseDetailDrawer (SessionRoute.vue:60) and EventLog (PhaseDetailDrawer.vue:31) receive a new sessionId without remounting. EventLog has no watch or key on sessionId (EventLog.vue:8-15), so the next poll requests /sessions/B/events?after=<A's last cursor>. I did not confirm an in-app link between two session routes, so this needs history traversal or a typed hash.

B14-07unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe live/stale flag is a computed that reads Date.now(), which Vue does not track, so after one successful poll the indicator keeps showing 'live' through an outage and never switches to 'stale · reconnecting'.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

A poll succeeds and usePolling sets lastPollAt (usePolling.ts:25). The server then stops answering: every later poll throws, usePolling's catch only increments failedAttempts (usePolling.ts:27-28), and lastPollAt is never reassigned. The props AppShell passes (lastPollAt, pollMs) do not change, so Vue never re-runs the cached computed and the badge reads 'live' for the whole outage while the data on screen can be minutes old. A fresh evaluation of the same expression reads stale two poll intervals after the last success. The badge can only read 'stale' when the failure happens before the first successful poll (lastPollAt still null).

Historical classification: bug · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: dashboard/src/components/LiveIndicator.vue:4 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B14-07. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: LiveIndicator maintains a reactive timer clock with unmount cleanup to update staleness status reactively.

B14-13unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe backdrop's @click.self closes the dialog when a text selection that starts inside the ticket source or build prompt ends over the backdrop, because browsers fire click on the nearest common ancestor of the mousedown and mouseup targets.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

The owner drags across part of the ticket source (the pre at line 74) to select it for copying, and releases the button outside the dialog but still over the dimmed overlay. The click's target is the overlay div, the nearest common ancestor of the two press points, so the @click.self guard passes and emit('close') runs. The dialog closes and the selection is lost, so the owner must reopen the ticket to copy the text. The overlay is a fixed full-viewport layer (dashboard.css:1200), so most releases outside the dialog land on it.

Historical classification: bug · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: dashboard/src/components/TicketSourceOverlay.vue:52 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B14-13. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: TicketSourceOverlay tracks mousedown and mouseup on backdrop so dragging selection outside does not dismiss modal.

B14-15unverifiablerecorded: fixedA poll started by a focus event while a timer is pending creates a second poll chain, because schedule() overwrites the timer handle without clearing the pending timer.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Mount schedules timer T1 for 500 ms in live mode. The window regains focus at 100 ms, so onFocus calls voidPoll; no poll is in flight, so it polls, and its finally schedules T2 at 600 ms, overwriting timer. T1 is never cleared, so two chains poll indefinitely. A chain ends only when its own timer fires while the other chain's poll is in flight (voidPoll returns at line 21 without rescheduling), which is rare at the 5 s idle cadence, so the duplicate can persist for minutes. Measured: 5 polls and 1 pending timer in 0-2000 ms without focus, versus 9 polls and 2 pending timers after one focus at 100 ms. Unmount clears only the latest handle, but the orphan timer returns at the stopped check, so no polls leak after unmount (measured 0).

Historical classification: bug · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: dashboard/src/composables/usePolling.ts:18 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B14-15. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: usePolling onFocus clears any pending timer handle before invoking voidPoll to prevent duplicate polling chains.

Original problem and consequence

While a continuation pair is open, every poll (500 ms live, 2 s grid) replaces the sessions array (App.vue line 213 sets sessions.value = nextData, and loadAllSessions in dashboard/src/session-pages.ts builds fresh session and plan objects on each call), so chain, middle and relation get new identities and the watch at line 143 fires. Line 144 sets reason to null, which the template renders (lines 354-356) as 'no reason was recorded — this link was declared at awsf new --continues, which takes none' until the events fetch returns, so a recorded reason flickers to a false claim at every poll. A failed fetch (line 148 returns, and the empty catch at lines 151-152 is silent) also leaves reason null and is shown as 'no reason was recorded', although the comment at line 152 says an unreadable reason is shown as unavailable, never invented.

fixed: Canvas continuation reason watch keys by session ID and relation and uses sequence counter against stale overwrites.

Independent assessment

Original problem and consequence

A reader drags dots, which writes the arrangement through keepPins at line 84, then opens a run. The reset control is still on screen because the filter section sits outside the v-if chain, and clicking it does nothing: map.value is null, so the camera does not refit and the pins are not cleared. Returning to the map shows the dragged arrangement, which breaks the comment's promise that this control is the only way back to how the map first drew. Fix: let the parent perform the reset itself (keepPins with an empty map and go with camera null) rather than routing through the child's reset(), or disable the control while the map is unmounted.

B14-27unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe continuation reason is written after an await with no check that its run is still the one on the wheel, so a slower, earlier request can overwrite the reason shown for a later run.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

Turning the run wheel from run N to N+1 quickly starts two requests (the watch at line 143 is keyed on [middle, relation]). If run N's response arrives after N+1's, line 150 writes run N's reason while N+1 is on screen, and it stays until the next watch fire. The same unguarded pattern appears in the opened-session tree watch (lines 170-193): line 189 `tree.value = payload;` assigns group A's tree after the reader has opened group B, and the only check (line 185, `payload.group !== group`) compares against the group captured when A's request started, so it passes. SessionRoute.vue lines 13-31 show the sequence-counter guard these watches lack.

Historical classification: bug · medium · PLAUSIBLE. Original location: dashboard/src/routes/canvas.vue:150 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B14-27. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Canvas continuation reason assignment verifies active sequence counter before writing to prevent race conditions.

Original problem and consequence

The owner opens a class (open is set, line 23). A later poll drops that class's last failed phase while other failures remain, so failures.length stays non-zero. The class is no longer in present (line 20), so its button is removed from the bar (line 51). The panel under v-if="open" (line 66) keeps the class note with an empty codes row and an empty list. Nothing in the panel can clear open, and the only writer, toggle() (lines 28-31), is reached only from the class buttons, so the stale panel stays until another class is clicked. If every failure goes away, the section is hidden but open is kept, so the same empty panel reappears already open when failures return.

Back or Forward, or a typed hash, changes props.plan, but the watch at lines 21-29 returns at line 24 because hasSeededSelection is already true, so selectedPlans does not change. Probe probes/B14-sweep/probe-backlog-plan.mjs replicates the watch (lines 11-29) with the real initialPlanSelection and Vue 3.5.13: after the seed the selection is [plan-a, plan-b]; setting props.plan to plan-b leaves [plan-a, plan-b]; a fresh mount with plan-b selects [plan-b]. Probe probes/B14-sweep/probe-layout-edge.mjs gives the same six node ids with and without one extra edge (run:a to run:f): the keys are equal, all six positions differ, and the a-to-f distance changes from 330.4 to 188.1. Whether a real projection produces such an edge without a node change was not established: membership, plan and replay edges are built at canvas-graph.ts:202-215, so this is latent unless a link is recorded later onto runs already on the map.

B14-36unverifiablerecorded: fixedThe in-flight guard is set before the wrapped poll is awaited and cleared only in finally, so a poll that never settles keeps polling true forever and turns the scheduler, focus catch-up and refresh into permanent no-ops.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the reported failure above with the current implementation and a mechanism-matched negative case plus a healthy control. Check caller integration, recovery and changed boundary assumptions before classifying resolution.

Original problem and consequence

The wrapped poll is a fetch with no timeout or AbortSignal, and nothing in dashboard/src sets one. If the server accepts a request and never answers, voidPoll never reaches its finally, schedule() never runs, and the board stops refreshing until a reload. The wrapper's bounded retry never engages, because it runs only when the poll settles. This needs a request that never settles, so severity is low, but nothing bounds it.

Historical classification: bug · low · PLAUSIBLE. Original location: dashboard/src/composables/usePolling.ts:21 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B14-36. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

fixed: usePolling races each poll against a 30 s deadline; a poll that never settles counts as failed and releases the in-flight guard.

Original problem and consequence

SessionCard.vue:13-22 and SwimlaneChart.vue:13-22 are the same block copied: start, an end that uses a four-state live list with Date.now(), and a 1 s floor on span. That live list is written three times (SessionHeader.vue:9, SessionCard.vue:19, SwimlaneChart.vue:19). CanvasRunCard.vue:18 uses endedAt ?? updatedAt, so for a live run its runtime stops at the last journal write, while the session header and the board card count to now; any stretch without a journal write leaves the canvas card behind the board card for the same run. The simpler form is one sessionExtent(session, now) and one isLiveState(state) in display.ts, used by all four. Cost: one run shows different numbers on different screens, and a new lifecycle state has to be added in three places.

provenance reconciliation only

Original problem and consequence

The reader has phase A open (detail = A) and clicks phase B. selectedPhaseId becomes B and loadPhase(B) sets loadingPhase = true and clears phaseError (lines 25-26), but detail stays A, so the drawer renders A's evidence with B highlighted in the swimlane until B arrives. If B's request fails, lines 38-39 set phaseError and the drawer still renders A's evidence beneath the error bar, because the template tests only selectedPhaseId && detail. The EventLog inside is keyed to detail.phase.phaseId (A), so it lists A's events as well. Simpler general change: keep the phase identity with the loaded detail and render the drawer only when it matches the selection (accepting key or id, as App.vue's phaseName already does), or clear detail when the selection changes; either removes the state where the displayed evidence and the selection disagree.

B14-41unverifiablerecorded: fixedEvery camera update during a pan or wheel zoom writes the URL hash, and each hash write makes App.vue reload the whole sessions projection, so one drag costs one full load per pointer move with no coalescing or in-flight guard.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

A ground drag emits update:camera on every pointermove (CanvasMap.vue:172) and every wheel tick (CanvasMap.vue:216). go() (canvas.vue:88) assigns location.hash each time, so a 60-move pan adds 60 history entries, fires 60 hashchange events, and runs 60 App.vue load() calls (App.vue:159). Each load() requests /api/v1/sessions?limit=100 and /api/v1/health, and nothing caps the concurrency. The probe measured 120 HTTP requests with up to 6 in flight. Each sessions request runs card() per session (core/src/api/routes.ts:435), which issues several SQL queries per session, plus a synchronous catalog re-read (routes.ts:394). Cheaper alternative: keep the camera in component state during a gesture and write the hash once on pointerup (or at most once per animation frame), or use history.replaceState for in-gesture updates so no hashchange or history entry is produced. Also let onHashChange skip load() when only the camera or the selection changed.

Historical classification: cleanup · medium · CONFIRMED. Original location: dashboard/src/routes/canvas.vue:88 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B14-41. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: Canvas camera updates replace the current history entry and update local route state, avoiding hashchange-triggered full reloads.

B14-43unverifiablerecorded: not-reproduced stale decision-tree responses are already sequence-guarded in both route watchersThe decision-tree loader is written twice (groups.vue:17-37 and canvas.vue:170-193) with no request sequencing, so when two trees are requested in quick succession an older, slower response can overwrite the tree for the group now selected.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

Both mismatch guards compare payload.group with the group captured when that request started (groups.vue:28, canvas.vue:185), not with the current selection, so a stale response passes them. Open a large journal, then switch to another group; if the first response arrives second, tree.value becomes the first group's tree while the heading and selection show the second, and loading clears while the second request is still pending. B14-46unverifiablerecorded: fixedEventLog runs a private one-second setInterval for as long as it is mounted, outside usePolling's cadence and backoff, and it has no watch on its session or phase, so the next request reuses the old cursor if the component is reused for another session.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

A reader leaves a phase drawer open while the board is in grid mode (2 s) or idle (5 s): EventLog still calls load() every second (line 50). If the server fails, each second's load() sets error and the next tick retries with no backoff, although usePolling doubles the interval and caps it at 30 s. Separately, App.vue:258 renders SessionRoute without a key, so a hand-edited hash that moves from one session's phase to another reuses the drawer and EventLog: the next page is requested after the old session's cursor, so the new session's earlier events are never loaded, and the old events are never cleared. Simpler general change: EventLog advances its cursor from the poll cycle the app already runs (or from a usePolling instance with the shared cadence), and App.vue keys the session route by session id so per-session state is recreated rather than patched.

Historical classification: cleanup · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: dashboard/src/components/EventLog.vue:50 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B14-46. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: EventLog uses shared polling cadence and backoff, refreshes on session/phase changes, and stops repeating for terminal phases.

B14-47unverifiablerecorded: dup-of B14-46The phase event log polls its events endpoint every second for as long as the drawer stays open, including for a finished run that can produce no new events. Each tick also toggles a template-visible loading flag, which re-renders every event row.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

Opening a phase drawer on a completed run starts setInterval(load, 1000) (line 50), which is cleared only on unmount. The browser therefore issues GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>/events?after=<cursor>&limit=200 once a second indefinitely, and each request returns an empty page. Each tick sets loading to true (line 32) and back to false after the response. loading is read in the template (line 58), so the whole event list re-renders about twice per second, and each row calls rowSummary (line 63) and a toLocaleTimeString formatter. Line 40 also rebuilds a Set of every event id on every tick, even when the page is empty. Cheaper alternative: stop the timer when the run is terminal, or refetch on a change of the parent's stateRevision instead of on a clock (SessionRoute.vue:44 already watches stateRevision). Keep loading out of the rendered state, or flip it only when a request returns rows. Dedupe with the monotonic cursor, or with a persistent Set updated on push instead of rebuilt per tick.

B14-52unverifiablerecorded: fixedLow severity: every SessionStack registers its own document click listener, and that listener calls event.composedPath() before checking whether any promotion is active. Each click anywhere on the board therefore runs one allocating check per stack.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

The listener is added on mount for every stack (line 95), so a board with N stacks holds N document click handlers. On each click, restoreDefault (lines 88-93) calls event.composedPath().includes(stack) for each stack whose element is set. Each call allocates an array, and the work is repeated for every click, even though the refs it then clears are usually already null. The cost is small per click but scales with the number of stacks. Cheaper alternative: return early when promotedIds and promotedFront are both null, which skips composedPath entirely. Or attach the listener only while a promotion is active and detach it when the promotion clears.

fixed: SessionStack returns before composedPath when no promotion is active.

Original problem and consequence

The reader is on #/backlog or #/groups: App.vue passes backlogRoute or groupsRoute through AppShell into TopNav, the Settings anchor is not rendered, and the only remaining route to it is editing the hash. Lines 173-176 hide each other link only on its own route (for example v-if="!backlog" on line 176), so the Settings rule is a special case layered on per-route booleans. Simpler general change: one current-route id from App.vue and a static link list where each entry hides when it is the current route; the three-boolean rule for Settings then disappears.

B14-56unverifiablerecorded: fixedBoth tree views are mounted at once with v-show, so the reading view (the full per-decision DOM) is built on every group load even though the default view is the graph and only one view is visible.

Independent assessment

The ledger disposition is recorded, but this assessment did not independently establish whether the current implementation addresses this exact original mechanism. Do not promote the recorded label to verified resolution.

Verification strength
provenance reconciliation only
Current mechanism evidence
The path/history and named-test links below were checked mechanically. No current semantic conclusion follows from them.
Remaining proof, boundary or maintenance cost
Compare the proposed simplification with the current structure and accepted contract. Establish whether the duplication or complexity remains and whether changing it would reduce a concrete maintenance cost without weakening a boundary.

Original problem and consequence

groups.vue:13 starts on the graph view, but once a tree loads, GroupTreeGraph (line 87) and GroupDecisionTree (line 88) are both created and laid out. v-show only toggles display. For a large journal (the code comments cite a 72-stage group), the hidden reading view costs one card per decision, with about six narrativeFields() calls per decision in its template (GroupDecisionTree.vue:58-66), plus the DOM for every ask and unit. That cost is paid for every group a reader opens, and the view stays mounted. canvas.vue already avoids this with v-if and v-else (canvas.vue:415-416). Cheaper alternative: render the reading view with v-if and v-else. GroupDecisionTree holds no local state, so switching loses nothing. If the graph's opened-node state must survive a switch, keep v-show for the graph only and lazy-mount the reading view on first activation.

Historical classification: cleanup · low · CONFIRMED. Original location: dashboard/src/routes/groups.vue:87 at 335a184. Source: ALL.json, record B14-56. This paragraph preserves the review’s account, not a new incident claim.

Recorded response and provenance

fixed: GroupDecisionTree mounts only in reading mode while GroupTreeGraph stays mounted to preserve graph state.

ELI B14 · Keeping dashboard screens usable

This batch covers the dashboard’s screens, components and refreshing behavior. One repair was checked in depth: a failed settings request no longer prevents later attempts from trying again. The other findings were not independently rechecked here. This supports a narrow claim about retrying settings, rather than a claim that the whole dashboard is reliable or that a user can recover from every failure.

Carried scoped judgments: 1 of 57 findings. The other 56 remain unverified. Report rendering is not a running-dashboard test.
